questions.question_en: How many medals did India win at the 2026 Asian Games (Aichi-Nagoya), finishing fourth in the table?
questions.explanation_en: India won 85 medals (21 gold, 27 silver, 37 bronze); its record 107 medals came at Hangzhou 2022.

questions.question_en: Vijay, who took oath as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister in May 2026, heads which party?
questions.explanation_en: Actor-politician Vijay's TVK won 107 seats and displaced the DMK; he was sworn in on 10 May 2026 with outside support from allies.

questions.question_en: Delhi conducted its first cloud-seeding trial in October 2025 in collaboration with which institution?
questions.explanation_en: The artificial-rain trials aimed at easing post-Diwali smog were conducted with IIT Kanpur using silver iodide and sodium chloride.

questions.question_en: How many days of guaranteed wage employment per rural household per year does the VB-G RAM G Act provide?
questions.explanation_en: The new Act raises the guarantee from 100 days under MGNREGA to 125 days per financial year.

questions.question_en: Under the Mahila Samriddhi Yojana approved by the Delhi Cabinet, eligible women are to receive a monthly assistance of:
questions.explanation_en: The BJP's manifesto promise of Rs 2,500 a month was cleared by the Delhi cabinet on 8 March 2025 for women aged 18-60 with limited family income.

questions.question_en: Who won the Orange Cap in IPL 2026 with 776 runs?
questions.explanation_en: Teenage opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi finished as the leading run-scorer of IPL 2026 with 776 runs; Kagiso Rabada took the Purple Cap (29 wickets).

questions.question_en: The Poona Pact (1932) was signed between Gandhiji and Dr B. R. Ambedkar after the announcement of the:
questions.explanation_en: Gandhi's fast against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes ended with the Poona Pact, which gave them reserved seats in joint electorates.

questions.question_en: India's first national park, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, is now called:
questions.explanation_en: Located in Uttarakhand, it was renamed Jim Corbett National Park in 1957; Project Tiger was launched here in 1973.

questions.question_en: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.explanation_en: Sukumar Sen (1950-58) conducted the first general elections of 1951-52.

questions.question_en: The highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India is:
questions.explanation_en: Anamudi (2,695 m) is in the Anamalai hills of Kerala; Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest in the Nilgiris.

questions.question_en: Which of the following was a member of the Cabinet Mission that came to India in 1946?
questions.explanation_en: The Mission comprised Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander; Wavell was the Viceroy and Attlee the Prime Minister.

questions.question_en: The first section of the Delhi Metro (Shahdara-Tis Hazari) started operations in:
questions.explanation_en: The Red Line section opened on 24 December 2002; DMRC was incorporated in 1995 with E. Sreedharan as managing director.

questions.question_en: The first princely state annexed by the British under Lord Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse was:
questions.explanation_en: Satara was annexed in 1848; Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854) followed.

questions.question_en: Which committee was appointed to inquire into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919?
questions.explanation_en: The Hunter Committee (1919-20) investigated the Punjab disturbances and General Dyer's firing at Amritsar.

questions.question_en: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, the first garden tomb on the Indian subcontinent, was commissioned by:
questions.explanation_en: Humayun's widow Hamida Banu Begum had it built from 1565; it inspired the Taj Mahal's design.

questions.question_en: According to the 10 per cent law, the energy that passes from one trophic level to the next is about:
questions.explanation_en: Only about 10 per cent of energy is stored at the next level; the rest is lost as heat in respiration.

questions.question_en: The general formula of the homologous series of alkynes is:
questions.explanation_en: Alkanes are CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n and alkynes CnH2n-2 (for example, ethyne C2H2).

questions.question_en: Gandhiji began the Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) on 12 March 1930 from:
questions.explanation_en: He walked about 385 km with 78 followers and broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.

questions.question_en: Who was the first woman to be awarded the Bharat Ratna?
questions.explanation_en: Indira Gandhi received it in 1971; Mother Teresa (1980), M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998) and Lata Mangeshkar (2001) came later.

questions.question_en: The Tropic of Cancer passes through all of the following states EXCEPT:
questions.explanation_en: It crosses eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.question_en:
Statement: The government has increased the tax on cigarettes by 50%.
Conclusions: I. The price of cigarettes is likely to rise. II. Every smoker will quit smoking.
questions.explanation_en: A higher tax raises the cost to sellers, so a price rise is a reasonable conclusion. 'Every smoker will quit' is an extreme claim that cannot be drawn.

questions.question_en: P is the father of Q. Q is the sister of R. R is the mother of S. How is P related to S?
questions.explanation_en: P is father of both Q and R. R is S's mother, so P is the father of S's mother: maternal grandfather.

questions.question_en: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at 4:20?
Judge : Court :: Chef : ?
questions.explanation_en: A judge works in a court; a chef works in a kitchen (person : place of work).

questions.question_en:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are birds.
Conclusions: I. All cats are birds. II. Some birds are dogs.
questions.explanation_en: Cats lie inside dogs, and dogs lie inside birds, so all cats are birds (I). Since all dogs are birds, at least some birds are dogs (II). Both follow.

questions.question_en: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi says, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl related to Ravi?
questions.explanation_en: Ravi's grandfather's only son is Ravi's father. The daughter of Ravi's father is Ravi's sister.

questions.question_en: If + and − are interchanged, and × and ÷ are interchanged, then 24 ÷ 6 + 8 × 2 − 3 = ?
questions.explanation_en: After interchanging the signs the expression is 24 × 6 − 8 ÷ 2 + 3. BODMAS: 144 − 4 + 3 = 143.

questions.question_en: Select the odd letter group: BDF, HJL, NPR, TVW
questions.explanation_en: BDF, HJL and NPR skip one letter each time (+2, +2). In TVW the gaps are +2, +1, so it is the odd one.

questions.question_en: If P means +, Q means −, R means × and S means ÷, then 20 R 3 P 8 S 4 Q 5 = ?
questions.explanation_en: Replace the letters: 20 × 3 + 8 ÷ 4 − 5. By BODMAS: 60 + 2 − 5 = 57.

questions.question_en: In a class of 60 students, 30 study Physics, 25 Chemistry and 20 Mathematics. 10 study Physics and Chemistry, 8 Chemistry and Mathematics, 6 Physics and Mathematics, and 4 study all three. How many students study at least one of the three subjects?
questions.explanation_en: By inclusion-exclusion: 30 + 25 + 20 - 10 - 8 - 6 + 4 = 55.

questions.question_en:
Statement: Should school uniforms be abolished?
Arguments: I. Yes, because uniforms are old-fashioned. II. No, because a particular tailor will lose business.

options.en: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong

questions.explanation_en: 'Old-fashioned' is a matter of opinion and not a sound reason. The business of one tailor is a narrow, personal concern. Neither argument is strong.

questions.question_en:
Statement: Should students be given homework daily?
Arguments: I. Yes, it helps them revise and practise concepts. II. No, because teachers do not like checking it.

options.en: Both I and II are strong
Neither I nor II is strong

questions.explanation_en: Learning value is a valid educational reason (strong). The convenience of teachers is not a good reason against a practice that helps students, so II is weak.

questions.question_en:
Statements: No flower is a stone. All stones are rocks.
Conclusions: I. No flower is a rock. II. Some rocks are not flowers.
questions.explanation_en: Stones are rocks and no stone is a flower, so those rocks (the stones) are not flowers: II follows. A flower may still be a rock that is not a stone, so I does not follow.

questions.question_en: Which letter is the 8th to the right of the letter that is 5th to the left of M in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation_en: M is the 13th letter. 5th to its left is the 8th letter, H. 8th to the right of H is the 16th letter, P.

questions.question_en: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock will the two hands of a clock coincide?
questions.explanation_en: Hands coincide when M = (60 × H) / 11 minutes past H. For H = 4: 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes past 4.

questions.question_en: A cube is cut with 7 plane cuts, each cut parallel to one of the faces. What is the maximum number of pieces that can be obtained?
questions.explanation_en: Distribute the cuts as evenly as possible: 2, 2 and 3. Pieces = (2 + 1)(2 + 1)(3 + 1) = 3 × 3 × 4 = 36.

questions.question_en: A series of figures shows a triangle, a square, a pentagon, a hexagon, and so on, each figure having one more side than the previous one. What is the total number of sides in the first six figures?
questions.explanation_en: Sides are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Sum = 33.

questions.question_en: A painted cube is cut into identical smaller cubes. Exactly 96 of the small cubes have only one face painted. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
questions.explanation_en: 6(n − 2)² = 96 gives (n − 2)² = 16, so n − 2 = 4 and n = 6. Two-face cubes = 12 × (n − 2) = 12 × 4 = 48.

questions.question_en: On a standard die (opposite faces add up to 7), which number can never appear on a face adjacent to the face showing 4?
questions.explanation_en: The face opposite 4 is 7 − 4 = 3. A face is adjacent to every face except itself and its opposite, so 3 can never be adjacent to 4.

questions.question_en: A cube has two opposite faces painted red, two opposite faces painted green and the remaining two faces painted blue. It is cut into 125 identical small cubes. How many small cubes have only red and green paint (one face of each, no blue)?
questions.explanation_en: Each red face meets each green face along one edge: 2 × 2 = 4 red–green edges. Excluding the corner cubes (which also have blue), each edge has n − 2 = 3 cubes, so 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.question_en: An article costing ₹500 is sold for ₹575. What is the profit percentage?
A can do a work in 15 days. He works for 5 days and then B finishes the remaining work in 10 days. In how many days can B alone do the whole work?
questions.explanation_en: A's 5 days = 5/15 = 1/3 of the work. Remaining 2/3 is done by B in 10 days, so the whole work takes B 10 × 3/2 = 15 days.

questions.question_en: What is the average of the first 10 even natural numbers?
questions.explanation_en: The numbers 2, 4, ..., 20 sum to 110. Average = 110/10 = 11.

questions.question_en: Find the value of 48.5% of 1200 + 12.5% of 640.
What is the third proportional to 4 and 12?
How many numbers between 100 and 200 are divisible by 7?
questions.explanation_en: The first multiple is 105 = 7 × 15 and the last is 196 = 7 × 28. Count = 28 − 15 + 1 = 14.

questions.question_en: A cyclist covers 24 km at 12 km/h and then 36 km at 18 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation_en: Time for the first part = 24/12 = 2 h; second part = 36/18 = 2 h. Total distance = 60 km and total time = 4 h, so average speed = 15 km/h.

questions.question_en: 12 men can complete a work in 18 days. In how many days can 9 men complete the same work?
questions.explanation_en: Men × days is constant: 12 × 18 = 216. Days for 9 men = 216/9 = 24.

questions.question_en: What is the compound interest on ₹12,000 for 1.5 years at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
questions.explanation_en: Rate per half-year = 5%, number of half-years = 3. Amount = 12000 × 1.05³ = 12000 × 1.157625 = 13,891.50. CI = ₹1,891.50. (₹1,800 is the simple interest.)

questions.question_en: At what rate of simple interest per annum will a sum of money double itself in 8 years?
questions.explanation_en: Interest = P in 8 years, so P = P × R × 8 / 100, giving R = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.question_en: In what ratio must rice at ₹40 per kg be mixed with rice at ₹55 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹46 per kg?
questions.explanation_en: By alligation, the ratio of cheaper : dearer = (55 − 46) : (46 − 40) = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2.

questions.question_en: The average of 11 results is 50. The average of the first six is 49 and of the last six is 52. What is the sixth result?
questions.explanation_en: Sum of first six + sum of last six = 6 × 49 + 6 × 52 = 294 + 312 = 606. This counts the sixth result twice. Total of all 11 = 550, so sixth result = 606 − 550 = 56.

questions.question_en: A man sells an article at a loss of 10%. Had he sold it for ₹150 more, he would have gained 5%. What is the cost price?
questions.explanation_en: The difference between 105% and 90% of CP is 15% of CP = ₹150. So CP = 150/0.15 = ₹1,000.

questions.question_en: A boat takes 4 hours to travel 48 km downstream and 8 hours to travel the same distance upstream. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.explanation_en: Downstream = 48/4 = 12 km/h, upstream = 48/8 = 6 km/h. Still water = (12 + 6)/2 = 9 km/h.

questions.question_en: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and pipe B in 18 hours. If both are opened together, how long will they take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation_en: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per hour. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 hours.

questions.question_en:
The table shows the number of students who appeared and passed in a Computer Science examination from five schools.
School | Appeared | Passed
P | 240 | 180
Q | 300 | 255
R | 180 | 117
S | 360 | 288
T | 220 | 198
What is the ratio of the number of students who failed in school P to those who failed in school Q?
The volume of a right circular cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is (take π = 22/7):
questions.explanation_en: V = πr²h = 22/7 × 49 × 10 = 154 × 10 = 1540 cm³. 440 cm² is the curved surface area 2πrh, a common mix-up.

questions.question_en: An arc of a circle subtends an angle of 120° at the centre. The angle it subtends at any point on the remaining part (major arc) of the circle is:
questions.explanation_en: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle it subtends at any point on the remaining part of the circle: 120° / 2 = 60°.

questions.question_en: Find the mean of the following frequency distribution. Values (x): 10, 20, 30, 40. Frequencies (f): 3, 5, 8, 4.
questions.explanation_en: Σfx = 10×3 + 20×5 + 30×8 + 40×4 = 30 + 100 + 240 + 160 = 530. Σf = 20. Mean = 530 / 20 = 26.5. The simple average of the values (25) ignores the frequencies.

questions.question_en: In triangle ABC, a line DE is drawn parallel to BC, with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 3 cm, DB = 2 cm and AE = 4.5 cm, then EC is:
questions.explanation_en: By the Basic Proportionality (Thales) theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC → 3/2 = 4.5/EC → EC = 3 cm.

questions.question_en: 'घी के दीये जलाना' मुहावरे का अर्थ क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'घी के दीये जलाना' मुहावरे का अर्थ क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: It means to celebrate joyfully.
questions.explanation_hi: 'घी के दीये जलाना' का अर्थ है अत्यधिक प्रसन्न होकर उत्सव मनाना — 'बेटे के लौटने पर घर में घी के दीये जलाए गए।'

questions.question_en: 'सापेक्ष' का विलोम शब्द चुनिए।
questions.question_hi: 'सापेक्ष' का विलोम शब्द चुनिए।
questions.explanation_en: Sapeksh (relative) vs nirpeksh (absolute).
questions.explanation_hi: सापेक्ष (किसी पर निर्भर) का विलोम निरपेक्ष (निर्भर न रहने वाला) है। परोक्ष का विलोम प्रत्यक्ष है।

questions.question_en: 'पानी गए न ऊबरै, मोती मानुष चून' — इस पंक्ति में 'पानी' शब्द के प्रयोग के कारण कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.question_hi: 'पानी गए न ऊबरै, मोती मानुष चून' — इस पंक्ति में 'पानी' शब्द के प्रयोग के कारण कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation_en: One word 'paani' carries three meanings at once (lustre, honour, water), so it is Shlesh (pun).
questions.explanation_hi: यहाँ 'पानी' शब्द एक बार प्रयुक्त होकर तीन अर्थ दे रहा है — मोती के लिए चमक, मनुष्य के लिए सम्मान और चूने के लिए जल। एक शब्द में अनेक अर्थ चिपके हों तो श्लेष अलंकार होता है।

questions.question_en: 'पवन' शब्द में कौन-सी संधि है?
questions.question_hi: 'पवन' शब्द में कौन-सी संधि है?
questions.explanation_en: Po + an = pavan; o becomes av before a vowel — ayadi sandhi.
questions.explanation_hi: पो + अन = पवन। 'ओ' के बाद भिन्न स्वर आने पर 'ओ' का 'अव्' हो जाता है; यह अयादि संधि है। इसी प्रकार भो + अन = भवन।

questions.question_en: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य चुनिए: (दही)
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य चुनिए: (दही)
questions.explanation_en: Dahi is masculine, so both modifiers must be masculine.
questions.explanation_hi: मानक हिंदी में 'दही' पुल्लिंग है, इसलिए सर्वनाम और विशेषण दोनों पुल्लिंग होंगे — 'मेरा दही खट्टा है।'

questions.question_en: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य चुनिए: (सज्जन)
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य चुनिए: (सज्जन)

options.en: वह एक सज्जन व्यक्ति पुरुष है।
options.hi: वह एक सज्जन व्यक्ति पुरुष है।

questions.explanation_en: Sajjan already means a good man, so 'purush' is redundant.
questions.explanation_hi: 'सज्जन' का अर्थ ही 'भला पुरुष' है, इसलिए 'सज्जन पुरुष' में पुनरुक्ति है। 'वे' के साथ 'है' लगाना वचन-दोष है।

questions.question_en: 'बेईमान' शब्द में प्रयुक्त उपसर्ग किस भाषा का है?
questions.question_hi: 'बेईमान' शब्द में प्रयुक्त उपसर्ग किस भाषा का है?
questions.explanation_en: 'Be' (without) is a Persian/Urdu prefix.
questions.explanation_hi: 'बे' उपसर्ग फ़ारसी/उर्दू का है जिसका अर्थ 'बिना' होता है, जैसे बेकार, बेखबर, बेवक्त। संस्कृत में इसके समकक्ष 'निर्' या 'अ' उपसर्ग हैं।

questions.subtopic: अनेक शब्दों के लिए एक शब्द
questions.question_en: 'जिसके आने की कोई तिथि न हो' — इसके लिए एक शब्द है:
questions.question_hi: 'जिसके आने की कोई तिथि न हो' — इसके लिए एक शब्द है:
questions.explanation_en: One whose date of arrival is not fixed = atithi.
questions.explanation_hi: अ + तिथि = अतिथि, अर्थात् जिसके आने की तिथि निश्चित न हो। आगंतुक और अभ्यागत का अर्थ 'आया हुआ' है।

questions.question_en:
निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

पुस्तकें मनुष्य की सबसे अच्छी मित्र होती हैं। वे बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं और कठिन समय में धैर्य बँधाती हैं। जो व्यक्ति नियमित रूप से अच्छी पुस्तकें पढ़ता है, उसके विचारों में गहराई आती है तथा उसकी भाषा समृद्ध होती है। आज के डिजिटल युग में भी पुस्तकों का महत्त्व कम नहीं हुआ है, केवल उनका रूप बदल गया है। अब ई-पुस्तकें और ऑडियो-पुस्तकें भी पाठकों तक पहुँच रही हैं। आवश्यकता इस बात की है कि विद्यार्थी केवल परीक्षा के लिए नहीं, बल्कि आनंद और जिज्ञासा के लिए भी पढ़ें।

प्रश्न: गद्यांश में प्रयुक्त 'समृद्ध' शब्द का विलोम क्या है?
questions.question_hi:
निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

पुस्तकें मनुष्य की सबसे अच्छी मित्र होती हैं। वे बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं और कठिन समय में धैर्य बँधाती हैं। जो व्यक्ति नियमित रूप से अच्छी पुस्तकें पढ़ता है, उसके विचारों में गहराई आती है तथा उसकी भाषा समृद्ध होती है। आज के डिजिटल युग में भी पुस्तकों का महत्त्व कम नहीं हुआ है, केवल उनका रूप बदल गया है। अब ई-पुस्तकें और ऑडियो-पुस्तकें भी पाठकों तक पहुँच रही हैं। आवश्यकता इस बात की है कि विद्यार्थी केवल परीक्षा के लिए नहीं, बल्कि आनंद और जिज्ञासा के लिए भी पढ़ें।

प्रश्न: गद्यांश में प्रयुक्त 'समृद्ध' शब्द का विलोम क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: The antonym of samriddh (prosperous) is vipann (destitute).
questions.explanation_hi: 'समृद्ध' का अर्थ है संपन्न या भरा-पूरा; इसका विलोम 'विपन्न' (अभावग्रस्त) है। संपन्न और वैभवशाली इसके पर्यायवाची हैं।

questions.question_en: 'उल्लेख' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'उल्लेख' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: Ut + lekh: t before l becomes l — vyanjan sandhi.
questions.explanation_hi: उत् + लेख = उल्लेख। 'त्' के बाद 'ल' आने पर 'त्' का 'ल्' हो जाता है; यह व्यंजन संधि है। इसी नियम से उत् + लास = उल्लास।

questions.question_en: 'होंठ' शब्द का तत्सम रूप क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'होंठ' शब्द का तत्सम रूप क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: The tatsam form of honth is oshth.
questions.explanation_hi: 'होंठ/ओठ' संस्कृत 'ओष्ठ' से बने हैं। 'ओष्ट' में 'ठ' के स्थान पर 'ट' लिखना सामान्य वर्तनी-भूल है।

questions.question_en: 'अभ्यागत' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग है?
questions.question_hi: 'अभ्यागत' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग है?
questions.explanation_en: Abhyagat = abhi + aagat; the prefix is 'abhi'.
questions.explanation_hi: अभ्यागत = अभि + आगत (आ + गत)। 'अभि' उपसर्ग के 'इ' का यण संधि से 'य्' हो गया है। अतः उपसर्ग 'अभि' है।

questions.question_en: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'आँख' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'आँख' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?
questions.explanation_en: Kapol means cheek; the others mean eye.
questions.explanation_hi: नेत्र, लोचन, दृग, नयन और चक्षु 'आँख' के पर्यायवाची हैं। 'कपोल' का अर्थ गाल है।

questions.question_en: 'एकैक' शब्द में कौन-सी संधि है?
questions.question_hi: 'एकैक' शब्द में कौन-सी संधि है?
questions.explanation_en: Ek + ek: a + e = ai — vriddhi sandhi.
questions.explanation_hi: एक + एक = एकैक। अ + ए = ऐ होता है, जो वृद्धि संधि का नियम है (जैसे सदा + एव = सदैव)।

questions.question_en:
निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

एक अच्छा शिक्षक केवल पाठ्यपुस्तक का ज्ञान नहीं देता, बल्कि विद्यार्थियों में सोचने की क्षमता जगाता है। वह प्रश्न पूछने को प्रोत्साहित करता है और गलती को सीखने का अवसर मानता है। कक्षा में भय का वातावरण होने पर विद्यार्थी अपनी शंकाएँ व्यक्त नहीं कर पाते, इसलिए शिक्षक को मित्रवत् व्यवहार करना चाहिए। राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति 2020 भी रटने के स्थान पर समझ पर आधारित शिक्षा पर बल देती है। वास्तव में शिक्षक वह दीपक है जो स्वयं जलकर दूसरों का मार्ग आलोकित करता है।

प्रश्न: गद्यांश में प्रयुक्त 'आलोकित' शब्द का अर्थ क्या है?
questions.question_hi:
निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

एक अच्छा शिक्षक केवल पाठ्यपुस्तक का ज्ञान नहीं देता, बल्कि विद्यार्थियों में सोचने की क्षमता जगाता है। वह प्रश्न पूछने को प्रोत्साहित करता है और गलती को सीखने का अवसर मानता है। कक्षा में भय का वातावरण होने पर विद्यार्थी अपनी शंकाएँ व्यक्त नहीं कर पाते, इसलिए शिक्षक को मित्रवत् व्यवहार करना चाहिए। राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति 2020 भी रटने के स्थान पर समझ पर आधारित शिक्षा पर बल देती है। वास्तव में शिक्षक वह दीपक है जो स्वयं जलकर दूसरों का मार्ग आलोकित करता है।

प्रश्न: गद्यांश में प्रयुक्त 'आलोकित' शब्द का अर्थ क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: Aalokit means illuminated (from aalok, light).
questions.explanation_hi: 'आलोक' का अर्थ है प्रकाश, इसलिए 'आलोकित' का अर्थ है प्रकाशित या रोशन। 'आलोचित' (जिसकी आलोचना हुई हो) और 'अवलोकित' (देखा गया) मिलती-जुलती ध्वनि वाले भ्रामक विकल्प हैं।

questions.question_en: 'नयन' शब्द में कौन-सी स्वर संधि है?
questions.question_hi: 'नयन' शब्द में कौन-सी स्वर संधि है?
questions.explanation_en: Ne + an = nayan; e changes to ay before a vowel — ayadi sandhi.
questions.explanation_hi: ने + अन = नयन। 'ए' के बाद कोई भिन्न स्वर आने पर 'ए' का 'अय्' हो जाता है; यह अयादि संधि है। गुण संधि में अ/आ के साथ इ, उ, ऋ मिलते हैं।

questions.question_en: 'महर्षि' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'महर्षि' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: Maha + rishi = maharshi; aa + ri = ar (gun sandhi).
questions.explanation_hi: महा + ऋषि = महर्षि। आ + ऋ = अर् होता है, यह गुण संधि का उदाहरण है (जैसे राजा + ऋषि = राजर्षि)।

questions.question_en: 'प्रतिकूल' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग है?
questions.question_hi: 'प्रतिकूल' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग है?
questions.explanation_en: Pratikool = prati + kool; 'prati' is the prefix.
questions.explanation_hi: प्रतिकूल = प्रति + कूल। 'प्रति' संस्कृत उपसर्ग है जिसका अर्थ 'विरुद्ध/उलटा' होता है, जैसे प्रतिध्वनि, प्रतिदिन।

questions.question_en: 'सोहत ओढ़े पीत पट, स्याम सलोने गात। मनहुँ नीलमनि सैल पर, आतप परयौ प्रभात॥' — इसमें कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.question_hi: 'सोहत ओढ़े पीत पट, स्याम सलोने गात। मनहुँ नीलमनि सैल पर, आतप परयौ प्रभात॥' — इसमें कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation_en: The word 'manahun' (as if) expresses imagined likeness, so it is Utpreksha.
questions.explanation_hi: पीले वस्त्र ओढ़े श्याम शरीर में नीलमणि पर्वत पर सुबह की धूप पड़ने की संभावना व्यक्त की गई है। 'मनहुँ' संभावना-सूचक वाचक शब्द है, अतः उत्प्रेक्षा अलंकार है।

questions.question_en: 'आस्तीन का साँप' मुहावरे का अर्थ क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'आस्तीन का साँप' मुहावरे का अर्थ क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: It means a friend who betrays, a snake in the sleeve.
questions.explanation_hi: आस्तीन (बाँह) में छिपा साँप पास रहकर ही डसता है; अतः यह मुहावरा कपटी मित्र या अपने बीच के धोखेबाज़ के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है।

questions.question_en: Change the voice: ‘The police arrested the thief.’

options.en: The police was arrested by the thief.
The thief had been arrested by the police.
The thief is arrested by the police.
The thief was arrested by the police.

questions.explanation_en: Simple past active becomes was/were + V3 in the passive; the object becomes the subject.

questions.question_en: This time next week, we ______ on the beach in Goa.
questions.explanation_en: “This time next week” refers to an action in progress at a specific future moment, so the future continuous (will be lying) is used.

questions.question_en: Select the word closest in meaning to TENACIOUS.
questions.explanation_en: Tenacious means holding firmly to a purpose; persistent is nearest.

questions.question_en:
Select the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. If no change is needed, select ‘No improvement’.
Each of the girls [have] brought her own lunch.
questions.explanation_en: “Each” is singular and needs “has”.

questions.question_en: Change the voice: ‘Someone has stolen my bicycle.’

options.en: My bicycle was stolen by someone.

questions.explanation_en: Present perfect passive = has/have been + V3; the vague agent ‘someone’ is normally omitted.

questions.question_en:
Identify the segment that contains an error.
Though he was tired, / but he / continued working / on the project.
questions.explanation_en: “Though” and “but” should not be used together in one sentence. Remove “but”.

questions.question_en: The Principal as well as the teachers ______ invited to the function.
questions.explanation_en: With “as well as”, “along with”, “together with”, the verb agrees with the first subject (Principal – singular).

questions.question_en:
Identify the segment that contains an error. If there is no error, select option 4.
He is taller / than any other boy / in his class.
questions.explanation_en: The comparative with “any other + singular noun” is correct, so the sentence has no error.

questions.question_en: Select the word opposite in meaning to TACITURN.
questions.explanation_en: Taciturn means habitually silent; talkative is its antonym.

questions.question_en: ______ Ganga is the holiest river of India.
questions.explanation_en: Names of rivers take the definite article “the”.

questions.question_en:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Water is (1) ______ for all living beings. However, in recent years many cities have been (2) ______ from acute water shortage. The main reason is the (3) ______ use of groundwater by industries and households. If we do not take steps to (4) ______ water, future generations will have to pay a heavy price. Every citizen should therefore (5) ______ responsibility and avoid wastage.

Select the most appropriate option to fill blank (3).
Relevant sentence: The main reason is the (3) ______ use of groundwater by industries and households.
questions.explanation_en: A ‘reason’ for shortage must be over-use, hence “excessive”.

questions.question_en: Select the one word that can replace: ‘One who devotes his life to the welfare of others’.
questions.explanation_en: An altruist is selflessly concerned for the well-being of others; an egoist is self-centred.

questions.question_en: I ______ this film three times.
questions.explanation_en: Repeated experience up to the present with no fixed past time takes the present perfect (have seen).

questions.question_en: Aman is senior ______ me by two years.
questions.explanation_en: Words such as senior, junior, superior, inferior, prefer take “to”, not “than”.

questions.question_en:
Select the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. If no change is needed, select ‘No improvement’.
He [is knowing] the answer to every question.
questions.explanation_en: “Know” is a stative verb and is not used in continuous forms; use the simple present.

questions.question_en: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation_en: The noun of “maintain” is spelt maintenance (-tenance, not -tainance).

questions.question_en: She has ______ MBA degree from a reputed institute.
questions.explanation_en: “MBA” is pronounced “em-bee-ay”, beginning with a vowel sound, so “an” is used.

questions.question_en:
Identify the segment that contains an error.
I prefer / walking than / driving to / the office.
questions.explanation_en: “Prefer” takes “to”: I prefer walking to driving.

questions.question_en: Select the word opposite in meaning to GENEROUS.
questions.explanation_en: Generous means giving freely; its antonym is stingy (unwilling to give).

questions.question_en: Select the word closest in meaning to CAPRICIOUS.
questions.explanation_en: Capricious means given to sudden changes of mood or behaviour, i.e. fickle.

questions.question_en: A system has a cache access time of 10 ns and a cache hit ratio of 90%. On a miss, the total access time (cache check plus main memory) is 110 ns. What is the average memory access time?
questions.explanation_en: Average time = hit ratio × hit time + miss ratio × miss time = 0.9 × 10 + 0.1 × 110 = 9 + 11 = 20 ns. Option 1 (19 ns) results from using 100 ns for the miss instead of the full 110 ns.

questions.question_en: The octal number (734)8 is equal to which hexadecimal number?
questions.explanation_en: Convert via binary: 7 3 4 → 111 011 100 = 111011100. Regroup in fours from the right: 1 1101 1100 = 1 D C. Check: 734 octal = 476 decimal = 256 + 208 + 12 = 1DC hex.

questions.question_en: A processor has a 32-bit address bus and an 8-bit addressable memory. What is the maximum memory it can directly address?
questions.explanation_en: With 32 address lines there are 2^32 = 4,294,967,296 distinct addresses; at one byte per address this is 4 GB. The width of the data bus does not change the number of addressable locations.

questions.question_en: An 8-to-3 priority encoder gives highest priority to input D7. If only inputs D5 and D2 are 1, the output code is:
questions.question_hi: 8-से-3 प्रायोरिटी एनकोडर में D7 को सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता है। यदि केवल D5 और D2 इनपुट 1 हैं, तो आउटपुट कोड क्या होगा?
questions.explanation_en: A priority encoder outputs the binary code of the highest-priority active input; D5 outranks D2, so the output is 5 = 101. 010 would be the code for D2.

questions.question_en: How many select lines are required for an 8-to-1 multiplexer?
questions.question_hi: 8-से-1 मल्टीप्लेक्सर के लिए कितनी सेलेक्ट लाइनें आवश्यक हैं?
questions.explanation_en: A MUX with 2^n data inputs needs n select lines; 8 = 2^3, so 3 select lines choose one of the 8 inputs. 8 is the number of data inputs, not select lines.

questions.question_en: An 8-bit shift register holds 00010110. After one shift-left operation (with 0 entering from the right), its contents and decimal value are:
questions.question_hi: एक 8-बिट शिफ्ट रजिस्टर में 00010110 है। एक बार बाएँ शिफ्ट करने (दाईं ओर से 0 प्रवेश) के बाद उसकी सामग्री और दशमलव मान क्या होंगे?
questions.explanation_en: Shifting left by one bit multiplies an unsigned number by 2: 00010110 = 22 becomes 00101100 = 44. A right shift would give 00001011 = 11 (division by 2).

questions.question_en: The decimal fraction 0.625 expressed in binary is:
questions.explanation_en: Multiply by 2 repeatedly: 0.625×2 = 1.25 (1), 0.25×2 = 0.5 (0), 0.5×2 = 1.0 (1). Reading the integer parts top-down gives 0.101, i.e. 1/2 + 1/8 = 0.625.

questions.question_en: Flash memory used in pen drives and SSDs is technically a form of:
questions.explanation_en: Flash is electrically erasable programmable ROM that erases whole blocks at a time rather than single bytes, which makes it cheap and dense. It is non-volatile and solid-state, unlike DRAM/SRAM (volatile) or magnetic disks.

questions.question_en: In a K-map, grouping eight adjacent 1s in a four-variable map eliminates how many variables from the resulting product term?
questions.explanation_en: A group of 2^k cells eliminates k variables: a pair removes one, a quad removes two and an octet removes three. In a 4-variable map an octet therefore leaves a single-literal term; a group of all 16 cells would make F = 1.

questions.question_en: A full adder can be constructed using:
questions.question_hi: फुल ऐडर का निर्माण किससे किया जा सकता है?

options.en: Two half adders and one OR gate
Two half adders and one AND gate
One half adder and one XOR gate

questions.explanation_en: The first half adder adds A and B; the second adds that sum to Cin giving the final Sum. The two partial carries are combined with an OR gate to give Cout (they can never both be 1).

questions.question_en: For a half adder with inputs A and B, the Sum and Carry outputs are respectively:
questions.question_hi: इनपुट A और B वाले हाफ ऐडर के Sum और Carry आउटपुट क्रमशः क्या हैं?
questions.explanation_en: A half adder adds two bits: Sum is 1 when exactly one input is 1 (XOR) and Carry is 1 only when both are 1 (AND). Swapping them (option 2) is the common slip.

questions.question_en: Which sequence correctly lists memory from fastest to slowest access time?
questions.explanation_en: Moving down the hierarchy, each level is larger, cheaper per bit and slower: registers (fastest), then cache, then main memory, then secondary storage such as a hard disk.

questions.question_en: The Format Painter tool in MS Word is used to:

options.en: Paint a watermark across every page
Change the colour of the page background
Copy formatting from one piece of text and apply it to another

questions.explanation_en: Format Painter picks up font, size, colour and paragraph formatting from the selection and applies it to the next text you select; double-clicking it keeps it active for repeated use.

questions.question_en: The cloud characteristic under which a customer is billed only for the computing resources actually consumed is known as:
questions.explanation_en: Cloud services are metered, so usage of storage, processing and bandwidth is measured and charged like an electricity bill, turning capital expenditure into operating expenditure.

questions.question_en: Pressing Shift + F3 on selected text in MS Word:

options.en: Cycles the text through UPPERCASE, lowercase and Capitalise Each Word

questions.explanation_en: Shift + F3 toggles the case of the selection among the case options. Shift + F7 opens the Thesaurus.

questions.question_en: The IT Act, 2000 was based on which international model law?

options.en: UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Commerce, 1996

questions.explanation_en: India enacted the IT Act following the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) Model Law on E-Commerce adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1997 (model law of 1996). India is not a party to the Budapest Convention.

questions.question_en: A program learns to play chess by playing many games against itself, receiving a positive reward for a win and a negative reward for a loss. This approach is:
questions.explanation_en: In reinforcement learning an agent interacts with an environment and improves its policy to maximise cumulative reward, as in AlphaZero. No labelled examples are given.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is the best example of the Internet of Things (IoT)?

options.en: A printed timetable on a notice board
A smart energy meter that sends electricity readings over the Internet to the supplier
A standalone desktop running a word processor offline

questions.explanation_en: IoT refers to everyday physical devices fitted with sensors, software and connectivity so that they collect and exchange data over the Internet, such as smart meters, smart watches and connected cameras.

questions.question_en: Which keyboard shortcut enters the current date into the active cell in MS Excel?
questions.explanation_en: Ctrl + ; (semicolon) inserts today's date as a fixed value; Ctrl + Shift + ; inserts the current time. Ctrl + D fills down and Ctrl + T creates a table.

questions.question_en: The single mobile app that gives citizens access to hundreds of central and state government services (EPFO, Income Tax, gas booking, etc.) is called:
questions.explanation_en: UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance), launched in 2017 by MeitY and NeGD, integrates many government services in one app. SWAYAM is a MOOC platform and e-Pathshala hosts NCERT e-books.

questions.question_en: The Government of India's initiative to use cloud computing for delivering e-services, under which a National Cloud is provided by NIC, is named:
questions.explanation_en: MeghRaj, the GI Cloud initiative of MeitY, aims to accelerate delivery of e-services through cloud infrastructure with the National Cloud operated by NIC. BharatNet is the rural broadband project.

questions.question_en: Who coined the term 'Artificial Intelligence' at the Dartmouth Conference in 1956?
questions.explanation_en: John McCarthy coined the term for the 1956 Dartmouth summer research project and later created the LISP language. Turing proposed the Turing Test earlier, in 1950.
A do-while loop runs its body once before checking the condition, so 10 is printed; then x < 5 is false and the loop ends.

questions.question_en: In Java, which keyword is used in a method header to declare the exceptions that the method may pass on to its caller?
questions.explanation_en: throws appears in the method signature, e.g. void read() throws IOException. throw is a statement that actually raises an exception object, e.g. throw new IOException();.
A static local variable is initialised once and keeps its value between calls. The three calls raise c to 1, 2 and 3, so the last call returns 3.

questions.question_en: In C++, if class D is derived as class D : protected B, the public members of B become ______ members of D.
questions.explanation_en: In protected inheritance, public and protected members of the base both become protected in the derived class. Private members of the base are never directly accessible in the derived class.

questions.question_en:
What does this Python code print?

s = "a,b,,c"
print(len(s.split(",")))
questions.explanation_en: split(',') splits at every comma, including adjacent ones, giving ['a', 'b', '', 'c'] - an empty string between the two commas - so the length is 4.

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

x = [1, 2]
x.append([3, 4])
x.extend([5, 6])
print(len(x), x[2])
questions.explanation_en: append adds its argument as one single element (the whole list [3, 4]), while extend adds each element of the iterable separately. x becomes [1, 2, [3, 4], 5, 6]: length 5, and x[2] is [3, 4].
get(ch, 0) returns 0 for a new character, so the loop builds a frequency table {h: 1, e: 1, l: 2, o: 1}. The letter l occurs twice and there are 4 distinct keys.
p points to a[0]; p + 2 points to a[2] and the dereference * gives its value 30. *(p + i) is equivalent to a[i].

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

s = "Mississippi"
print(s.count("ss"), s.find("sip"), s.replace("i", "I", 2))
questions.explanation_en: ss occurs twice. sip first appears at index 6 (M0 i1 s2 s3 i4 s5 s6 i7 p8). replace with count 2 changes only the first two i's.

After printing 1, a char is thrown, so the rest of the try block is skipped. C++ matches handlers by exact type without promotion: catch(int) does not match a char, catch(char) does and prints 4. Only the first matching handler runs, so catch(...) is skipped, then 6 is printed.

questions.question_en: In C, what is the data type of the result of the expression 'a' + 1?
questions.explanation_en: Arithmetic on char operands triggers integer promotion: the char is converted to int before the addition, so the expression has type int (value 98).

options.en: A NameError is raised because ABC is undefined
An object of Sq is created successfully
A TypeError is raised because Sq does not implement area()
A SyntaxError is raised because area() has an empty body

questions.explanation_en: Sq inherits the abstract method area() without overriding it, so Sq is still abstract. Python raises TypeError (Can't instantiate abstract class Sq...) when you try to create an object of it.

questions.question_en: Why should a C++ base class that is meant to be used polymorphically have a virtual destructor?

options.en: So that the constructor of the derived class becomes virtual
So that deleting a derived object through a base-class pointer also runs the derived destructor
So that the base-class destructor is never called
So that objects of the base class cannot be created

questions.explanation_en: If the destructor is not virtual, delete basePtr calls only the base destructor (formally undefined behaviour), so resources owned by the derived part leak. A virtual destructor makes the derived destructor run first, then the base destructor. Constructors cannot be virtual in C++.

questions.question_en:
What is the result of running the following Python code?

s = "hello"
s[0] = "H"
print(s)
questions.explanation_en: Python strings are immutable, so item assignment s[0] = 'H' raises TypeError. A new string must be built instead, e.g. 'H' + s[1:].
Subtracting two pointers into the same array gives the number of elements between them, not bytes. p points to index 4 and a to index 0, so the difference is 4.

questions.question_en: A variable declared inside a Java interface is implicitly:
questions.explanation_en: Interface fields are constants: they are automatically public static final and must be initialised where declared. Interface methods (without a body) are implicitly public abstract.
n takes the values 3, 6, 9 and then 12. The test n < 10 fails only when n is already 12, so 12 is printed.

questions.question_en: In the TCP/IP model, the layer that combines the functions of the OSI Physical and Data Link layers is the:
questions.explanation_en: The Network Access or Link layer of TCP/IP handles hardware addressing, framing and physical transmission, i.e. OSI layers 1 and 2. The Internet layer corresponds to OSI layer 3.

questions.question_en: What is the network (subnet) address of the host 192.168.10.77/26?
questions.explanation_en: A /26 mask is 255.255.255.192, block size 64. The subnets in the last octet are 0, 64, 128, 192; 77 falls in 64–127, so the network address is 192.168.10.64 (broadcast 192.168.10.127).

questions.question_en: Wired Ethernet traditionally used CSMA/CD, but Wi-Fi uses CSMA/CA because:

options.en: A wireless station cannot reliably detect collisions while transmitting, so it tries to avoid them
Wi-Fi uses token passing instead of carrier sensing
CSMA/CA gives higher speed than CSMA/CD on cables

questions.explanation_en: A radio cannot listen while it transmits and may not hear hidden stations, so collision detection is impractical. Wi-Fi therefore uses collision avoidance with random back-off and optional RTS/CTS.

questions.question_en: Which cable has a central copper conductor surrounded by an insulating layer, a braided metallic shield and an outer plastic jacket?
questions.explanation_en: This layered construction describes coaxial cable, used in cable TV and older Ethernet (10BASE2/10BASE5). UTP has no metallic shield and fibre has a glass core.

questions.question_en: Which application is generally best served by UDP rather than TCP?

options.en: Live voice call over the Internet (VoIP)

questions.explanation_en: Real-time voice tolerates the loss of a few packets but not the delay caused by retransmission, so UDP's low overhead suits it. Downloads, e-mail and banking pages need every byte to arrive correctly, so they use TCP.

questions.question_en: A device that connects two LAN segments and filters traffic by MAC address, thereby dividing one collision domain into two, is called a:
questions.explanation_en: A bridge is a two-port layer-2 device that forwards frames between segments only when needed; a switch is essentially a multi-port bridge. A repeater does not filter anything.

questions.question_en: Wi-Fi wireless LANs are based on which IEEE standard family?
questions.explanation_en: Wi-Fi is the IEEE 802.11 family (a/b/g/n/ac/ax). 802.3 is wired Ethernet, 802.15 covers wireless PANs such as Bluetooth, and 802.5 is Token Ring.

questions.question_en: The purpose of the Time To Live (TTL) field in an IPv4 packet is to:

options.en: Indicate how long a TCP connection may remain idle
Give the priority of the packet in a router queue
Stop a packet from circulating endlessly; each router decrements it and discards the packet at 0
Record the time at which the packet was created

questions.explanation_en: Every router reduces TTL by 1 and drops the packet when it reaches 0, preventing routing loops from flooding the network. The traceroute command exploits this behaviour. IPv6 calls the same field Hop Limit.

questions.question_en: In the Ethernet designation 100BASE-TX, what do '100', 'BASE' and 'T' indicate respectively?
questions.explanation_en: The number is the data rate in Mbps, BASE means baseband (the whole cable carries one digital signal) and T stands for twisted pair; F would mean fibre and 2/5 referred to thin/thick coaxial lengths.

questions.question_en: Which pair of remote-login protocols and ports is correct?
questions.explanation_en: SSH on port 22 encrypts the whole session, while Telnet on port 23 sends everything, including passwords, as clear text. That is why SSH has replaced Telnet for remote administration.

questions.question_en: TCP prevents a fast sender from overwhelming a slow receiver by using the:

options.en: Sliding window mechanism advertised by the receiver

questions.explanation_en: The receiver advertises a window size indicating how much data it can buffer, and the sender limits unacknowledged data to that window; this is TCP flow control. Checksum is for error detection and TTL belongs to IP.

questions.question_en: A geostationary communication satellite appears fixed above one point on the equator because it orbits at a height of approximately:
questions.explanation_en: At about 35,786 km (≈36,000 km) a satellite's orbital period equals the Earth's rotation period (24 h), so it stays over the same spot; this is why a fixed dish antenna works.

questions.question_en: In UNIX/Linux, what happens when a process successfully calls one of the exec() family of system calls?

options.en: A new child process is created that is a copy of the caller
The process waits until one of its children terminates
Its memory image is replaced by a new program, while the process ID stays the same
The process terminates and returns a status to its parent

questions.explanation_en: exec loads a new program into the CURRENT process, replacing its code, data and stack; the PID is unchanged and exec does not return on success. Creating a copy is fork(), ending is exit() and waiting is wait().

questions.question_en: Page size is 4 KB (4096 bytes) and page 3 of a process is loaded in frame 7. What physical address corresponds to the logical address 13000 (decimal)?
questions.explanation_en: Page = 13000 ÷ 4096 = 3 (3 × 4096 = 12288), offset = 13000 − 12288 = 712. Physical = 7 × 4096 + 712 = 28672 + 712 = 29384. 28672 is only the frame's base address without the offset.

questions.question_en: A high-priority process H is waiting for a resource held by a low-priority process L, while a medium-priority process M keeps preempting L. H therefore waits indefinitely. This problem and its standard remedy are:

options.en: Priority inversion; resolved by priority-inheritance protocol

questions.explanation_en: This is priority inversion: a low-priority process effectively blocks a high-priority one. With priority inheritance, L temporarily inherits H's priority until it releases the resource, so M can no longer preempt it. The Mars Pathfinder incident is the famous example.

questions.question_en: A child process on UNIX/Linux has finished executing, but its parent has not yet called wait() to read its exit status. The child is now a:
questions.explanation_en: A terminated process whose entry still remains in the process table because the parent has not collected its status is a zombie. An orphan is the opposite situation: the parent terminates first and the child is adopted by init/systemd. A daemon is a background service process.

questions.question_en: A CPU uses a relocation (base) register = 24000 and a limit register = 5000. A process generates the logical address 4200. The resulting physical address is:
questions.explanation_en: The MMU first checks 4200 < limit 5000 (valid), then adds the base: 24000 + 4200 = 28200. A trap would occur only for a logical address of 5000 or more.

questions.question_en: The system calls open(), read(), write() and close() belong to which category?
questions.explanation_en: File-management calls create, open, read, write, close and delete files. Process control includes fork, exec, exit and wait; information maintenance includes getpid, time and date calls.

questions.question_en: A process is best defined as:

options.en: A collection of files belonging to one user
A set of instructions written in a high-level language
A program in execution, including its current activity
A program stored on the disk

questions.explanation_en: A program is a passive entity (a file on disk); a process is that program in execution together with its program counter, registers, stack, heap and data section. The same program run twice gives two processes.

questions.question_en: A process is moved from the Running state to the Ready state when:

options.en: Its time quantum expires or a higher-priority process arrives

questions.explanation_en: Preemption (quantum expiry in round robin, or arrival of a higher-priority process in preemptive priority scheduling) takes the CPU away from a process that can still run, so it returns to the ready queue. An I/O request sends it to Waiting; exit() sends it to Terminated.

questions.question_en: The act of saving the state of the currently running process and loading the saved state of the next process is called:
questions.explanation_en: A context switch saves the old process's context in its PCB and restores the new process's context. It is pure overhead, since no useful user work is done during the switch, and its cost depends on hardware (register count, memory-management support).

questions.question_en: A segment table has: segment 0 (base 2000, length 600), segment 1 (base 5200, length 300), segment 2 (base 3100, length 900). Which logical address (segment, offset) causes an addressing trap?
questions.explanation_en: An offset must be smaller than the segment length. Segment 1 has length 300, so offset 320 is illegal → trap. The others are legal: (0,599) → 2599, (2,750) → 3850, (1,299) → 5499.

questions.question_en: Which operator is used with a subquery that returns multiple values, e.g., WHERE D_ID ______ (SELECT D_ID FROM DEPT WHERE City = 'Delhi')?
questions.explanation_en: '=' works only with a single-row subquery; a multi-row subquery needs IN, ANY/SOME, ALL or EXISTS. Using '=' with multiple rows raises 'subquery returns more than 1 row'.

questions.question_en: Which ACID property guarantees that once a transaction is committed, its changes survive a system crash or power failure?
questions.explanation_en: Durability is ensured by writing to a log/journal before confirming the commit, so committed data can be recovered. Atomicity deals with partial failures within a transaction, not persistence.

questions.question_en: A transaction has executed its last statement but has not yet been committed. According to the transaction state diagram it is in the ______ state.
questions.explanation_en: States: Active → Partially committed (after final statement) → Committed (after commit succeeds). If something goes wrong in active or partially committed state it moves to Failed → Aborted.

questions.question_en: If the base table EMP is modified after a view V on EMP was created, a subsequent SELECT * FROM V will:

options.en: Show the updated data, because the view query runs on the current table
Show only the rows that existed at creation time
Show the old data until the view is recreated

questions.explanation_en: A standard view is not a stored copy; it executes its defining SELECT each time, so it always reflects the current contents of the base table.

questions.question_en: The number of attributes in a relation is called its:
questions.explanation_en: Degree (or arity) is the number of columns; cardinality is the number of tuples (rows). A relation EMP(ID, Name, Salary) has degree 3.

questions.question_en: Tables EMP(E_ID, Name, D_ID) with 5 rows and DEPT(D_ID, D_Name) with 3 rows. The query SELECT * FROM EMP, DEPT; (no WHERE clause) returns:
questions.explanation_en: Listing two tables without a join condition produces a Cartesian product (cross join): 5 × 3 = 15 rows. Adding WHERE EMP.D_ID = DEPT.D_ID turns it into an equi-join.

questions.question_en: In relation ENROL(Student_ID, Course_ID, Grade) where a student can take many courses, the primary key is:
questions.explanation_en: Neither Student_ID nor Course_ID alone is unique because a student takes many courses and a course has many students; the combination is unique, giving a composite primary key.

questions.question_en: What is the difference between a UNIQUE constraint and a PRIMARY KEY constraint in MySQL?

options.en: UNIQUE disallows NULL while PRIMARY KEY allows it
A table can have many UNIQUE constraints that allow NULL, but only one PRIMARY KEY that disallows NULL
A PRIMARY KEY can be duplicated but UNIQUE cannot

questions.explanation_en: Both enforce uniqueness, but PRIMARY KEY also implies NOT NULL and a table may have only one; UNIQUE columns may hold NULLs (multiple NULLs in MySQL) and several UNIQUE constraints can exist.

questions.question_en: STUDENT(Class, Name): (10, Asha), (10, Ravi), (11, Neha), (12, Dev), (11, Om), (10, Tara). Output of SELECT Class, COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT GROUP BY Class ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, Class; is:
questions.explanation_en: Counts: Class 10 has 3, Class 11 has 2, Class 12 has 1. ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC sorts from largest group to smallest, giving 10, 11, 12.

questions.question_en: Table T(ID INT PRIMARY KEY, Code VARCHAR(5) UNIQUE). Two rows are inserted: (1, NULL) and (2, NULL). In MySQL InnoDB this:

options.en: Succeeds only for the first row
Fails, because UNIQUE implies NOT NULL
Succeeds, because UNIQUE allows multiple NULLs
Fails, because NULL = NULL violates UNIQUE

questions.explanation_en: In SQL, NULL is not equal to anything including NULL, so a UNIQUE index in MySQL permits any number of NULLs. A PRIMARY KEY column, however, cannot be NULL at all.

questions.question_en: Which CSS selector targets all <input> elements whose type attribute is exactly "text"?
questions.explanation_en: Square brackets form an attribute selector: [type="text"] matches the attribute value exactly. input.type.text would look for classes named type and text.

questions.question_en: What is the default value of the CSS position property for HTML elements?
questions.explanation_en: Every element is position: static by default, meaning it follows normal document flow and ignores top/left/right/bottom offsets and z-index.

questions.question_en: Where are HTTP cookies stored?

options.en: On the client, in the user's browser
Only in the web server's database
Inside the HTML file of the page

questions.explanation_en: A cookie is a small piece of data the server asks the browser to store and send back with later requests to the same site. Server-side sessions, by contrast, keep data on the server and usually identify the user with a session-id cookie.

questions.question_en: An HTTP method is idempotent if making the same request many times has the same effect on the server as making it once. Which of these methods is NOT idempotent?
questions.explanation_en: Sending the same POST twice may create two orders or two records, so POST is not idempotent. GET does not change state, and repeating a PUT or DELETE leaves the server in the same final state.

questions.question_en: A freelance photographer licenses her photos to companies through a stock-image website. Which e-commerce model does this represent?
questions.explanation_en: In C2B the individual is the seller and the business is the buyer, reversing the usual B2C flow. Freelance services and reverse auctions are typical C2B examples.

questions.question_en: Which tag pair should be used to give text strong importance (semantic meaning), rather than merely making it look bold?
questions.explanation_en: <strong> conveys importance to browsers and screen readers, which usually render it bold. <b> is purely presentational, and <big> and <font> are obsolete in HTML5.

questions.question_en: HTTPS secures web traffic by running HTTP over which protocol, and on which default port?
questions.explanation_en: HTTPS = HTTP over TLS/SSL, using port 443 by default, with the server's identity proved by a certificate. Plain HTTP uses port 80.
The inner function forms a closure over the variable c, which survives between calls. The three calls make c 1, 2 and 3, and the third return value, 3, is printed.

questions.question_en: A queue is implemented with two stacks: enqueue pushes onto S1; dequeue pops from S2, first moving ALL elements of S1 into S2 (pop then push) if S2 is empty. For the sequence enqueue 1, enqueue 2, enqueue 3, dequeue, enqueue 4, enqueue 5, dequeue, dequeue, dequeue — how many push operations are performed in total on both stacks?
questions.explanation_en: Enqueue 1–3: 3 pushes. First dequeue: move 3 items to S2 (3 pushes), pop 1. Enqueue 4, 5: 2 pushes. Next two dequeues pop 2 and 3 from S2. Last dequeue: S2 empty, move 4 and 5 (2 pushes), pop 4. Total = 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 10.

questions.question_en: To insert a new element at the FIRST position of an unsorted array that currently holds n elements (with spare capacity), the worst-case time complexity is:
questions.explanation_en: All n existing elements must be shifted one place to the right to make room at index 0, so the work grows linearly. Inserting at the end would be O(1).

questions.question_en: Which sorting algorithm repeatedly finds the minimum element of the unsorted part and swaps it into the first position of that part?
questions.explanation_en: Selection sort 'selects' the smallest remaining element on each pass. Insertion sort instead takes the next element and inserts it into the already sorted left part.

questions.question_en: The time required to build a binary heap from an unordered array of n elements using the bottom-up (heapify) method is:
questions.explanation_en: Most nodes are near the bottom and sift down only a little; summing the heights gives a total that is bounded by 2n, i.e. O(n). Inserting the n elements one at a time would cost O(n log n).

questions.question_en: How many structurally different binary search trees can be built using the three keys 1, 2 and 3?
questions.explanation_en: The count is the Catalan number C(3) = (1/(3+1)) × 6C3 = 20/4 = 5: root 1 (2 shapes), root 2 (1 shape), root 3 (2 shapes). 6 = 3! counts insertion orders, but two orders (2,1,3 and 2,3,1) give the same tree.

questions.question_en: What is the minimum number of stacks needed to implement a queue (without using any other data structure)?
questions.explanation_en: One stack receives enqueued items; when a dequeue is needed and the second stack is empty, all items are popped from the first and pushed onto the second, reversing them into FIFO order. A single stack can only give LIFO order.

questions.question_en: In a structure chart, a well-designed system generally shows:

options.en: High fan-in for utility modules and low-to-moderate fan-out
Low fan-in and very high fan-out for every module
Equal fan-in and fan-out for all modules

questions.explanation_en: Fan-in is the number of modules that call a given module; high fan-in means good reuse. Fan-out is the number of modules a module calls; very high fan-out suggests poor decomposition and complexity.

questions.question_en: The spiral model of software development was proposed by:
questions.explanation_en: Barry Boehm described the risk-driven spiral model in 1986 (published widely in 1988). Royce is linked with the waterfall paper of 1970, Schwaber co-created Scrum, and Jacobson is known for use cases and UML.

questions.question_en: Which UML diagram emphasises the time ordering of messages exchanged between objects, using vertical lifelines?
questions.explanation_en: A sequence diagram arranges objects horizontally and time vertically, so the order of messages is easy to read. A communication diagram shows the same interactions but emphasises links between objects rather than time.

questions.question_en: Which black-box technique represents combinations of input conditions (causes) and actions (effects) in tabular form to derive test cases?
questions.explanation_en: Decision tables list every combination of conditions and the corresponding actions; each column becomes a test case. Basis path, statement coverage and data-flow testing are white-box techniques.

questions.question_en: Which type of coupling is the WORST (most undesirable)?
questions.explanation_en: Content coupling occurs when one module directly modifies or depends on the internal workings of another, so a change in one breaks the other. From best to worst: data, stamp, control, external, common, content.

questions.question_en: In the Herbartian step of 'Association (Comparison)' while teaching 'Linear search', the teacher would most appropriately:

options.en: Announce the objectives of the lesson
Give the students a program to write at home
Define linear search and write its algorithm
Relate linear search with the way students search for a name in an unsorted attendance list

questions.explanation_en: Association links the newly presented idea with familiar experiences or earlier knowledge so that it is assimilated (Herbart's apperception). Defining and stating the algorithm is Presentation; homework belongs to Application.

questions.question_en:
Match the teaching method with its originator.
A. Project method   1. Socrates
B. Heuristic method   2. W. H. Kilpatrick
C. Question–answer (dialectic) method   3. H. E. Armstrong
questions.explanation_en: Kilpatrick (a student of Dewey) gave the project method, H. E. Armstrong introduced the heuristic method of teaching science, and the questioning method goes back to Socrates. Hence A-2, B-3, C-1.

questions.question_en: A test of 'Python programming' is found to give almost the same scores when the same students take it again after a week, but its items mostly test English vocabulary. The test is:
questions.explanation_en: Consistent scores across two administrations show test–retest reliability. But the items do not measure what the test claims (programming), so content validity is poor. A test can be reliable without being valid, though not the reverse.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a good test?
questions.explanation_en: A good test is valid (measures what it claims), reliable (consistent), objective (scorer-independent), usable and discriminating. Subjectivity in scoring reduces reliability and is a defect.

questions.question_en: The draft of the National Education Policy 2020 was prepared by a committee chaired by:
questions.explanation_en: Former ISRO chairman Dr K. Kasturirangan chaired the drafting committee (draft submitted 2019). T. S. R. Subramanian chaired an earlier 2016 committee; Kothari headed the 1964–66 Education Commission.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a correctly written behavioural (specific) objective for a lesson on data types?

options.en: To make students understand data types
The student will be able to classify given literals as int, float or string
To teach the concept of data types
The student will appreciate data types

questions.explanation_en: A behavioural objective is stated from the learner's side, uses an action verb and is observable ('classify given literals'). 'Understand', 'appreciate' and teacher-centred 'to teach' are vague and not directly observable.

questions.question_en: To introduce sequencing, loops and events to Class 6 students without the burden of syntax errors, the most suitable ICT tool is:
questions.explanation_en: Scratch, developed at the MIT Media Lab, uses drag-and-drop blocks, so children learn programming logic without syntax errors. MySQL Workbench and Wireshark are database and network tools, and a C compiler demands precise syntax.

questions.question_en: Which of the following features correctly describes an Open Educational Resource (OER)?

options.en: Any resource that is available on the Internet for a fee
Content that may be freely used, adapted and redistributed under an open licence such as Creative Commons
A video that can be viewed but never downloaded
A software purchased by the school for teaching

questions.explanation_en: OERs are teaching, learning and research materials in the public domain or released under an open licence permitting free use, adaptation and sharing (the '5 Rs': retain, reuse, revise, remix, redistribute). NROER and DIKSHA host Indian OERs.

questions.question_en: The three-dimensional chart that shows the weightage given to objectives, content units and forms of questions while setting a question paper is called the:
questions.explanation_en: A blueprint (design of the question paper) specifies weightage to objectives, content and question types, ensuring content validity. A rubric is a scoring guide for performance tasks.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a norm-referenced interpretation of a test score?

options.en: Rohan can write a program for the given flowchart
Rohan scored higher than 85% of his classmates
Rohan has mastered 90% of the loop concepts
Rohan needs remedial teaching on arrays

questions.explanation_en: Norm-referenced tests compare a student with the group (percentile ranks, class ranking). Criterion-referenced tests report mastery against a fixed standard, as in the other three options.

tests.description: 200 new questions in the real exam blueprint (Section A 100 + Section B 100, 120 min, −0.25).
