questions.question_en: The race-around condition in a level-triggered JK flip-flop occurs when:
questions.question_hi: लेवल-ट्रिगर्ड JK फ्लिप-फ्लॉप में रेस-अराउंड स्थिति कब उत्पन्न होती है?

options.en: J = K = 0 and the clock is low
J = K = 1 and the clock pulse is wider than the propagation delay
J = K = 1 and the clock pulse is shorter than the propagation delay
J = 1, K = 0 and the clock is very fast

questions.explanation_en: With J = K = 1 the output keeps toggling as long as the clock stays high; if the pulse width exceeds the flip-flop's propagation delay it toggles several times and the final state is uncertain. Master–slave or edge-triggered designs remove it.

questions.question_en: A T flip-flop has its T input permanently tied to 1 and is driven by a 10 kHz clock. The frequency of its output Q is:
questions.question_hi: एक T फ्लिप-फ्लॉप का T इनपुट स्थायी रूप से 1 है और उसे 10 kHz क्लॉक दी जाती है। आउटपुट Q की आवृत्ति क्या होगी?
questions.explanation_en: With T = 1 the output toggles on every clock edge, so one full output cycle takes two clock cycles; the frequency is divided by 2: 10/2 = 5 kHz. 2.5 kHz would need two cascaded toggling stages.

questions.question_en: In 8-bit 2's complement arithmetic, 01100100 (+100) is added to 00110010 (+50). What happens?

options.en: Overflow occurs; the stored result 10010110 reads as −106
The correct result +150 is stored as 10010110
The ALU automatically extends the result to 9 bits
An end carry is generated and discarded, giving +22

questions.explanation_en: +150 exceeds the 8-bit signed maximum of +127. The sum 10010110 has its sign bit set, so it is interpreted as −(01101010) = −106. Two positive operands producing a negative result is the classic overflow signature.

questions.question_en: According to the excitation table of a JK flip-flop, to make the output change from Q = 0 to Q = 1, the required inputs are:
questions.question_hi: JK फ्लिप-फ्लॉप की एक्साइटेशन तालिका के अनुसार आउटपुट को Q = 0 से Q = 1 करने के लिए आवश्यक इनपुट क्या हैं?
questions.explanation_en: A 0→1 transition is achieved either by setting (J = 1, K = 0) or toggling (J = 1, K = 1), so K is a don't-care: J = 1, K = X. J = 0, K = X is the entry for 0→0.

questions.question_en: Fifth-generation computing is most closely associated with which of the following?

options.en: Artificial intelligence and parallel processing using ULSI chips

questions.explanation_en: The fifth generation (1980s onward) aims at machines that understand natural language and reason, using AI, parallel processing and Ultra Large Scale Integration. The other options describe earlier generations.

questions.question_en: Which of the following 4-bit groups is NOT a valid BCD digit?
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा 4-बिट समूह मान्य BCD अंक नहीं है?
questions.explanation_en: BCD uses only 0000–1001 for the digits 0–9; the six patterns 1010–1111 are invalid. 1100 (decimal 12) is therefore not a BCD digit, while 1001 = 9 and 1000 = 8 are valid.

questions.question_en: A circuit whose output depends on the present inputs as well as on its past state (stored in memory elements) is called a:
questions.question_hi: वह परिपथ जिसका आउटपुट वर्तमान इनपुट के साथ-साथ पिछली अवस्था पर भी निर्भर करता है, क्या कहलाता है?
questions.explanation_en: Sequential circuits (flip-flops, counters, registers) contain memory, so the output depends on the input history. Combinational circuits such as MUXes and decoders depend only on present inputs.

questions.question_en: In a full adder with inputs A, B and carry-in Cin, the carry-out Cout can be written as:
questions.question_hi: इनपुट A, B और Cin वाले फुल ऐडर का कैरी-आउट Cout किस प्रकार लिखा जा सकता है?
questions.explanation_en: Cout = AB + BCin + ACin, which is equivalently AB + Cin(A ⊕ B) — the form obtained when a full adder is built from two half adders. A ⊕ B ⊕ Cin is the Sum output, not the carry.

questions.question_en: An AND gate whose two inputs are both inverted (a 'bubbled' AND gate) is logically equivalent to:
questions.explanation_en: The output is A'·B', which by De Morgan's theorem equals (A + B)', the NOR function. Similarly a bubbled OR gate (A' + B') equals a NAND gate. This equivalence is the basis of converting AND-OR networks into NAND-NAND or NOR-NOR form.

questions.question_en: Which of the following printers is a non-impact printer?
questions.explanation_en: A laser printer forms the image with a laser, toner and heat, with nothing striking the paper, so it is non-impact. Dot-matrix, daisy-wheel and drum printers all hammer pins or characters against a ribbon.

questions.question_en: Which type of ROM is erased by exposing the chip to ultraviolet light through a quartz window?
questions.explanation_en: EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM) is wiped by UV light and then reprogrammed. EEPROM is erased electrically, PROM can be programmed only once and Mask ROM is fixed at manufacture.

questions.question_en: The fourth generation of computers is chiefly characterised by the use of:
questions.explanation_en: From 1971 onward, VLSI technology put a whole CPU on a single chip (the microprocessor), making personal computers possible. Transistors belong to the second generation and SSI/MSI ICs to the third.

questions.question_en: Renting virtual machines, storage and networks from a provider such as Amazon EC2, on which the customer installs and manages its own operating system, is an example of:
questions.explanation_en: Infrastructure as a Service offers the basic computing infrastructure; the customer remains responsible for the OS, middleware and applications. With PaaS the provider would also manage the OS and runtime.

questions.question_en: A teacher wants the school logo, font style and colour scheme to appear identically on every slide of a 40-slide presentation without editing each slide. She should use the:
questions.explanation_en: Changes made in the Slide Master are applied to all slides based on its layouts, ensuring a uniform design. The Animation Pane only controls effects on objects.

questions.question_en: An attacker poisons a DNS server so that users typing the correct address of a bank are silently redirected to a fake look-alike website. This attack is known as:
questions.explanation_en: Pharming manipulates DNS or the hosts file so even a correctly typed URL leads to a fraudulent site. Phishing, by contrast, relies on luring the user to click a deceptive link.

questions.question_en: What does the Excel formula =INT(-7.4) return?
questions.explanation_en: INT rounds a number DOWN to the nearest integer, i.e. towards minus infinity, so −7.4 becomes −8. TRUNC(−7.4) would give −7 by simply removing the decimal part.

questions.question_en: A machine-learning model scores 99% accuracy on its training data but only 60% on new, unseen test data. The model is most likely suffering from:
questions.explanation_en: Overfitting means the model has memorised noise in the training set and fails to generalise. Underfitting would show poor accuracy on both training and test data.

questions.question_en: In MS Excel, the error value #DIV/0! is displayed when a formula:

options.en: Produces a result too wide for the column
Divides a number by zero or by an empty cell

questions.explanation_en: #DIV/0! appears when the divisor is 0 or blank. A deleted reference gives #REF!, a misspelled function gives #NAME? and a too-narrow column shows #####.

questions.question_en: Which PowerPoint view shows miniature versions of all slides together so that they can be easily rearranged by dragging?
questions.explanation_en: Slide Sorter displays thumbnails of every slide, making it easy to reorder, delete or apply transitions to many slides at once.

questions.question_en: A principal wants to send the same invitation letter to 300 parents, each letter showing the parent's own name and address. The MS Word feature to use is:
questions.explanation_en: Mail Merge combines a main document with a data source (a list of names and addresses) to produce a personalised copy for every record.

questions.question_en: A program that appears to be a useful free game but secretly gives an attacker access to the computer is known as a:
questions.explanation_en: Like the wooden horse of legend, a Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software; unlike a worm, it does not replicate on its own.

questions.question_en: Cells A1:A5 contain 40, 60, 75, 50 and 90. What is the result of =SUMIF(A1:A5,">50")?
questions.explanation_en: Only values strictly greater than 50 are added: 60 + 75 + 90 = 225. Including 50 (as '>=50' would) gives 275.
x = 5 is an assignment, not a comparison; its value is 5, which is non-zero and therefore true. This classic bug prints Yes.
A string literal initialiser includes the terminating null character, so the array holds h, e, l, l, o and '\0' = 6 bytes. strlen(s) would give 5.

questions.question_en: Run-time polymorphism through virtual functions in C++ is usually implemented by the compiler using:

options.en: A virtual table (vtable) and a hidden virtual pointer (vptr)
Inline expansion of all member functions
A separate copy of each function for every object

questions.explanation_en: Each class with virtual functions gets a vtable of function addresses, and each object carries a hidden vptr pointing to its class's vtable. A virtual call looks up the address through the vptr at run time. Templates and inlining are compile-time mechanisms.

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

with open("s.txt", "w") as f:
    f.writelines(["a\n", "b\n", "c"])

with open("s.txt") as f:
    lines = f.readlines()
print(len(lines), lines[-1])
questions.explanation_en: writelines() writes the strings exactly as given and adds no newlines of its own, so the file holds a, b and c on three lines (the last without a newline). readlines() returns a list of 3 lines, the last being 'c'.

questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?

class Counter:
    total = 0
    def __init__(self):
        self.total += 1

c1 = Counter()
c2 = Counter()
print(c1.total, c2.total, Counter.total)
questions.explanation_en: self.total += 1 reads the class attribute (0) but assigns to self.total, creating a new instance attribute with value 1 in each object. The class attribute Counter.total is never changed, so it stays 0. To share a count you must write Counter.total += 1.

When return x executes, the value 20 is saved as the return value. finally then runs and changes the local x to 30, but that does not alter the already-saved return value. (A return statement inside finally would override it.)

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

with open("n.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("0123456789")

with open("n.txt") as f:
    f.seek(4)
    print(f.read(3), f.tell())
questions.explanation_en: seek(4) moves the file pointer to offset 4 (counting from 0), so read(3) returns the characters at positions 4, 5 and 6: 456. The pointer is then at offset 7, which tell() reports.

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

nums = [x * x for x in range(1, 8) if x % 2 == 1]
print(nums, sum(nums))
questions.explanation_en: range(1, 8) gives 1 to 7; the condition keeps the odd values 1, 3, 5, 7, whose squares are 1, 9, 25, 49. Their sum is 84.
Addresses of x and y are passed, so the function swaps the actual variables through the pointers. x becomes 2 and y becomes 1, printing 21.
Java passes everything by value, but for an array the value is a reference, so modify changes the shared array element. The primitive b is copied, so b stays 1.

questions.question_en: Which statement correctly compares an abstract class and an interface in Java (Java 8 or later)?

options.en: An abstract class may contain only abstract methods
A class can implement many interfaces but can extend only one abstract class
Methods of an interface are private by default
An abstract class cannot have a constructor

questions.explanation_en: Java allows single class inheritance but multiple interface implementation. An abstract class can have constructors, instance fields and concrete methods; interface methods are public by default.
The sequence from fib(0) is 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, so fib(6) = 8.
First i++ yields 10 (i becomes 11), second i++ yields 11 (i becomes 12). The sum 21 is then assigned to i, overwriting the 12.
*p++ dereferences first and then increments the pointer (postfix ++ binds to p). So v = 3 and p now points to 6. (*p)++ would instead increment the value a[0].

questions.question_en:
What is printed by the following Java statement?

System.out.println(10 + 20 + "30" + 10 + 20);
questions.explanation_en: Evaluation is left to right. 10 + 20 = 30 (numeric). Then 30 + "30" becomes string "3030", after which + performs concatenation: "303010" and then "30301020".
Constructors run from base to derived (B then D); destructors run in the reverse order, derived first (~D then ~B).
count is static, so one copy is shared by all objects and reaches 3 after three constructions. id is an instance variable; object a stored the value of count at the time it was created, i.e. 1.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Data Link layer?
questions.explanation_en: Logical addressing (IP addresses) is a Network layer function. Framing, MAC addressing, error detection and media access control are all Data Link layer responsibilities.

questions.question_en: Which networking device can operate at all seven layers of the OSI model, translating between entirely different protocol suites?
questions.explanation_en: A gateway performs protocol conversion and may work up to the Application layer. A switch works at layer 2, a bridge at layer 2 and a router at layer 3.

questions.question_en: Which Wi-Fi security protocol is considered the weakest and should no longer be used?
questions.explanation_en: Wired Equivalent Privacy has serious flaws and can be cracked in minutes. WPA2 with AES and the newer WPA3 are the recommended options.

questions.question_en: Which routing protocol is used to exchange routes between different autonomous systems (for example, between ISPs) on the Internet?
questions.explanation_en: Border Gateway Protocol is the exterior gateway protocol that connects autonomous systems. RIP and OSPF are interior protocols used within one organisation, and ARP is not a routing protocol at all.

questions.question_en: A 100 MB file is downloaded over a link with an effective speed of 8 Mbps. Ignoring overheads, the download time is approximately (take 1 MB = 8 Mb):
questions.explanation_en: 100 MB = 100 × 8 = 800 megabits. Time = 800 Mb ÷ 8 Mbps = 100 s. Dividing 100 by 8 gives 12.5 s, the trap of forgetting that link speed is in bits and file size in bytes.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is an unguided (wireless) transmission medium?
questions.explanation_en: Guided media use a physical conductor (copper or glass). Microwave, radio waves and infrared travel through free space and are unguided media.

questions.question_en: A teacher reads her school e-mail on a laptop, a phone and a desktop and wants every folder and 'read' status to stay synchronised on all of them. The retrieval protocol best suited is:
questions.explanation_en: IMAP keeps messages and folders on the server and synchronises state across devices. POP3 usually downloads and removes mail from the server, so the devices fall out of sync; SMTP only sends mail.

questions.question_en: HTTP is called a 'stateless' protocol because:

options.en: It works without a TCP connection
The server does not retain information about previous requests from the same client
It does not use any port number
It cannot carry images or video

questions.explanation_en: Each HTTP request is processed independently; the server keeps no memory of earlier requests. Websites therefore use cookies or sessions to remember logged-in users.

questions.question_en: The well-known port number of HTTP is:
questions.explanation_en: HTTP servers listen on port 80 by default. Port 25 is SMTP, 110 is POP3 and 53 is DNS.

questions.question_en: In symmetric-key cryptography such as AES:

options.en: The same secret key is used for encryption and decryption
No key is needed for decryption
A public key encrypts and a private key decrypts
Each message uses a key pair published in a directory

questions.explanation_en: Symmetric algorithms (AES, DES) share one secret key between sender and receiver, making them fast but creating a key-distribution problem. Public/private key pairs are used in asymmetric systems such as RSA.

questions.question_en: The subnet mask written in CIDR notation as /26 is equivalent to:
questions.explanation_en: /26 means 26 one-bits: 24 bits give 255.255.255 and the remaining 2 bits in the last octet give 128 + 64 = 192. /25 is .128 and /27 is .224.

questions.question_en: DNS queries are normally sent to which port?
questions.explanation_en: DNS uses port 53 (UDP for ordinary queries, TCP for zone transfers and large replies). 67 is DHCP server, 123 is NTP and 161 is SNMP.

questions.question_en: Processes P1, P2, P3 with bursts 10, 5, 8 ms arrive at time 0 and are scheduled by Round Robin with quantum 4 ms. The response time of P3 (time from arrival until it first gets the CPU) is:
questions.explanation_en: P1 runs 0-4 and P2 runs 4-8, so P3 first receives the CPU at time 8; response time = 8 − 0 = 8 ms. Response time matters for interactive systems and is what RR is designed to keep small.

questions.question_en: Which technique lets a program larger than the available memory run by keeping in memory only those instructions and data needed at a given time, with the PROGRAMMER designing which parts replace each other?
questions.explanation_en: Overlays are programmer-managed: independent sections are loaded over one another. Demand paging achieves a similar effect automatically by the OS and hardware, without programmer design.

questions.question_en: Requiring a process to request and be allocated ALL the resources it needs before it begins execution is a deadlock-prevention technique that breaks:
questions.explanation_en: A process that already holds everything never waits while holding, so the hold-and-wait condition is denied. Its drawbacks are low resource utilisation and possible starvation.

questions.question_en: Numbering all resource types and forcing every process to request resources only in increasing order of their numbers prevents deadlock by eliminating which condition?
questions.explanation_en: If requests always go up the numbering, a cycle P1→P2→…→P1 would need a resource number to be both larger and smaller than another, which is impossible, so circular wait cannot occur.

questions.question_en: A situation in which a process spends more time swapping pages in and out than executing, causing CPU utilisation to drop sharply, is called:
questions.explanation_en: Thrashing happens when processes do not have enough frames for their working sets, so page faults occur continuously. Raising the degree of multiprogramming at this point makes it worse.

questions.question_en: In the output of ls -l a file is shown as -rw-r-----. The equivalent numeric (octal) permission is:
questions.explanation_en: The leading '-' means a regular file. Owner rw- = 4+2 = 6, group r-- = 4, others --- = 0 → 640. 644 would give others read permission too.

questions.question_en: A system call is best described as:

options.en: The programming interface through which a user program requests a service from the operating-system kernel
A command typed by the user at the shell prompt
A call from one user function to another in the same program
A hardware interrupt generated by an I/O device

questions.explanation_en: System calls (e.g. open, read, fork) are the entry points into the kernel; they switch the CPU from user mode to kernel mode through a trap. Shell commands are programs that themselves use system calls.

questions.question_en: SPOOL in the context of operating systems stands for:
questions.explanation_en: Spooling (Simultaneous Peripheral Operation On-Line) buffers data for a slow device such as a printer on disk so that the CPU and other programs need not wait for the device.

questions.question_en: The component of the operating system that actually gives control of the CPU to the process selected by the short-term scheduler is called the:
questions.explanation_en: The dispatcher performs the context switch, switches to user mode and jumps to the proper location in the user program. The time it takes to stop one process and start another is the dispatch latency.

questions.question_en: Wasted memory INSIDE an allocated partition, because the partition is larger than the process placed in it, is called:
questions.explanation_en: Fixed-size partitions/pages leave unused space inside the block — internal fragmentation. External fragmentation is free memory scattered in small holes BETWEEN allocations.

questions.question_en: Which clause is used to filter groups after GROUP BY has been applied?
questions.explanation_en: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping and cannot contain aggregate functions; HAVING filters the groups produced by GROUP BY and may use aggregates like COUNT or SUM.

questions.question_en: The main purpose of creating an index on a table column is to:

options.en: Speed up searching and retrieval of rows
Reduce the storage size of the table

questions.explanation_en: An index is an auxiliary structure (usually a B+ tree) that lets the DBMS locate rows without a full table scan. It uses extra storage and slows inserts/updates slightly.

questions.question_en: Which data structure is most commonly used to implement indexes in relational databases such as MySQL InnoDB?
questions.explanation_en: B+ trees are balanced, keep all keys in leaf nodes linked together (good for range queries) and have high fan-out, which minimises disk reads. Hash indexes support only equality lookups.

questions.question_en: Which statement adds a new column 'Email VARCHAR(50)' to an existing table STUDENT?

options.en: INSERT INTO STUDENT COLUMN Email VARCHAR(50);
MODIFY TABLE STUDENT ADD Email VARCHAR(50);
ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD Email VARCHAR(50);

questions.explanation_en: Structural changes use ALTER TABLE ... ADD / DROP / MODIFY (or CHANGE in MySQL). UPDATE and INSERT only change data, not the schema.

questions.question_en: A view in SQL is best described as a:

options.en: Virtual table defined by a stored SELECT query
Physical copy of a table on disk

questions.explanation_en: A view stores only the query definition; its rows are computed each time it is referenced. A materialised view (not supported natively in MySQL) would store the data physically.

questions.question_en: An index whose search key order is the same as the physical order of records in the file is called a:
questions.explanation_en: A clustered index determines the physical arrangement of rows, so a table can have only one. Secondary (non-clustered) indexes point to rows stored in a different order and can be many.

questions.question_en: Which constraint supplies a value for a column automatically when INSERT does not mention that column?
questions.explanation_en: DEFAULT 'Delhi' on a City column stores 'Delhi' when the insert omits City. NOT NULL would instead cause an error if no value and no default exist.

questions.question_en: Which SQL statement is used to insert a new record into a table?
questions.explanation_en: INSERT INTO table_name (col1, col2) VALUES (v1, v2); adds a row. MySQL also allows INSERT ... SELECT to copy rows from another table.

questions.question_en: The join condition in an equi-join uses which comparison operator?
questions.explanation_en: An equi-join compares columns with '='. A join using any other operator (<, >, <>) is a non-equi join or theta join.

questions.question_en: The constraint CHECK (Age >= 18) on table VOTER will:

options.en: Automatically set Age to 18 when it is lower
Reject any insert or update where Age is less than 18
Only warn the user but allow the row
Delete rows whose Age is below 18

questions.explanation_en: A CHECK constraint is a rule evaluated on INSERT/UPDATE; rows that make it false are rejected with an error. It never modifies or deletes data.

questions.question_en: Which event fires when a web page (including its images and other resources) has completely finished loading?
questions.explanation_en: The load event (onload) of window/body fires after the whole page and its resources are loaded. onchange fires when a form control's value changes, and onblur when an element loses focus.

questions.question_en: Which group of tags is used to create a description (definition) list in HTML?
questions.explanation_en: A description list <dl> contains terms <dt> and their descriptions <dd>. <li> items belong only to ordered and unordered lists.
var is function-scoped, so a is visible outside the block. let is block-scoped, so b does not exist outside; typeof on an undeclared name safely returns "undefined" instead of throwing.

questions.question_en: In <label for="email">Email</label>, the value of the for attribute must match which attribute of the related input control?
questions.explanation_en: The for attribute links the label to the control whose id is the same, so clicking the label focuses that control. name is used for submitting data and need not match.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a server-side scripting language?
questions.explanation_en: PHP code runs on the web server and sends generated HTML to the browser. HTML and CSS are markup/styling languages processed by the browser, and XML is a data-description language.

questions.question_en: Which statement correctly distinguishes XML from HTML?

options.en: XML has a fixed set of predefined tags, whereas HTML tags are user-defined
XML is designed to store and transport data with user-defined tags; HTML displays data using predefined tags
XML can only be used inside web browsers
XML is not case-sensitive, whereas HTML is strictly case-sensitive

questions.explanation_en: XML describes what data is, using tags the author defines, and it is case-sensitive. HTML has predefined tags for how content is displayed and is case-insensitive.

questions.question_en: The DOM method document.getElementById("demo") returns:

options.en: An array of all elements with class "demo"
The single element whose id is "demo" (or null if none)
The text typed inside the element

questions.explanation_en: Since ids are meant to be unique, getElementById returns one element object or null. getElementsByClassName and querySelectorAll return collections of elements.

Declarations made with var are hoisted to the top of their scope and initialised to undefined; only the assignment x = 7 stays in place. With let or const, the same code would throw a ReferenceError (temporal dead zone).

questions.question_en: The worst-case time complexity of searching for a key in a binary search tree with n nodes (not necessarily balanced) is:
questions.explanation_en: If keys are inserted in sorted order the BST degenerates into a chain (skewed tree) of height n − 1, so a search may visit every node. O(log n) holds only for balanced trees such as AVL or red-black trees.

questions.question_en: In separate chaining, each slot of the hash table stores:

options.en: A pointer to the next empty slot
A linked list of all keys that hash to that slot
Exactly one key, with collisions sent to the next free slot

questions.explanation_en: Chaining keeps every colliding key in a list attached to its home slot, so the table never 'fills up' and the load factor can exceed 1. Moving to the next free slot describes open addressing.
The outer loop runs n times; for each, the inner loop doubles j and so runs about log₂ n + 1 times. Total ≈ n(log₂ n + 1) = O(n log n).

questions.question_en: For f(n) = 3n² + 5n + 2, which statement is correct?
questions.explanation_en: The highest-order term dominates: for n ≥ 1, 3n² ≤ f(n) ≤ 10n², so f(n) is both O(n²) and Ω(n²), i.e. Θ(n²). It is O(n³) but not Θ(n³) or Ω(n³), and it is not O(n).

questions.question_en: Counting sort on n integers whose values lie in the range 0 to k has time complexity:
questions.explanation_en: Counting sort counts occurrences of each value (O(n)), accumulates the counts over the range (O(k)) and places the elements (O(n)). It is not comparison-based, so the Ω(n log n) bound does not apply, but it needs O(k) extra space.

questions.question_en: The elements of a one-dimensional array are stored in memory:

options.en: At random locations linked by pointers

questions.explanation_en: An array occupies one continuous block of memory, which is what makes index arithmetic possible. Elements linked by pointers describe a linked list.

questions.question_en: Re-running previously passed test cases after a code change, to make sure the change has not broken existing functionality, is called:
questions.explanation_en: Regression testing detects new defects introduced into previously working features. Smoke testing is a quick check that a new build is stable enough for further testing.

questions.question_en: A major drawback of using Lines of Code (LOC) as a size metric is that it:

options.en: Can be counted only after the requirements phase
Depends heavily on the programming language and coding style
Measures only the number of test cases

questions.explanation_en: The same functionality may need very different LOC in assembly and in Python, and programmers' styles differ, so LOC penalises high-level languages. Function points were proposed partly to overcome this language dependence.

questions.question_en: In a use case diagram, a relationship where a base use case ALWAYS incorporates the behaviour of another use case (for example, 'Withdraw Cash' always uses 'Authenticate User') is shown with the stereotype:
questions.explanation_en: «include» denotes mandatory reuse of common behaviour. «extend» is for optional or conditional behaviour that is added to a base use case only under certain conditions.

questions.question_en: Modifying software so that it works on a new operating system or hardware platform is called:
questions.explanation_en: Adaptive maintenance adapts software to changes in its environment. Corrective fixes bugs, perfective adds or improves features, and preventive improves future maintainability.

questions.question_en: UML (Unified Modeling Language) is standardised and maintained by:
questions.explanation_en: UML was created by Booch, Rumbaugh and Jacobson and adopted as a standard by the OMG in 1997; it was later also published as ISO/IEC 19501. W3C standardises web technologies such as HTML.

questions.question_en: Classical conditioning was experimentally demonstrated by:
questions.explanation_en: Ivan Pavlov showed that dogs learnt to salivate at the sound of a bell paired with food (classical conditioning). Skinner is associated with operant conditioning and Kohler with insight learning.

questions.question_en: SWAYAM, the Government of India's MOOC platform, is closely associated with which of the following?

options.en: NPTEL and UGC courses with credit transfer

questions.explanation_en: SWAYAM hosts online courses from NPTEL, UGC, NCERT, IGNOU etc., and UGC regulations allow up to 40% of credits in a programme to be earned through SWAYAM. DIKSHA is the school-level platform; PM e-VIDYA refers to the one-class-one-channel TV initiative.

questions.question_en: A purposeful collection of a student's programs, project reports and reflections gathered over the whole session to show growth is called a:
questions.explanation_en: A portfolio is a systematic collection of student work over time that shows progress and is used in authentic assessment. A blueprint is the design plan of a question paper.

questions.question_en: In an item analysis, 60 students attempted an MCQ and 45 of them answered it correctly. The difficulty index (p) of the item is:
questions.explanation_en: Difficulty index p = number correct / number attempted = 45/60 = 0.75. A p of 0.75 means a fairly easy item; 0.25 would be the proportion who got it wrong.

questions.question_en: A teacher asks: 'Compare the time complexity of bubble sort and merge sort and explain which is better for large inputs.' This question mainly tests which level of Bloom's taxonomy?
questions.explanation_en: Comparing two algorithms, breaking them into parts and relating them is Analysis. Recalling the formula would be Remembering; using an algorithm on a given list would be Applying.

questions.question_en: Which of the following objectives of teaching Computer Science belongs to the affective domain?

options.en: Explaining the difference between RAM and ROM
Typing 40 words per minute without errors
Developing a respect for intellectual property and ethical use of software
Writing an SQL query to retrieve records

questions.explanation_en: Values, attitudes and appreciation (e.g. ethics, respecting copyright) are affective objectives. Typing speed is psychomotor; writing queries and explaining concepts are cognitive.

questions.question_en: Robert Mager's three essential components of a well-written instructional objective are:
questions.explanation_en: Mager (1962) said an objective must state the observable performance, the condition under which it is shown, and the criterion of acceptable performance, e.g. 'Given a flowchart (condition), the student will write the C code (performance) with no syntax errors (criterion)'.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a projected teaching aid?
questions.explanation_en: Projected aids need a projection device and screen (LCD/overhead projector, film strips), while chalkboards, flannel boards and flash cards are non-projected aids.

questions.question_en: According to NEP 2020, by 2030 the minimum degree qualification for school teaching will be:

options.en: A Master's degree in the subject
A one-year B.Ed. after any degree

questions.explanation_en: NEP 2020 (para 5.23) states that by 2030 the minimum qualification for teaching will be a 4-year integrated B.Ed. covering content, pedagogy and practice. Two-year and one-year B.Ed. remain only for graduates and postgraduates respectively.

questions.question_en: Which pair of verbs is correctly matched with the level of the revised Bloom's taxonomy?
questions.explanation_en: 'Summarise', 'explain', 'classify' and 'paraphrase' are Understand-level verbs. 'Design' belongs to Create, 'Recall' to Remember and 'Define' to Remember — so the other three pairs are mismatched.

questions.question_en: Whom did India defeat in the final of the ICC Women's ODI World Cup 2025 to win its first title?
questions.explanation_en: India beat South Africa by 52 runs at DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai on 2 November 2025.

questions.question_en: Who is the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (as of October 2026)?
questions.explanation_en: Sanjay Malhotra took over as the 26th RBI Governor in December 2024 and chairs the MPC.

questions.question_en: The India AI Impact Summit 2026 was organised around three 'Sutras'. These were:
questions.explanation_en: The three foundational pillars of the summit were People, Planet and Progress.

questions.question_en: Who received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award announced in September 2025, India's highest cinema honour?
questions.explanation_en: Malayalam superstar Mohanlal received the award for 2023 at the 71st National Film Awards ceremony.

questions.question_en: Which scheme/mission did Union Budget 2026-27 announce as the next phase of India's chip-making push?
questions.explanation_en: Budget 2026-27 announced India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 to deepen the domestic chip ecosystem.

questions.question_en: In February 2026 the US announced an interim trade deal with India reducing its tariff on Indian goods to:
questions.explanation_en: President Trump announced on 2 February 2026 a cut in US reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods to 18%; Modi confirmed the rate.

questions.question_en: The Jharia coalfield, the largest source of coking coal in India, is in:
questions.explanation_en: Jharia, near Dhanbad, contains the best coking coal needed for steel making.

questions.question_en: The Luni river, which rises in the Aravallis near Ajmer, ends in:
questions.explanation_en: The Luni is an inland drainage river of Rajasthan that disappears in the marshes of the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.

questions.question_en: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added which Schedule listing 29 subjects for Panchayats?
questions.explanation_en: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule; the 74th added the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects) for municipalities.

questions.question_en: Fiscal deficit of the Government is equal to total expenditure minus:
questions.explanation_en: Fiscal deficit shows the government's total borrowing requirement; primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.

questions.question_en: Two resistors of 6 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is:
questions.explanation_en: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 3/6, so R = 2 ohm; series would give 9 ohm.

questions.question_en: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised in the year:
questions.explanation_en: The RBI began on 1 April 1935 as a private shareholders' bank and was nationalised on 1 January 1949; 14 commercial banks were nationalised in 1969.

questions.question_en: The Quit India resolution was passed in August 1942 at which venue in Bombay?
questions.explanation_en: The AICC passed the resolution on 8 August 1942 at Gowalia Tank Maidan (now August Kranti Maidan) and Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die'.

questions.question_en: In 2025, who became the first Indian astronaut to visit the International Space Station, on the Axiom-4 mission?
questions.explanation_en: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew as pilot of Axiom-4 and spent about 18 days on the ISS in June-July 2025.

questions.question_en: The river Yamuna, flowing through Delhi, originates from:
questions.explanation_en: It rises from the Yamunotri glacier on the Bandarpoonch range in Uttarakhand and joins the Ganga at Prayagraj.

questions.question_en: World Environment Day is observed every year on:
questions.explanation_en: Started by the UN in 1974 following the Stockholm Conference of 1972; Earth Day is on 22 April.

questions.question_en: International Literacy Day is observed on:
questions.explanation_en: UNESCO proclaimed it in 1965; first celebrated in 1966. 24 January is National Girl Child Day.

questions.question_en: Who was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation_en: Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for Gitanjali; Raman was the first Indian to win in a science field (1930).

questions.question_en: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the share of a bank's deposits that must be kept:

options.en: As gold in its own vaults
In government securities with the bank

questions.explanation_en: CRR is held with the RBI and earns no interest; SLR is held by banks themselves in liquid assets such as G-secs and gold.

questions.question_en: The chemical name of baking soda is:
questions.explanation_en: Baking soda is NaHCO3; washing soda is Na2CO3.10H2O.

questions.question_en: Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship among Doctors, Surgeons and Teachers?

options.en: Surgeons lie wholly inside Doctors; Teachers form a separate circle outside both
Three circles overlapping at a common region
Doctors lie inside Surgeons, and Teachers lie inside Doctors

questions.explanation_en: Every surgeon is a doctor, so Surgeons is a subset of Doctors. A teacher is a different profession, so Teachers is a separate set.

questions.question_en: Complete the series: ACE, FHJ, KMO, ?
questions.explanation_en: Each letter in a group moves 5 places ahead of the same position in the previous group: K+5 = P, M+5 = R, O+5 = T.

questions.question_en: A is taller than B, B is taller than C, D is taller than A, and E is shorter than C. Who is the second tallest?
questions.explanation_en: The order is D > A > B > C > E. D is the tallest, so A is second tallest.

questions.question_en: Find the next term: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ?
questions.explanation_en: These are squares of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Next is 7^2 = 49.
7 x 8 = 56, i.e. n x (n + 1). So 9 x 10 = 90. The option 72 comes from wrongly using 9 x 8.

questions.question_en: Sunita is facing north-west. She turns 90 degrees clockwise and then 180 degrees anticlockwise. In which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation_en: North-west turned 90 degrees clockwise is north-east. Turning 180 degrees from north-east gives the opposite direction, south-west.

questions.question_en: If the numbers 3 and 5 are interchanged and the signs + and × are interchanged, then the value of 3 + 5 × 4 is:
questions.explanation_en: Interchanging 3 and 5 gives 5 + 3 × 4; interchanging the signs gives 5 × 3 + 4. So 15 + 4 = 19.

questions.question_en: If the letters of the word DELHI are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter will be in the middle?
questions.explanation_en: Alphabetical order: D, E, H, I, L. The middle (third) letter is H.

questions.question_en: P is heavier than Q but lighter than R. S is heavier than R. T is lighter than Q. Who is the second heaviest?
questions.explanation_en: Order from heaviest: S > R > P > Q > T. So R is second heaviest.

questions.question_en: Sculptor : Statue :: Poet : ?
questions.explanation_en: A sculptor creates a statue; a poet creates a poem (creator : creation).

questions.question_en: Find the next term: 100, 91, 83, 76, 70, ?
questions.explanation_en: Differences are -9, -8, -7, -6, so the next is -5: 70 - 5 = 65.

questions.question_en: Find the next letter: B, E, H, K, N, ?
questions.explanation_en: Each letter moves 3 steps ahead; N + 3 = Q.

questions.question_en: ACE : FHJ :: BDF : ?
questions.explanation_en: Each letter is shifted 5 places ahead (A-F, C-H, E-J). B-G, D-I, F-K gives GIK.

questions.question_en: Pointing to a lady, Anil said, 'She is the wife of my mother's only brother.' How is the lady related to Anil?
questions.explanation_en: Anil's mother's only brother is his maternal uncle (Mama). The uncle's wife is Anil's Mami, i.e. maternal aunt.

questions.question_en: Kiran ranks 15th from the top and 25th from the bottom in a class. Divya ranks 7 places above Kiran. What is Divya's rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation_en: Total = 15 + 25 - 1 = 39. Divya's rank from top = 15 - 7 = 8. From the bottom = 39 - 8 + 1 = 32.

questions.question_en: A square sheet is folded along one diagonal to form a triangle, and this triangle is folded in half again to form a smaller triangle. A single hole is punched through it. How many holes are seen on unfolding?
questions.explanation_en: Each fold doubles the layers: 2 folds → 4 layers, so one punch gives 4 holes, placed symmetrically about both diagonals.

questions.question_en: A long strip of paper is folded in half, then folded in half again, and then once more, always in the same direction. When it is opened out flat, how many crease lines will it show?
questions.explanation_en: Three folds divide the strip into 2³ = 8 equal sections. 8 sections are separated by 8 − 1 = 7 creases.

questions.question_en: A square sheet is folded top-half onto bottom-half, and then right-half onto left-half, giving a smaller square. A quarter-circle is cut from the corner of this small square where the two fold lines meet. What will the sheet look like when unfolded?

options.en: Four small circular holes near the centre
Two semicircular notches on opposite edges
Four quarter-circle notches at the corners
One circular hole at the centre of the sheet

questions.explanation_en: The corner where both folds meet is the centre of the original sheet. The four quarter-circles (one in each layer) meet at that point and form a single circle, giving one circular hole at the centre.

questions.question_en: A rectangular sheet is folded in half. A semicircle is cut out from the middle of the folded edge (the curved side pointing away from the fold). What will the sheet look like when unfolded?

options.en: Two circular holes side by side
One circular hole in the middle of the sheet
One semicircular notch on the outer edge
Two semicircular holes at the outer edges

questions.explanation_en: The cut is made on the fold line, so its mirror image joins it across the fold: two halves of a circle meet to form one complete circular hole in the middle.

questions.question_en: The corners of a square carry letters: top-left A, top-right B, bottom-right C, bottom-left D. In every step, each letter moves one corner clockwise. After 3 steps, which letter is at the top-left corner?
questions.explanation_en: Moving clockwise, the top-left corner receives the letter from bottom-left each step: after step 1 it has D, after step 2 C, after step 3 B.

questions.question_en: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they complete a work in 14 days. In how many days can B alone complete it?
questions.explanation_en: Let B's rate be b, so A's is 2b. 3b = 1/14, so b = 1/42. B alone takes 42 days.

questions.question_en: In what ratio should water be mixed with milk costing ₹12 per litre so that the mixture is worth ₹8 per litre?
questions.explanation_en: Water costs 0. Alligation: water : milk = (12 − 8) : (8 − 0) = 4 : 8 = 1 : 2.

questions.question_en: The population of a town is 25,000. If it increases by 10% every year, what will it be after 2 years?
questions.explanation_en: Population = 25000 × (1.1)² = 25000 × 1.21 = 30,250. (30,000 is what simple growth would give; 27,500 is only one year's growth.)

questions.question_en: What is the smallest number which, when divided by 8, 12 and 15, leaves a remainder of 5 in each case?
questions.explanation_en: LCM of 8, 12, 15 = 120. The required number = 120 + 5 = 125.

questions.question_en: The average of 7 consecutive integers is 20. What is the largest of them?
questions.explanation_en: For consecutive integers the average is the middle (4th) number, 20. The largest is 3 more: 23.

questions.question_en: ₹810 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/6. What is A's share?
questions.explanation_en: Multiply by 6: 3 : 2 : 1 (sum 6). A's share = 3/6 × 810 = ₹405.

questions.question_en: A boat covers 18 km downstream in 2 hours and 12 km upstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation_en: Downstream = 9 km/h, upstream = 6 km/h. Stream = (9 − 6)/2 = 1.5 km/h (still-water speed = 7.5 km/h).

questions.question_en: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their expenditures are in the ratio 3 : 2. If each saves ₹1,600, what is A's income?
questions.explanation_en: Let incomes be 5x, 4x and expenses 3y, 2y. 5x − 3y = 1600 and 4x − 2y = 1600. From the second, y = 2x − 800. Substituting: 5x − 6x + 2400 = 1600, so x = 800. A's income = 5 × 800 = ₹4,000 (B's income is ₹3,200).

questions.question_en: The ages of two persons are in the ratio 4 : 5 and their sum is 45 years. What is the age of the elder?
questions.explanation_en: Parts = 9, one part = 45/9 = 5 years. Elder = 5 × 5 = 25 years.

questions.question_en: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?
questions.explanation_en: Test: (sum of digits at odd places) − (sum at even places) should be 0 or a multiple of 11. For 3685: (3 + 8) − (6 + 5) = 0, so it is divisible (3685 = 11 × 335). The others give differences of 6 (4372), 10 (5281) and 7 (6153), so they are not divisible.

questions.question_en: If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, then A : B : C is:
questions.explanation_en: Make B equal: multiply the first ratio by 4 and the second by 3. A : B = 8 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 15, so A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15.

questions.question_en: What is the value of (25² − 15²) ÷ 40?
Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5. If 10 is added to each, the ratio becomes 5 : 7. What is the smaller number?
questions.explanation_en: Let the numbers be 3x and 5x. (3x + 10)/(5x + 10) = 5/7 gives 21x + 70 = 25x + 50, so x = 5. Smaller number = 15 (the numbers are 15 and 25).

questions.question_en: The cost price of 12 articles is equal to the selling price of 10 articles. What is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation_en: 12 CP = 10 SP, so SP/CP = 12/10 = 1.2. Profit = 20%.

questions.question_en: The value of cos 0° + sin 90° + tan 45° is:
questions.explanation_en: cos 0° = 1, sin 90° = 1 and tan 45° = 1, so the sum is 3.

questions.question_en:
The table shows the production (in thousand units) of three items by a company.
Year | Laptops | Tablets | Printers
2020 | 40 | 25 | 15
2021 | 45 | 30 | 20
2022 | 50 | 35 | 18
2023 | 60 | 32 | 24
2024 | 55 | 40 | 30
By approximately what percent did the total production of the three items increase from 2021 to 2024?
A cuboid of dimensions 12 cm × 8 cm × 6 cm is melted and recast into cubes of side 2 cm. How many cubes are obtained?
questions.explanation_en: Cuboid volume = 12 × 8 × 6 = 576 cm³. Each cube = 2³ = 8 cm³. Number of cubes = 576 / 8 = 72.

questions.question_en: If sec θ + tan θ = 4, then sec θ − tan θ equals:
questions.explanation_en: sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, i.e. (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1. So sec θ − tan θ = 1/4.

questions.question_en: In a triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, the length of the median drawn to the longest side is:
questions.explanation_en: 6² + 8² = 100 = 10², so the triangle is right-angled with hypotenuse 10 cm. The median to the hypotenuse equals half of it (the midpoint is the circumcentre): 5 cm.

questions.question_en: 'आस्तिक' का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'आस्तिक' का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: Aastik (theist) vs nastik (atheist).
questions.explanation_hi: आस्तिक (ईश्वर को मानने वाला) का विलोम नास्तिक (ईश्वर को न मानने वाला) है।

questions.question_en: 'मेघ आए बड़े बन-ठन के सँवर के' — इस पंक्ति में मुख्य रूप से कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.question_hi: 'मेघ आए बड़े बन-ठन के सँवर के' — इस पंक्ति में मुख्य रूप से कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation_en: Clouds are shown dressing up like a person, so it is personification (Manvikaran).
questions.explanation_hi: यहाँ बादलों (प्रकृति) को मनुष्य की तरह सज-धजकर आते हुए दिखाया गया है। प्राकृतिक वस्तु पर मानवीय भावों और क्रियाओं का आरोप मानवीकरण अलंकार है।

questions.question_en: 'अनुलोम' का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'अनुलोम' का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: Anulom (in order) vs pratilom (reverse order).
questions.explanation_hi: अनुलोम (क्रम के अनुसार) का विलोम प्रतिलोम (उल्टे क्रम में) है; जैसे अनुलोम-प्रतिलोम प्राणायाम। 'विलोम' सामान्य शब्द है, पर 'अनुलोम' का मानक जोड़ा 'प्रतिलोम' है।

questions.question_en: 'पीपर पात सरिस मन डोला' — इस पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.question_hi: 'पीपर पात सरिस मन डोला' — इस पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation_en: The mind is compared to a peepal leaf using the comparison word 'saris', so it is Upama (simile).
questions.explanation_hi: मन (उपमेय) की तुलना पीपल के पत्ते (उपमान) से 'सरिस' (समान) वाचक शब्द द्वारा की गई है, अतः उपमा अलंकार है। रूपक में वाचक शब्द नहीं होता और अभेद दिखाया जाता है।

questions.question_en: 'सूर्य' का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.question_hi: 'सूर्य' का पर्यायवाची शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation_en: Dinkar means sun; the other options are names of the moon.
questions.explanation_hi: दिनकर (दिन को बनाने वाला) सूर्य का पर्यायवाची है। निशाकर, रजनीश और सुधाकर तीनों चंद्रमा के पर्यायवाची हैं।

questions.question_en: 'कवि' शब्द का शुद्ध स्त्रीलिंग रूप क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'कवि' शब्द का शुद्ध स्त्रीलिंग रूप क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: The correct feminine of kavi is kavayitri.
questions.explanation_hi: 'कवि' का स्त्रीलिंग 'कवयित्री' है। 'कवियित्री' लिखना प्रचलित भूल है, और 'कविता' रचना का नाम है, स्त्रीलिंग रूप नहीं।

questions.subtopic: अनेक शब्दों के लिए एक शब्द
questions.question_en: 'जिसकी आशा न की गई हो' — इसके लिए एक शब्द चुनिए।
questions.question_hi: 'जिसकी आशा न की गई हो' — इसके लिए एक शब्द चुनिए।
questions.explanation_en: Unexpected = apratyashit.
questions.explanation_hi: जिसकी आशा न की गई हो = अप्रत्याशित। 'आशातीत' = आशा से अधिक; 'अनपेक्षित' = जिसकी अपेक्षा न हो, निकट है पर मानक उत्तर 'अप्रत्याशित' है।

questions.question_en: 'माला' शब्द का बहुवचन (बिना विभक्ति) रूप क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'माला' शब्द का बहुवचन (बिना विभक्ति) रूप क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: Mala becomes maalaayen in the direct plural.
questions.explanation_hi: आकारांत स्त्रीलिंग शब्दों में 'एँ' जोड़कर बहुवचन बनता है — माला → मालाएँ। 'मालाओं' विभक्ति लगने पर बनने वाला रूप है।

questions.question_en: 'बड़ों द्वारा दी गई शुभकामना' अर्थ वाले शब्द की शुद्ध वर्तनी चुनिए।
questions.question_hi: 'बड़ों द्वारा दी गई शुभकामना' अर्थ वाले शब्द की शुद्ध वर्तनी चुनिए।
questions.explanation_en: Correct spelling is aashirvaad with the r-sign above 'va'.
questions.explanation_hi: शुद्ध रूप 'आशीर्वाद' है (आशीः + वाद)। रेफ़ (र्) 'व' के ऊपर लगता है, इसलिए 'आर्शीवाद' अशुद्ध है।

questions.question_en: 'लिखावट' शब्द में कौन-सा प्रत्यय है?
questions.question_hi: 'लिखावट' शब्द में कौन-सा प्रत्यय है?
questions.explanation_en: Likhavat = likh + aavat; 'aavat' forms abstract nouns from verbs.
questions.explanation_hi: लिखावट = लिख + आवट। 'आवट' कृत् प्रत्यय है जो क्रिया से भाववाचक संज्ञा बनाता है, जैसे सजावट, बनावट, रुकावट।

questions.question_en: 'वह कलम से पत्र लिखता है।' — इस वाक्य में 'कलम से' में कौन-सा कारक है?
questions.question_hi: 'वह कलम से पत्र लिखता है।' — इस वाक्य में 'कलम से' में कौन-सा कारक है?
questions.explanation_en: The pen is the instrument, so 'se' here is karan (instrumental) case.
questions.explanation_hi: कलम क्रिया (लिखना) का साधन है; साधन बताने वाला 'से' करण कारक का चिह्न है। अलग होने के अर्थ में आने वाला 'से' अपादान कारक का होता है।

questions.question_en:
निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

परिश्रम ही सफलता की कुंजी है। इतिहास साक्षी है कि जिन लोगों ने कठिन परिश्रम किया, वे साधनों के अभाव में भी ऊँचाइयों तक पहुँचे। भाग्य के भरोसे बैठे रहने वाला व्यक्ति अवसर आने पर भी उसका लाभ नहीं उठा पाता। परिश्रमी व्यक्ति असफलता से निराश नहीं होता; वह अपनी भूलों से सीखकर फिर प्रयास करता है। आलस्य मनुष्य का सबसे बड़ा शत्रु है, जो उसकी प्रतिभा को धीरे-धीरे नष्ट कर देता है।

प्रश्न: गद्यांश के अनुसार परिश्रमी व्यक्ति असफल होने पर क्या करता है?
questions.question_hi:
निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।
