प्रश्न: गद्यांश के अनुसार परिश्रमी व्यक्ति असफल होने पर क्या करता है?

options.en: अपनी भूलों से सीखकर फिर प्रयास करता है
options.hi: अपनी भूलों से सीखकर फिर प्रयास करता है

questions.explanation_en: He learns from mistakes and tries again.
questions.explanation_hi: गद्यांश कहता है कि परिश्रमी व्यक्ति असफलता से निराश नहीं होता, बल्कि 'अपनी भूलों से सीखकर फिर प्रयास करता है।'

questions.subtopic: अनेक शब्दों के लिए एक शब्द
questions.question_en: 'दूसरों के दोष खोजने वाला' — इसके लिए एक शब्द चुनिए।
questions.question_hi: 'दूसरों के दोष खोजने वाला' — इसके लिए एक शब्द चुनिए।
questions.explanation_en: One who looks for faults in others = chhidranveshi.
questions.explanation_hi: छिद्र (दोष) + अन्वेषी (खोजने वाला) = छिद्रान्वेषी। आलोचक गुण-दोष दोनों देखता है; निंदक बुराई करता है; मानक उत्तर 'छिद्रान्वेषी' है।

questions.question_en: 'चंद्रमुख' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.question_hi: 'चंद्रमुख' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation_en: Moon-like face: upaman–upamey relation — karmadharaya.
questions.explanation_hi: चंद्रमुख = चंद्र के समान मुख। यहाँ उपमान (चंद्र) और उपमेय (मुख) का संबंध है, जो कर्मधारय समास का एक भेद है। यदि अर्थ 'चंद्र-जैसा मुख है जिसका' लिया जाए तो बहुव्रीहि होता, पर सामान्य विग्रह कर्मधारय का ही है।

questions.question_en: 'सुयोग' शब्द में उपसर्ग अलग कीजिए।
questions.question_hi: 'सुयोग' शब्द में उपसर्ग अलग कीजिए।
questions.explanation_en: Suyog = su + yog; 'su' means good.
questions.explanation_hi: सुयोग = सु + योग। 'सु' उपसर्ग का अर्थ 'अच्छा' है, जैसे सुपुत्र, सुगम, सुलभ।

questions.question_en:
निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

एक अच्छा शिक्षक केवल पाठ्यपुस्तक का ज्ञान नहीं देता, बल्कि विद्यार्थियों में सोचने की क्षमता जगाता है। वह प्रश्न पूछने को प्रोत्साहित करता है और गलती को सीखने का अवसर मानता है। कक्षा में भय का वातावरण होने पर विद्यार्थी अपनी शंकाएँ व्यक्त नहीं कर पाते, इसलिए शिक्षक को मित्रवत् व्यवहार करना चाहिए। राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति 2020 भी रटने के स्थान पर समझ पर आधारित शिक्षा पर बल देती है। वास्तव में शिक्षक वह दीपक है जो स्वयं जलकर दूसरों का मार्ग आलोकित करता है।

प्रश्न: 'शिक्षक वह दीपक है जो स्वयं जलकर दूसरों का मार्ग आलोकित करता है' — इस वाक्य में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.question_hi:
निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

एक अच्छा शिक्षक केवल पाठ्यपुस्तक का ज्ञान नहीं देता, बल्कि विद्यार्थियों में सोचने की क्षमता जगाता है। वह प्रश्न पूछने को प्रोत्साहित करता है और गलती को सीखने का अवसर मानता है। कक्षा में भय का वातावरण होने पर विद्यार्थी अपनी शंकाएँ व्यक्त नहीं कर पाते, इसलिए शिक्षक को मित्रवत् व्यवहार करना चाहिए। राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति 2020 भी रटने के स्थान पर समझ पर आधारित शिक्षा पर बल देती है। वास्तव में शिक्षक वह दीपक है जो स्वयं जलकर दूसरों का मार्ग आलोकित करता है।

प्रश्न: 'शिक्षक वह दीपक है जो स्वयं जलकर दूसरों का मार्ग आलोकित करता है' — इस वाक्य में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation_en: The teacher is directly called a lamp, so it is Rupak (metaphor).
questions.explanation_hi: यहाँ शिक्षक (उपमेय) को सीधे दीपक (उपमान) कह दिया गया है, बिना किसी वाचक शब्द के; उपमेय पर उपमान का अभेद आरोप रूपक अलंकार है।

questions.question_en: 'बहुत अधिक' अर्थ वाले शब्द की शुद्ध वर्तनी कौन-सी है?
questions.question_hi: 'बहुत अधिक' अर्थ वाले शब्द की शुद्ध वर्तनी कौन-सी है?
questions.explanation_en: Ati + adhik = atyadhik (yan sandhi), not atyaadhik.
questions.explanation_hi: अति + अधिक = अत्यधिक (यण संधि)। 'इ' का 'य्' हो जाता है और 'अ' ज्यों-का-त्यों रहता है, इसलिए 'अत्याधिक' अशुद्ध है।

questions.question_en: 'पृथ्वी' का पर्यायवाची शब्द चुनिए।
questions.question_hi: 'पृथ्वी' का पर्यायवाची शब्द चुनिए।
questions.explanation_en: Vasundhara means earth; varid is cloud, vyom is sky, vipin is forest.
questions.explanation_hi: वसुंधरा (वसु = धन, धरा = धारण करने वाली) पृथ्वी का पर्यायवाची है। वारिद = बादल, व्योम = आकाश, विपिन = वन।

questions.question_en: 'नीलकमल' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.question_hi: 'नीलकमल' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation_en: Adjective + noun relation (blue lotus) — karmadharaya.
questions.explanation_hi: नीलकमल = नीला है जो कमल। यहाँ विशेषण (नील) और विशेष्य (कमल) का संबंध है, अतः कर्मधारय समास है।

questions.question_en: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य चुनिए: (रहस्य)
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य चुनिए: (रहस्य)
questions.explanation_en: A secret is already confidential; rahasya is masculine, so 'bataya'.
questions.explanation_hi: 'रहस्य' स्वयं गोपनीय बात है, इसलिए 'गोपनीय रहस्य' पुनरुक्ति है। 'रहस्य' पुल्लिंग है, अतः क्रिया 'बताया' होगी, 'बताई' नहीं।

questions.question_en: Select the word closest in meaning to ABATE.
questions.explanation_en: To abate is to become less intense, e.g. the storm abated; subside is closest.

questions.question_en: Change the voice: ‘Do it at once.’

options.en: Let it be done at once.

questions.explanation_en: Imperative sentences become passive with ‘Let + object + be + V3’.

questions.question_en:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Sleep is often treated as a luxury by students and working adults, yet scientists consider it as essential as food and water. During sleep the brain does not simply switch off; it sorts the information gathered during the day, stores important memories and clears away harmful chemicals that accumulate while we are awake. Children who sleep for less than eight hours are more likely to have difficulty in concentrating and to show poor results in examinations. Adults who regularly sleep for only five or six hours face a higher risk of heart disease and depression. Experts therefore advise a fixed bedtime, avoiding screens an hour before sleeping and keeping the bedroom dark and quiet. Contrary to popular belief, sleeping late on weekends cannot fully repay the “sleep debt” collected during the week.

Which of the following is NOT mentioned as something the brain does during sleep?

options.en: Sorts information gathered in the day

questions.explanation_en: The passage lists sorting information, storing memories and clearing chemicals. Bone strength is never mentioned.

questions.question_en:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Reading is a habit that (1) ______ the mind and improves imagination. A student who reads regularly (2) ______ better vocabulary and writing skills than one who does not. Unfortunately, the (3) ______ of mobile phones has reduced the time young people (4) ______ on books. Teachers should (5) ______ students to visit libraries and discuss what they read.

Select the most appropriate option to fill blank (2).
Relevant sentence: A student who reads regularly (2) ______ better vocabulary and writing skills than one who does not.
questions.explanation_en: A regular reader develops better vocabulary; the other options are illogical.

questions.question_en:
Identify the segment that contains an error.
The furniture in the new office / are made / of teak wood / and looks elegant.

options.en: The furniture in the new office

questions.explanation_en: “Furniture” is an uncountable, singular noun, so the verb should be “is made”.

questions.question_en: Select the word opposite in meaning to MAGNANIMOUS.
questions.explanation_en: Magnanimous means generous and forgiving; petty means small-minded and mean.

questions.question_en:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Water is (1) ______ for all living beings. However, in recent years many cities have been (2) ______ from acute water shortage. The main reason is the (3) ______ use of groundwater by industries and households. If we do not take steps to (4) ______ water, future generations will have to pay a heavy price. Every citizen should therefore (5) ______ responsibility and avoid wastage.

Select the most appropriate option to fill blank (4).
Relevant sentence: If we do not take steps to (4) ______ water, future generations will have to pay a heavy price.
questions.explanation_en: The sentence calls for steps to save water, so “conserve” fits.

questions.question_en: What ______ pity that he failed again!
questions.explanation_en: In exclamations with a singular countable noun, “What a/an + noun” is used: What a pity!

questions.question_en: Change into indirect speech: He said to her, “Please help me.”

options.en: He ordered her to help him.
He asked that she helps him.
He requested her to help him.
He said her to help me.

questions.explanation_en: A polite request with ‘please’ is reported with ‘requested’ + to-infinitive.

questions.question_en: Select the meaning of the idiom: ‘Swan song’.

options.en: A final performance or act before retirement

questions.explanation_en: A swan song is the last work or appearance of a person before retirement or death.

questions.question_en:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Trees in cities do much more than make streets look pleasant. A single mature tree can absorb about twenty kilograms of carbon dioxide in a year and release enough oxygen for two people. Their leaves trap dust, while their shade can lower the temperature of a neighbourhood by several degrees, reducing the need for air conditioners. In many Indian cities, however, trees are felled for widening roads and constructing flyovers, often without any plan to replace them. Urban planners argue that development and greenery are not enemies; roads can be designed around existing trees, and every felled tree can be compensated by planting several saplings. Citizens, too, must take the initiative by protecting trees in their own colony instead of waiting for the government to act.

The word ‘felled’ in the passage means:
questions.explanation_en: To fell a tree is to cut it down.

questions.question_en: Choose the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation_en: “Receive” follows the rule ‘i before e except after c’, so ‘Recieve’ is wrong.

questions.question_en: Select the word closest in meaning to OBSOLETE.
questions.explanation_en: Obsolete describes something no longer in use or out of date.

questions.question_en:
Select the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. If no change is needed, select ‘No improvement’.
I [am living] in Jaipur since my childhood.
questions.explanation_en: “Since + point of time” with an action continuing now needs the present perfect continuous: have been living.

questions.question_en: The old man was accused ______ theft.
questions.explanation_en: “Accuse” is followed by “of”: accused of theft.

questions.question_en:
Select the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. If no change is needed, select ‘No improvement’.
I would have helped you [if you would have asked].
questions.explanation_en: In the third conditional, the if-clause uses the past perfect (if + had + V3) and the main clause uses would have + V3.

questions.question_en: Look! The children ______ in the garden.
questions.explanation_en: “Look!” signals an action happening at this moment, so the present continuous is required.

questions.question_en: I prefer tea ______ coffee.
questions.explanation_en: “Prefer” is always followed by “to”, never “than”.

questions.question_en: Change the voice: ‘The students completed the project.’

options.en: The students were completed by the project.
The project has been completed by the students.
The project was completed by the students.
The project is completed by the students.

questions.explanation_en: Simple past: object + was/were + V3 + by + agent.

questions.question_en:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Trees in cities do much more than make streets look pleasant. A single mature tree can absorb about twenty kilograms of carbon dioxide in a year and release enough oxygen for two people. Their leaves trap dust, while their shade can lower the temperature of a neighbourhood by several degrees, reducing the need for air conditioners. In many Indian cities, however, trees are felled for widening roads and constructing flyovers, often without any plan to replace them. Urban planners argue that development and greenery are not enemies; roads can be designed around existing trees, and every felled tree can be compensated by planting several saplings. Citizens, too, must take the initiative by protecting trees in their own colony instead of waiting for the government to act.

Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.en: Citizens are not interested in trees.
One tree supplies oxygen for a whole colony.
Many Indian cities cut trees without a replacement plan.

questions.explanation_en: The phrase “often without any plan to replace them” supports this inference; the other options exaggerate or contradict the text.

questions.question_en: What is the output of a three-input XOR gate when all three inputs are 1?
questions.explanation_en: A multi-input XOR outputs 1 when an odd number of inputs are 1 (it is an odd-parity function). Three 1s is odd, so the output is 1. Students often wrongly treat XOR as 'exactly one input is 1', which would give 0.

questions.question_en: The 2's complement of the 8-bit number 00101100 is:
questions.explanation_en: Invert all bits: 11010011 (the 1's complement), then add 1: 11010100. Check: 00101100 = 44 and 11010100 = 212 = 256 − 44.

questions.question_en: In a 4-to-1 multiplexer with data inputs I0–I3 and select lines S1 S0, which input reaches the output when S1 S0 = 10?
questions.question_hi: डेटा इनपुट I0–I3 और सेलेक्ट लाइन S1 S0 वाले 4-से-1 मल्टीप्लेक्सर में S1 S0 = 10 होने पर कौन-सा इनपुट आउटपुट पर जाता है?
questions.explanation_en: The select lines form the binary index of the chosen input: S1 S0 = 10 = 2, so I2 is routed to the output.

questions.question_en: Which of the following numbers has the largest value?
questions.explanation_en: The same digits are worth more in a bigger base: (100)2 = 4, (100)8 = 64, (100)10 = 100 and (100)16 = 256.

questions.question_en: What is the 1's complement of the 5-bit binary number 01101?
questions.explanation_en: The 1's complement simply inverts every bit: 01101 → 10010. Adding 1 to that (10011, option 2) would give the 2's complement.

questions.question_en: What is the product of the binary numbers 1101 and 101?
The function F(A, B, C) = Σm(1, 3, 5, 7) simplifies, using a K-map, to:
questions.explanation_en: Minterms 1, 3, 5 and 7 are 001, 011, 101 and 111: every combination of A and B with C = 1. On the map they form one group of four cells that eliminates A and B, leaving F = C.

questions.question_en: Which pair of gates is known as the universal gates?
questions.question_hi: गेटों के किस युग्म को यूनिवर्सल गेट कहा जाता है?
questions.explanation_en: Any Boolean function can be realised using only NAND gates, or only NOR gates, so each is called universal. AND, OR and NOT individually cannot build every function (for example, AND and OR alone cannot produce an inverter).

questions.question_en: In an SR latch built from NOR gates, which input combination is invalid (forbidden)?
questions.question_hi: NOR गेट से बने SR लैच में कौन-सा इनपुट संयोजन अमान्य (वर्जित) है?
questions.explanation_en: S = R = 1 forces both Q and Q' to 0, violating Q' being the complement of Q, and the next state is unpredictable when the inputs return to 0. S = R = 0 is simply the hold (no change) state.

questions.question_en: Cache memory is placed between which two components to reduce the average time to access data?
questions.explanation_en: Cache is a small, fast SRAM buffer between the processor and the slower main memory; frequently used instructions and data are kept there so the CPU does not wait on RAM.

questions.question_en: The decimal number 45 in binary is:
questions.explanation_en: Repeated division by 2 gives remainders 1,0,1,1,0,1 (read bottom-up: 101101). Check: 32 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 45. Option 2 (110101) equals 53.

questions.question_en: Which unit of the CPU fetches instructions from memory, decodes them and directs the other units to carry them out, without itself doing any arithmetic?
questions.explanation_en: The Control Unit sequences the fetch–decode–execute cycle and sends control signals to the ALU, registers and memory. The ALU performs the actual arithmetic and logic; the accumulator and MDR are registers that hold data.

questions.question_en: A company filing its GST returns on the government's online portal is an example of which e-governance interaction model?
questions.explanation_en: Interactions between government and businesses, such as tax filing, licensing and e-procurement, are G2B. A citizen applying for a birth certificate online would be G2C.

questions.question_en: What does the Excel formula =MID("COMPUTER",4,3) return?
questions.explanation_en: MID(text, start, count) extracts count characters starting at position start. Starting at the 4th letter (P) and taking 3 characters gives PUT.

questions.question_en: Self-executing programs stored on a blockchain such as Ethereum, which automatically carry out the terms of an agreement when preset conditions are met, are called:
questions.explanation_en: Smart contracts run on the blockchain and execute automatically, e.g. releasing payment when delivery is confirmed. The genesis block is simply the first block of a chain.

questions.question_en: During a PowerPoint slide show, pressing the B key:

options.en: Opens the slide in Backstage view
Turns the screen black until a key is pressed
Jumps back to the first slide

questions.explanation_en: B (or the full stop) blacks out the screen and W (or comma) turns it white, letting the presenter draw attention away from the slides. Pressing the key again resumes the show.

questions.question_en: The primary purpose of the Information Technology Act, 2000 was to:

options.en: Make computer education compulsory in schools
Give legal recognition to electronic records, digital signatures and e-commerce
Fix the prices of computers sold in India

questions.explanation_en: The Act provides legal recognition for transactions carried out by electronic data interchange and electronic records, authenticates them with digital signatures, and defines cyber offences.

questions.question_en: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), which acts as the national agency for responding to cyber-security incidents, derives its statutory role from which section of the IT Act?
questions.explanation_en: Section 70B designates CERT-In (under MeitY) as the national agency for incident response. Section 70A relates to the nodal agency for critical information infrastructure (NCIIPC) and Section 69 to interception and decryption.

questions.question_en: Big data is commonly characterised by the '3 Vs'. These are:
questions.explanation_en: Doug Laney's 3 Vs are Volume (huge size), Velocity (speed of generation) and Variety (many formats). Veracity and Value are often added as the 4th and 5th Vs.

questions.question_en: The ability of a cloud system to automatically add resources when demand rises and release them when demand falls is called:
questions.explanation_en: Rapid elasticity (a NIST essential characteristic) lets capacity scale out and in quickly, appearing unlimited to the user. Resource pooling refers to serving many customers from shared physical resources.

questions.question_en: A programmer deliberately alters the source code of a company's billing software that is required to be maintained by law. This is an offence under which section of the IT Act?

options.en: Section 65 – tampering with computer source documents

questions.explanation_en: Section 65 punishes knowingly concealing, destroying or altering computer source code, with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to ₹2 lakh or both.

questions.question_en: Malware that encrypts the victim's files and demands payment, often in cryptocurrency, to restore access is called:
questions.explanation_en: Ransomware (e.g. WannaCry, 2017) locks or encrypts data and demands a ransom for the decryption key. Adware shows unwanted ads and spyware secretly collects information.

options.en: AttributeError: Robot is not a Duck

questions.explanation_en: Python uses duck typing: any object that has a speak() method can be used in the loop, even without a common base class. len() is itself polymorphic and works on both a string (3) and a list (2).
& is intersection {3, 4}; A - B keeps elements of A not in B, {1, 2}; | is union {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} whose size is 5. The symmetric difference would be A ^ B = {1, 2, 5}.
C has no boolean keywords in printf output; relational operators yield int 1 for true and 0 for false. x == 5 is 1 and x != 5 is 0.

questions.question_en: In Python, which function is used to write (serialise) an object such as a dictionary into a binary file opened in 'wb' mode?
questions.explanation_en: pickle.dump(obj, file) serialises a Python object into a binary file and pickle.load(file) reads it back. csv.writer() writes text rows, and json.loads() parses a JSON string rather than writing a file.
check(20) returns ok, which is printed. check(15) executes raise, so the second print never runs and control jumps to except, where printing the exception object shows its message, minor.
Post-increment a++ supplies the old value 10 to the multiplication, so b = 20; afterwards a becomes 11.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a valid identifier in C?
questions.explanation_en: An identifier must begin with a letter or underscore, never a digit. 2sum starts with a digit and is rejected by the compiler.

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

with open("t.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("abc\n")
    f.write("de")
with open("t.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("XY")
with open("t.txt") as f:
    print(len(f.read()))
questions.explanation_en: Opening an existing file in 'w' mode truncates it to zero length, so the earlier 6 characters (abc, newline, de) are lost. Only XY remains and read() returns a 2-character string. Mode 'a' would have kept the old data.
continue skips the rest of the current iteration only. When i is 3 nothing is printed, and the loop goes on with i = 4, so the digits 0, 1, 2 and 4 appear.

questions.question_en:
What is the result of running the following Python code?

t = (1, [2, 3], 4)
t[1].append(5)
print(t)

options.en: TypeError: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment

questions.explanation_en: A tuple is immutable: it cannot be made to refer to different objects. But t[1] is a mutable list, and append modifies that list in place without reassigning any tuple element, so no error occurs.

questions.question_en: In C++, a pure virtual function is declared as:
questions.explanation_en: Writing = 0 after a virtual function declaration makes it pure virtual. A class with at least one pure virtual function becomes abstract and cannot be instantiated. C++ has no 'abstract' or 'pure' keyword.
Dereferencing a NULL pointer writes to an invalid address. The code compiles, but at run time it causes undefined behaviour, typically a segmentation fault.

questions.question_en: Which C library function copies the contents of one string into another?
questions.explanation_en: strcpy(dest, src) copies src including its null terminator into dest. strcat appends, strcmp compares and strlen returns the length.

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

t = (5)
u = (5,)
print(type(t).__name__, type(u).__name__)
questions.explanation_en: Parentheses alone only group an expression, so (5) is just the integer 5. A one-element tuple needs a trailing comma: (5,) or simply 5,.
StringBuilder is mutable: append gives abcde and reverse() reverses it in place to edcba. Method chaining works because each method returns the same builder.
Default arguments fill in missing trailing parameters. add(1) = 1 + 10 + 20 = 31; add(1, 2) = 1 + 2 + 20 = 23.
The ternary operator evaluates the condition a > 3, which is true, so b takes the value of a * 2 = 10. The a + 2 branch (7) is never evaluated.

questions.question_en: The Class C network 192.168.1.0 is subnetted with prefix /28. How many subnets are created and how many usable hosts does each have?
questions.explanation_en: From the default /24, 4 bits are borrowed: 2^4 = 16 subnets. 4 host bits remain: 2^4 − 2 = 14 usable hosts per subnet.

questions.question_en: What is the length of an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation_en: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long, written as eight groups of four hexadecimal digits. IPv4 addresses are 32 bits and MAC addresses are 48 bits.

questions.question_en: Which topology offers the highest fault tolerance and privacy but also the highest cabling cost?
questions.explanation_en: Mesh has dedicated links between every pair of nodes, so there are always alternative paths and traffic is not shared, but the number of cables and ports grows rapidly with n.

questions.question_en: A default Class B network (mask 255.255.0.0) can have at most how many usable hosts?
questions.explanation_en: Class B leaves 16 host bits: 2^16 = 65,536 addresses minus 2 (network and broadcast) = 65,534. 16,777,214 is the Class A figure and 254 is Class C.

questions.question_en: Data compression, encryption and conversion between character encodings (e.g. ASCII to Unicode) are services of which OSI layer?
questions.explanation_en: The Presentation layer (layer 6) is the 'translator' of the OSI model: it handles data format, compression and encryption. The Session layer manages dialogues, not data representation.

questions.question_en: How many usable host addresses does a /22 network provide?
questions.explanation_en: Host bits = 32 − 22 = 10, giving 2^10 = 1024 addresses; removing the network and broadcast addresses leaves 1022 usable hosts.

questions.question_en: Infrared communication (as used in TV remote controls) is limited because infrared signals:

options.en: Need a licence from the government
Cannot pass through walls and require line of sight

questions.explanation_en: Infrared waves are blocked by opaque objects, so they work only over short, unobstructed distances, which also makes them secure within a room.

questions.question_en: DHCP uses UDP ports 67 and 68, and SNMP uses UDP port 161. Which of the following also runs over UDP on port 69?
questions.explanation_en: Trivial File Transfer Protocol is a simple, no-authentication file transfer protocol that uses UDP port 69. FTP uses TCP 20/21 and SFTP runs over SSH on TCP 22.

questions.question_en: A Windows PC that cannot reach a DHCP server automatically assigns itself an address such as 169.254.23.7. This address range is called:
questions.explanation_en: 169.254.0.0/16 is the link-local range used by Automatic Private IP Addressing when DHCP fails; it only works on the local segment.

questions.question_en: Match the protocol with its default port: SMTP, POP3, IMAP.
questions.explanation_en: SMTP (sending mail) uses port 25, POP3 (downloading mail) uses 110 and IMAP (accessing mail on the server) uses 143.

questions.question_en: HTTPS differs from HTTP mainly because HTTPS:

options.en: Does not need a web server
Can transfer only text, not images

questions.explanation_en: HTTPS is HTTP carried inside an SSL/TLS encrypted channel, protecting data from eavesdropping and tampering and authenticating the server through a certificate. It still uses TCP.

questions.question_en: In which topology does data travel in one direction from node to node, and a single node or cable failure can bring down the entire network unless a dual ring is used?
questions.explanation_en: In a ring, each node is connected to exactly two neighbours and data (often a token) circulates in one direction, so one break can disable the whole ring.

questions.question_en: Four processes arrive at time 0 with burst times P1 = 5, P2 = 2, P3 = 8, P4 = 3 ms. With non-preemptive SJF scheduling, the average waiting time is:
questions.explanation_en: SJF order: P2 (2) → P4 (3) → P1 (5) → P3 (8). Start times are 0, 2, 5, 10, so waiting times are P2 = 0, P4 = 2, P1 = 5, P3 = 10. Total = 17; average = 17/4 = 4.25 ms.

questions.question_en: Which statement about kernel-level threads compared with user-level threads is correct?

options.en: User-level threads are always faster to execute once running
Kernel-level threads can be scheduled on different processors, but their creation and switching are slower than for user-level threads
Kernel-level threads are managed by a user library without OS support
User-level threads can be scheduled directly by the OS scheduler

questions.explanation_en: Kernel threads are known to the OS, so they can be scheduled on separate cores and a blocking thread does not stop the others, but each operation needs a mode switch. User-level threads are managed by a library, are cheap to create and switch, but are invisible to the kernel scheduler.

questions.question_en: SJF predicts the next CPU burst by exponential averaging: τ(n+1) = α·t(n) + (1 − α)·τ(n). If α = 0.5, the previous predicted burst τ(n) = 10 ms and the actual last burst t(n) = 6 ms, the next predicted burst is:
questions.explanation_en: τ(n+1) = 0.5 × 6 + 0.5 × 10 = 3 + 5 = 8 ms. With α = 0 the prediction would ignore recent history (stay 10); with α = 1 it would equal the last burst (6).

questions.question_en: P1 arrives at 0 (burst 5, priority 3), P2 at 1 (burst 3, priority 1), P3 at 2 (burst 4, priority 2); lower number = higher priority. Under preemptive priority scheduling the average waiting time is:
questions.explanation_en: Gantt: P1 (0-1), P2 preempts at 1 and runs 1-4, then P3 (priority 2 beats P1's 3) runs 4-8, finally P1 runs 8-12. Waiting: P1 = 12 − 0 − 5 = 7, P2 = 0, P3 = 8 − 2 − 4 = 2. Average = 9/3 = 3 ms.

questions.question_en: Why is a thread called a 'lightweight process'?

options.en: Creating and switching between threads is cheaper because threads share the process's address space and resources
It always runs with lower priority than a process
It uses fewer CPU instructions than a process

questions.explanation_en: Thread creation needs no new address space and a thread switch does not change the memory map, so both are much faster than the corresponding process operations. Threads can do I/O and have no inherent priority penalty.

questions.question_en: The 'convoy effect', in which many short processes wait behind one long CPU-bound process, is a drawback mainly of:
questions.explanation_en: In FCFS a long job that gets the CPU first holds it until completion, so all I/O-bound jobs queue up behind it and devices sit idle. Preemptive schemes like RR and SRTF avoid this by not letting one process monopolise the CPU.

questions.question_en: Which Linux command is used to search for lines matching a text pattern inside files?
questions.explanation_en: grep 'pattern' file prints every line that contains the pattern (e.g. grep -i 'error' log.txt). find and locate search for files by name or attributes, not for text inside them.

questions.question_en: In the many-to-one multithreading model, if one user-level thread makes a blocking system call, what happens?

options.en: The blocking call is converted to a non-blocking one by the thread library
The kernel automatically creates a new kernel thread for the remaining user threads
Only that thread blocks; the other threads of the process keep running
The entire process blocks because all user threads are mapped to a single kernel thread

questions.explanation_en: Many-to-one maps all user threads onto one kernel thread, so the kernel sees a single schedulable entity; a blocking call by any thread blocks the whole process, and the threads cannot run in parallel on multiple cores. One-to-one and many-to-many models avoid this problem.

questions.question_en: The data structure in which the operating system stores the state, program counter, registers, scheduling information and accounting information of a process is the:
questions.explanation_en: Every process is represented in the OS by a process control block (also called a task control block) holding its state, PC, CPU registers, scheduling and memory-management information, accounting data and I/O status. The page table only maps the process's memory.

questions.question_en:
Consider the statements about operating-system structure:
I. A monolithic kernel runs all OS services in a single address space in kernel mode, so a bug in a driver can crash the whole system.
II. Android uses a modified Linux kernel while iOS is derived from the Darwin (BSD-based) kernel.
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation_en: Both are correct. Monolithic kernels (traditional UNIX, Linux) have everything in kernel space, so a faulty module has full privileges. Android is built on the Linux kernel; iOS is built on Darwin, which is BSD/Mach based.

questions.question_en: Which statement creates a view showing only employees of department 10?

options.en: CREATE VIEW D10 AS SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE D_ID = 10;
CREATE TABLE D10 AS VIEW EMP WHERE D_ID = 10;
MAKE VIEW D10 FROM EMP WHERE D_ID = 10;

questions.explanation_en: The syntax is CREATE [OR REPLACE] VIEW view_name AS SELECT ...; The view is then queried like any table: SELECT * FROM D10;

questions.question_en: A shared (S) lock on a data item allows other transactions to:

options.en: Neither read nor write the item
Read the item but not write it
Write the item but not read it

questions.explanation_en: Many transactions may hold shared (read) locks simultaneously, but an exclusive (X) lock, needed for writing, cannot be granted while any S lock exists.

questions.question_en: The 'Isolation' property of transactions means that:

options.en: Concurrent transactions do not see each other's intermediate (uncommitted) results
A transaction cannot read any table that another user owns
Data is encrypted during the transaction
Each transaction runs on a separate server

questions.explanation_en: Isolation makes concurrent execution appear as if transactions ran one after another (serially). It is implemented by locking or multiversion concurrency control, not by separate hardware.

questions.question_en: An attribute 'Age' that is computed from 'Date_of_Birth' is shown in an ER diagram as a:
questions.explanation_en: A derived attribute is drawn as a dashed ellipse. A double ellipse is a multivalued attribute (e.g., phone numbers), and an underlined attribute is the key attribute.

questions.question_en: Which statement about a primary key is correct?

options.en: It may have duplicate values if the table is small
It cannot contain NULL values and must be unique
It can contain NULL in at most one row
It must always be a single attribute

questions.explanation_en: The entity integrity rule says no part of a primary key may be NULL, and values must be unique. A primary key can be composite (more than one attribute). A UNIQUE constraint, by contrast, usually permits NULLs.

questions.question_en: Which aggregate function returns the number of rows in a result set, including duplicates?
questions.explanation_en: COUNT(*) counts every row, including rows with NULLs and duplicates. COUNT(DISTINCT col) counts unique non-NULL values of a column.

questions.question_en: Relation ORDER(Order_No, Item_No, Qty, Item_Name) has key (Order_No, Item_No). Item_Name depends only on Item_No. The highest normal form of ORDER is:
questions.explanation_en: Item_Name is a non-prime attribute depending on part of the composite key (Item_No), which is a partial dependency. Such a relation is in 1NF but not 2NF; splitting into ORDER(Order_No, Item_No, Qty) and ITEM(Item_No, Item_Name) fixes it.

questions.question_en: What is the output of SELECT CONCAT(UPPER(LEFT('delhi', 1)), LOWER(RIGHT('DELHI', 4)));?
questions.explanation_en: LEFT('delhi',1) = 'd' → UPPER → 'D'; RIGHT('DELHI',4) = 'ELHI' → LOWER → 'elhi'; CONCAT joins them into 'Delhi'.

questions.question_en: In the ACID properties of a transaction, 'A' stands for:
questions.explanation_en: ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability. Atomicity means all operations of a transaction complete or none do ('all or nothing').

questions.question_en: In MySQL, which setting makes every single statement a separate transaction that is committed immediately?
questions.explanation_en: With autocommit on (the default), each statement is committed as soon as it executes. START TRANSACTION or SET AUTOCOMMIT = 0 is needed to group several statements and use ROLLBACK.

questions.question_en: What does document.querySelector(".item") return when the page contains five elements with class="item"?

options.en: null, because more than one element matches
All five elements as a NodeList
The last element with class item
Only the first element with class item

questions.explanation_en: querySelector returns the first element matching the CSS selector (or null if none). To get all five, use querySelectorAll, which returns a static NodeList.

questions.question_en:
What will be the marker of the first list item?
  1. Apple
  2. Mango
questions.explanation_en: type="a" chooses lowercase letters and start="4" begins counting at the 4th value, so the items are labelled d. and e. The start value is always a number even when letters are displayed.
Without a compare function, sort() converts elements to strings and compares them in dictionary order: "1" < "10" < "3". For numeric order, use a.sort((x, y) => x - y).

questions.question_en: The declaration <!DOCTYPE html> at the top of a document tells the browser that the page is written in:
questions.explanation_en: HTML5 uses the short, case-insensitive <!DOCTYPE html>. HTML 4.01 and XHTML 1.0 required long doctypes referring to a DTD.
Both rules have equal specificity, so the cascade applies the one that appears later in the stylesheet, i.e. blue. Colours are never mixed.

questions.question_en: Which CSS property converts all the text of an element to capital letters without changing the HTML?
questions.explanation_en: text-transform: uppercase displays every letter in capitals; capitalize capitalises only the first letter of each word. The other properties shown do not exist in CSS.

questions.question_en: Which statement correctly attaches the function show to the click event of a button referenced by btn?
questions.explanation_en: addEventListener takes the event name without the 'on' prefix and a reference to the handler. Writing show() would call the function immediately and pass its return value instead.

questions.question_en: Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), the computer-to-computer exchange of standard business documents such as purchase orders and invoices, is mainly used in:
questions.explanation_en: EDI automates document exchange between the systems of trading partners — manufacturers, suppliers and retailers — which is business-to-business commerce.

questions.question_en: For a sorted array whose values are uniformly distributed, interpolation search has an average-case time complexity of:
questions.explanation_en: Interpolation search estimates the probe position from the key's value instead of always using the middle, which on uniform data shrinks the range much faster, giving O(log log n). Its worst case, on skewed data, degrades to O(n).

questions.question_en: A hash table has 60 slots and currently stores 45 keys. Its load factor is:
questions.explanation_en: Load factor α = number of keys / number of slots = 45 / 60 = 0.75. A larger α means more collisions; with open addressing α can never exceed 1.

questions.question_en: In a singly circular linked list, the next pointer of the last node points to:
questions.explanation_en: Making the last node point back to the first closes the circle, so traversal can start anywhere and continue round. NULL marks the end of an ordinary (non-circular) linked list.

questions.question_en: For a graph with V vertices and E edges, the space needed by an adjacency matrix and by an adjacency list is respectively:
questions.explanation_en: A matrix has a V × V cell for every vertex pair whether or not an edge exists. A list stores each vertex plus one entry per edge (two for undirected), which is far smaller for sparse graphs.

questions.question_en: An input-restricted deque is one in which:

options.en: Deletion is allowed at only one end, but insertion at both ends
Both insertion and deletion are allowed at only one end
Insertion is allowed at only one end, but deletion at both ends
Insertion and deletion are allowed only in the middle

questions.explanation_en: 'Input-restricted' limits the input operation (insertion) to one end while deletions may happen at either end. The reverse arrangement is an output-restricted deque.
i takes the values 1, 2, 4, 8, … and stops once 2^k ≥ n, so the loop runs about log₂ n times. Doubling (or halving) a loop variable gives logarithmic complexity.

questions.question_en: The V-model is also known as the:
questions.explanation_en: The 'V' stands for Verification and Validation: every development stage on the left arm has a matching testing stage on the right arm, so test planning starts early.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a key difference between centralised (e.g. SVN) and distributed (e.g. Git) version control systems?

options.en: A centralised VCS requires no server
In a distributed VCS every developer has a full copy of the repository history
A distributed VCS cannot handle branches
A centralised VCS stores no history

questions.explanation_en: In Git each clone is a complete repository, so commits, history and branching work offline. SVN keeps the full history on one central server that developers must contact for most operations.

questions.question_en: An SRS is said to be 'verifiable' when:

options.en: Every requirement has been approved by the government
It is written in a programming language
There is a finite, cost-effective way to check that the software meets each requirement

questions.explanation_en: Verifiability means each requirement can be tested objectively; vague terms like 'user-friendly' or 'fast' make an SRS unverifiable. Approval or language of writing have nothing to do with verifiability.

questions.question_en: In Git, 'git pull' is essentially equivalent to:

options.en: git fetch followed by git merge
git push followed by git fetch
git add followed by git commit
git clone followed by git init

questions.explanation_en: git pull downloads new commits from the remote (fetch) and integrates them into the current branch (merge, or rebase if configured). git push does the opposite, sending local commits to the remote.

questions.question_en: Which Git command creates a local copy of an existing remote repository?
questions.explanation_en: git clone copies a remote repository, including its full history, to the local machine. git init creates a new empty repository, and git commit records staged changes locally.

questions.question_en: 'Given a buggy C program, the student will locate the logical error.' The level of the cognitive domain tested here is primarily:
questions.explanation_en: Debugging requires breaking the program into parts, tracing relationships and finding what does not fit — the hallmarks of Analysis (differentiating, organising, attributing). Simply running a known algorithm would be Applying.

questions.question_en: In the Herbartian approach, 'Recapitulation' at the end of a lesson on 'Primary keys' usually takes the form of:

options.en: Writing the aim of the lesson on the board
Introducing the next topic of foreign keys
Short questions to check what students have grasped

questions.explanation_en: Recapitulation (sometimes merged with Application) is a quick check of the lesson's outcomes through oral or written questions. Stating the aim happens after preparation; the new topic belongs to the next lesson.

questions.question_en: The theory of Multiple Intelligences, which includes logical–mathematical, linguistic and spatial intelligence, was proposed by:
questions.explanation_en: Howard Gardner proposed Multiple Intelligences in 'Frames of Mind' (1983), originally listing seven and later eight intelligences. Programming draws strongly on logical–mathematical intelligence.

questions.question_en: Micro-teaching is primarily used for:

options.en: Developing specific teaching skills of trainee teachers
Evaluating students at the end of a term
Teaching a complete chapter to a full class

questions.explanation_en: Micro-teaching is a teacher-training technique that reduces class size, time and content so that a trainee can practise one skill at a time under observation and feedback.

questions.question_en: Which of the following items is usually written FIRST in a lesson plan?
questions.explanation_en: A lesson plan begins with identifying data (class, subject, topic, time) and the general and specific objectives, because the content, methods, aids and evaluation are all chosen to achieve those objectives.

questions.question_en: Students start imitating the systematic debugging habits that their teacher models aloud while fixing code. This is best explained by:
questions.explanation_en: Bandura's social learning theory holds that people learn by observing and imitating models (attention, retention, reproduction, motivation). Classical conditioning involves associating stimuli, not imitation.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is an example of a preventive (proactive) classroom management strategy rather than a reactive one?

options.en: Sending a disruptive student out of the lab
Establishing clear lab rules and routines on the first day
Scolding students who talk during the demonstration
Deducting marks after a student damages a keyboard

questions.explanation_en: Preventive strategies (Kounin's 'withitness', clear rules, routines, engaging lessons) stop problems before they occur. The other three are reactions after misbehaviour has already happened.

questions.question_en: A short test given at the start of a course to decide whether a student should join the beginner or the advanced Python batch is an example of:
questions.explanation_en: Placement evaluation checks entry behaviour before instruction to place learners at the right level. Diagnostic evaluation, by contrast, locates the specific causes of persistent learning difficulty.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is an example of a Learning Management System (LMS)?
questions.explanation_en: Moodle is an open-source LMS used to host courses, assignments and quizzes. Scratch is a block-based programming environment, IDLE is a Python editor and Tinkercad is a 3D design/electronics tool.

questions.question_en: The discrimination index of a multiple-choice item is 0.05 and its difficulty value is 0.92. The best interpretation is:

options.en: The item is of average difficulty and should be retained
The item is negatively discriminating and must be reversed
The item is very easy and does not discriminate between high and low scorers
The item is very hard and discriminates well

questions.explanation_en: Difficulty value 0.92 means 92% answered correctly — a very easy item. A discrimination index near zero (0.05) shows high and low groups perform almost equally, so the item does not separate able from weak students and should be revised.
