questions.explanation_en: Gantt: P1 (0-4), P2 (4-8), P3 (8-12), P1 (12-16), P2 (16-17), P3 (17-21), P1 (21-23). Completion times: P1 = 23, P2 = 17, P3 = 21 (all arrived at 0, so turnaround = completion). Average = (23+17+21)/3 = 61/3 = 20.33 ms. Average waiting time would be 12.67 ms.

questions.question_en: GRANT and REVOKE statements are part of which category of SQL?
questions.explanation_en: DCL controls access rights: GRANT gives privileges and REVOKE takes them back. TCL (COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT) controls transactions.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is the fastest type of memory in a computer?
questions.question_hi: कंप्यूटर में निम्न में से सबसे तेज़ मेमोरी कौन-सी है?
questions.explanation_en: Registers sit inside the CPU and are accessed in a single clock cycle, making them the fastest (and smallest) level of the memory hierarchy. Cache is next, followed by RAM and then secondary storage.

questions.question_en: The range of integers that can be represented in 8-bit 2's complement form is:
questions.question_hi: 8-बिट 2's complement में निरूपित की जा सकने वाली पूर्णांकों की सीमा है:
questions.explanation_en: An n-bit 2's complement number spans −2^(n−1) to +2^(n−1) − 1, so for n = 8: −128 to +127. Only one zero exists, which is why the negative side has one extra value. −127 to +127 is the range of sign-magnitude and 1's complement.

questions.question_en: When a form is submitted with method="get", the form data is:

options.en: Stored in a cookie on the client
Appended to the URL as a query string
Sent in the body of the HTTP request and never visible in the URL

questions.explanation_en: With GET, name=value pairs are added after a '?' in the URL, so they are visible, bookmarkable and limited in length. POST sends data in the request body, which is preferred for passwords and large data.

questions.question_en:
What does the following JavaScript code print?
console.log("5" + 3, "5" - 3);
questions.explanation_en: With +, if either operand is a string the other is converted to a string and concatenated, giving "53". The - operator works only on numbers, so "5" is converted to 5 and 5 − 3 = 2.

questions.question_en: An online store such as Amazon or Flipkart selling products directly to individual shoppers is an example of which e-commerce model?
questions.explanation_en: In B2C a business sells directly to end consumers. B2B is trade between businesses, such as a manufacturer buying from a wholesaler.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is valid JSON?
questions.explanation_en: JSON requires keys and string values in double quotes and does not allow trailing commas. Single quotes and unquoted keys are allowed in JavaScript object literals but not in JSON.

questions.question_en: A situation in which the final result depends on the exact order in which several processes access and modify shared data is called a:
questions.explanation_en: A race condition arises when concurrent processes access shared data without proper synchronisation, so the outcome depends on timing. The critical-section problem is about preventing exactly this.

questions.question_en: A switch forwards a frame only to the port on which the destination is located. To do this it maintains a table of:
questions.explanation_en: A switch is a layer-2 device; it learns the source MAC address of each frame and builds a MAC (CAM) address table that maps addresses to ports. Routers use IP addresses.

questions.question_en: Which UML diagram shows the actors of a system and the services (functionalities) the system provides to them?
questions.explanation_en: A use case diagram captures functional requirements from the user's point of view through actors and use cases. Class diagrams show static structure and deployment diagrams show hardware nodes.
The inner statement executes n times for each of the n outer iterations, i.e. n × n = n² times. Two loops one AFTER another would be O(n), but nested loops multiply.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT one of the four necessary (Coffman) conditions for a deadlock?
questions.explanation_en: The four necessary conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, NO preemption and circular wait. If resources can be preempted, the 'no preemption' condition fails and deadlock cannot arise, so 'preemption of resources' is not a condition.

questions.question_en: Which logic gate produces an output of 1 only when all of its inputs are 1?
questions.question_hi: कौन-सा लॉजिक गेट केवल तभी आउटपुट 1 देता है जब उसके सभी इनपुट 1 हों?
questions.explanation_en: An AND gate implements logical multiplication: Y = A·B, which is 1 only for the input row 1,1. An OR gate gives 1 if any input is 1, and NAND gives 0 (not 1) for the all-ones input.

questions.question_en: Which OSI layer is responsible for routing packets from the source host to the destination host across multiple networks?
questions.explanation_en: Routing and logical (IP) addressing belong to the Network layer (layer 3). The Data Link layer delivers frames only within one physical network segment.

questions.question_en: Keys 14, 25, 36 and 47 are inserted in this order into a hash table of size 11 using h(k) = k mod 11 and linear probing. At which index is 47 stored?
questions.explanation_en: All four keys hash to 3 (14, 25, 36, 47 mod 11 = 3). 14 → 3; 25 → 3 taken → 4; 36 → 3, 4 taken → 5; 47 → 3, 4, 5 taken → 6.

questions.question_en: Breadth-first search (BFS) of a graph is normally implemented with the help of a:
questions.explanation_en: BFS visits all neighbours of a vertex before going deeper, which is FIFO behaviour, so a queue is used. DFS uses a stack (or recursion).

questions.question_en: An Aadhaar number issued by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) consists of:
questions.explanation_en: Aadhaar is a 12-digit random number linked to the resident's biometric and demographic data. The 10-character PAN is issued by the Income Tax Department.

questions.question_en: EMP(Name, Salary): (Amit 30000), (Bela 50000), (Chand 40000), (Dev 60000). Output of SELECT Name FROM EMP WHERE Salary > (SELECT AVG(Salary) FROM EMP); is:
questions.explanation_en: Average salary = (30000+50000+40000+60000)/4 = 45000. Rows with Salary > 45000 are Bela (50000) and Dev (60000).

questions.question_en: The connector normally used to terminate Cat 5e / Cat 6 twisted-pair Ethernet cables is:
questions.explanation_en: RJ45 is the 8-pin connector for Ethernet twisted-pair cables. RJ11 is for telephone lines, BNC for coaxial cable and SC/ST/LC for optical fibre.

questions.question_en: In a queue, elements are inserted at the ______ and deleted from the ______.
questions.explanation_en: A queue is FIFO: new elements join at the rear and the oldest element leaves from the front, like a line at a ticket counter.

questions.question_en: A browser shows HTTP status code 404. This means:

options.en: The requested resource was not found on the server
Access is forbidden even with valid credentials
The server encountered an internal error

questions.explanation_en: 404 Not Found means the server is reachable but the requested URL does not exist. 500 is an internal server error, 200 means OK, and 403 means forbidden.

questions.question_en: In MS Word, which keyboard shortcut centre-aligns the selected paragraph?
questions.explanation_en: Ctrl + E centres text. Ctrl + L is left align, Ctrl + J justifies and Ctrl + C copies the selection.

questions.question_en: The document that formally records what a software system must do, and which acts as an agreement between client and developer, is the:
questions.explanation_en: The SRS states the functional and non-functional requirements of the system and serves as the baseline contract. Test reports and user manuals come much later in the life cycle.

questions.question_en: Quick sort that always picks the FIRST element as pivot shows its worst-case O(n²) behaviour when the input array is:

options.en: Made up of distinct prime numbers

questions.explanation_en: On sorted input the first element is the smallest, so every partition is maximally unbalanced (0 and n − 1 elements), giving n + (n − 1) + … ≈ n²/2 comparisons. Random or median-of-three pivots avoid this in practice.

questions.question_en: What is the key difference between DELETE and TRUNCATE in SQL?

options.en: DELETE is faster than TRUNCATE for large tables
DELETE can use a WHERE clause and can be rolled back; TRUNCATE removes all rows and is DDL
TRUNCATE removes the table structure; DELETE does not
There is no difference; they are synonyms

questions.explanation_en: DELETE is row-level DML, logs each row, allows WHERE and ROLLBACK. TRUNCATE is DDL that deallocates all data pages quickly and in most systems cannot be rolled back. DROP is the command that removes the structure.
C passes arguments by value: change receives a copy of a, doubles the copy, and the original a remains 5. To modify a, a pointer (change(&a)) would be needed.

questions.question_en: Four processes share a resource type, and each process may need at most 3 units of it. What is the minimum number of units that guarantees the system can never deadlock?
questions.explanation_en: Worst case: every process holds (3 − 1) = 2 units and waits for one more → 4 × 2 = 8 units are stuck. One extra unit lets someone finish, so minimum = 4 × (3 − 1) + 1 = 9. With 8 units deadlock is possible.

questions.question_en: The Banker's algorithm is used by an operating system for deadlock:
questions.explanation_en: The Banker's algorithm grants a request only if the system stays in a safe state, i.e. it avoids deadlock dynamically using the declared maximum needs. Prevention instead structurally denies one of the four conditions.

questions.question_en: A relation is in First Normal Form (1NF) if:

options.en: Every determinant is a candidate key
Every attribute holds only atomic (indivisible) values

questions.explanation_en: 1NF forbids repeating groups and multivalued cells; each cell must contain a single atomic value. Removing partial dependency gives 2NF, transitive dependency 3NF, and 'every determinant is a candidate key' is BCNF.

questions.question_en: The Gray code equivalent of the binary number 1011 is:
questions.question_hi: बाइनरी संख्या 1011 का ग्रे कोड क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: Keep the MSB (1), then XOR each pair of adjacent binary bits: 1⊕0 = 1, 0⊕1 = 1, 1⊕1 = 0, giving 1110. 1101 is the result of converting 1011 the wrong way (Gray→binary).

questions.question_en: An attack in which malicious JavaScript is injected into a trusted website so that it runs in other users' browsers is called:
questions.explanation_en: XSS injects client-side script into pages viewed by others, often to steal cookies or session tokens. SQL injection targets the back-end database instead of the browser.

questions.question_en: In which topology is every node connected by its own cable to a central device such as a hub or switch?
questions.explanation_en: Star topology uses a central connecting device. It is the most common LAN topology today because one cable fault isolates only one node.

questions.question_en: Evaluation carried out during the teaching–learning process to give feedback and improve learning is called:
questions.explanation_en: Formative evaluation (Scriven, 1967) happens during instruction and is 'assessment for learning'. Summative is at the end for grading; diagnostic identifies specific learning difficulties; placement happens before instruction.

questions.question_en: Micro-teaching was first developed at Stanford University in 1963 by:
questions.explanation_en: Dwight W. Allen and his associates (Acheson, Bush) developed micro-teaching at Stanford in 1963 as a scaled-down teaching encounter for practising single skills.

questions.question_en: Under the CCE scheme introduced by CBSE in 2009, 'Continuous' and 'Comprehensive' respectively refer to:

options.en: Regular unit tests only; scholastic subjects only
Assessment spread over the whole year; coverage of both scholastic and co-scholastic areas
Daily homework; coverage of all textbook chapters
Term-end examination; covering the complete syllabus

questions.explanation_en: In CCE 'continuous' means assessment is regular and integrated with teaching (formative and summative across the year) and 'comprehensive' means it covers scholastic (academic) as well as co-scholastic (life skills, attitudes, co-curricular) growth.

questions.question_en: DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) is best described as:

options.en: A satellite television channel for Class 12
A university-level MOOC platform with credit transfer
A hardware scheme for distributing laptops to teachers
A national platform for school education with QR-coded energised textbooks and teacher resources

questions.explanation_en: DIKSHA, launched in 2017 by MoE/NCERT, hosts e-content linked to textbook QR codes, teacher training courses (NISHTHA) and state-wise resources. SWAYAM is the MOOC platform and PM e-VIDYA/SWAYAM Prabha are TV channels.

questions.question_en: NEP 2020 recommends that the medium of instruction, wherever possible, should be the home language/mother tongue at least till:

options.en: Class 5, preferably till Class 8 and beyond

questions.explanation_en: Para 4.11 of NEP 2020 says the medium of instruction will be the home language/mother tongue/local language until at least Grade 5, but preferably till Grade 8 and beyond, with the three-language formula retained flexibly.

questions.question_en: The National Education Policy 2020 replaces the 10+2 school structure with the:
questions.explanation_en: NEP 2020 proposes 5+3+3+4: Foundational (3 years pre-primary + Classes 1–2), Preparatory (3–5), Middle (6–8) and Secondary (9–12), covering ages 3–18.

questions.question_en: Edgar Dale's 'Cone of Experience' places which of the following at the base (most concrete) level?
questions.explanation_en: Dale's cone runs from the most concrete direct purposeful experiences at the base to the most abstract verbal symbols at the apex. Students learn and retain more from concrete experiences.

tests.description: 100 high-probability questions chosen from the 2023–24 paper trends, all sections.

tests.title: Most Expected Questions — Set 2
tests.subject: Computer Science

questions.question_en: A large square is divided into a 4 × 4 grid of 16 equal small squares. How many squares of all sizes are there in the figure?
questions.explanation_en: Squares of side k in an n × n grid = (n − k + 1)². For n = 4: 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30. The answer 16 counts only the smallest squares.

questions.question_en: If TABLE is coded as UBCMF, then how is CHAIR coded?
questions.explanation_en: Each letter is shifted one step forward: C-D, H-I, A-B, I-J, R-S. So DIBJS.

questions.question_en: A is 5 m east of B. C is 5 m north of B. D is 5 m west of C. In which direction is D with respect to A?
questions.explanation_en: Take B at (0, 0): A = (5, 0), C = (0, 5), D = (-5, 5). D is 10 m west and 5 m north of A, so it lies north-west of A.

questions.question_en: Find the next letter: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.explanation_en: Position gaps are +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6. O is the 15th letter; 15 + 6 = 21 = U.

questions.question_en: A standard die (opposite faces add up to 7) rests on a table with 3 on the top face. What is the sum of the numbers on the four vertical side faces?
questions.explanation_en: Total of all faces = 1 + 2 + … + 6 = 21. Top 3 and bottom 4 (opposite of 3) add to 7, so the four sides add to 21 − 7 = 14. The sides of a standard die always total 14.

questions.question_en: What is the minimum number of straight cuts needed to divide a cube into 64 identical smaller cubes?
questions.explanation_en: 64 = 4 × 4 × 4 pieces need 3 cuts in each of the three directions: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

questions.question_en:
Statement: Many people in a colony are suffering from dengue.
Courses of action: I. The municipal corporation should start fogging and remove stagnant water. II. People should be asked to leave the colony permanently.
questions.explanation_en: Fogging and removing breeding sites tackle the cause (I). Asking people to leave permanently is impractical and extreme (II).

questions.question_en: Find the next term: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation_en: Differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12: 30 + 12 = 42. (Also n(n+1): 6 x 7 = 42.)

questions.question_en: A square sheet of paper is folded in half, and then folded in half again to form a smaller square. One hole is punched through all the layers. How many holes will there be when the sheet is unfolded?
questions.explanation_en: Two folds make 2 × 2 = 4 layers, and a hole punched through all layers appears once in each layer. So 4 holes.

questions.question_en: CAT : DBU :: DOG : ?
questions.explanation_en: Every letter moves one step forward: C-D, A-B, T-U. So D-E, O-P, G-H gives EPH.

questions.question_en:
Statements: Some men are kings. No king is a thief.
Conclusions: I. Some men are not thieves. II. No man is a thief.
questions.explanation_en: The men who are kings are not thieves, so some men are not thieves (I). Nothing is known about the other men, so II does not follow.

questions.question_en: On which day of the week did India become independent on 15 August 1947?
questions.explanation_en: Odd-day method: 1600 years = 0, next 300 years = 1, next 46 years (11 leap years) = 57 days = 1, so 1946 years = 2 odd days. Days from 1 Jan to 15 Aug 1947 = 227 = 3 odd days. Total 5 odd days, and 5 corresponds to Friday (0 = Sunday).

questions.question_en: A wall clock shows 4:20. What time will its image in a plane mirror (placed vertically beside it) appear to show?
questions.explanation_en: Mirror time = 11:60 − actual time = 11:60 − 4:20 = 7:40.

questions.question_en:
Matrix I (rows 0–4, columns 0–4):
Row 0: P E N T A
Row 1: E N T A P
Row 2: N T A P E
Row 3: T A P E N
Row 4: A P E N T
Matrix II (rows 5–9, columns 5–9):
Row 5: O R S I L
Row 6: R S I L O
Row 7: S I L O R
Row 8: I L O R S
Row 9: L O R S I
Each letter is coded by its row number followed by its column number (for example, P can be 00 or 14). Which set of numbers correctly represents the word PEARL?
questions.explanation_en: P = 00, E = 10, A = 22, R = 65, L = 77 are all correct. In the other sets 69 = O, 58 = I and 03 = T, so each has one wrong letter.

questions.question_en: Raj is 9th from the top in a class. Amit is 14th from the bottom. If they exchange positions, Raj becomes 19th from the top. How many students are in the class?
questions.explanation_en: Raj now stands where Amit stood, so Amit's original position is 19th from the top and 14th from the bottom. Total = 19 + 14 - 1 = 32.

questions.question_en: The new Income Tax Act, 2025 replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961 came into effect from:
questions.explanation_en: The Income Tax Act, 2025 is in force from 1 April 2026 and introduces 'tax year' in place of previous year/assessment year.

questions.question_en: Which state elected its first BJP government in the Assembly election results declared in May 2026?
questions.explanation_en: The BJP won about 206-207 of 294 seats in West Bengal, ending the Trinamool Congress's 15-year rule; Suvendu Adhikari was sworn in on 9 May 2026.

questions.question_en: Dr Ambedkar called which Article the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.explanation_en: Article 32 gives the right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

questions.question_en: How many Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A at present?
questions.explanation_en: Ten duties were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) and the 11th (duty of parents to educate children aged 6-14) by the 86th Amendment (2002).

questions.question_en: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (106th Amendment, 2023) provides what reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies?
questions.explanation_en: It reserves one-third of seats, including within SC/ST quotas, but will be applied only after the next Census and delimitation.

questions.question_en: World Teachers' Day is observed internationally on:
questions.explanation_en: UNESCO observes 5 October; India celebrates Teachers' Day on 5 September, the birthday of Dr S. Radhakrishnan.

questions.question_en: Who took oath as the 53rd Chief Justice of India on 24 November 2025?
questions.explanation_en: Justice Surya Kant succeeded Justice B. R. Gavai and is due to retire on 9 February 2027.

questions.question_en: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation_en: The 42nd Amendment is the only one to have changed the Preamble.

questions.question_en: If tan θ = 3/4 and θ is acute, then sin θ is:
questions.explanation_en: Take opposite = 3, adjacent = 4, so hypotenuse = √(9 + 16) = 5. sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse = 3/5.

questions.question_en: A and B together can do a job in 12 days. A alone can do it in 20 days. In how many days can B alone do it?
questions.explanation_en: B's one-day work = 1/12 − 1/20 = (5 − 3)/60 = 1/30. So B alone takes 30 days.

questions.question_en: What single discount is equivalent to successive discounts of 20% and 10%?
questions.explanation_en: Net multiplier = 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72, so the net discount = 28%. (Adding to 30% is the common mistake.)

questions.question_en: Two articles are sold at ₹1,200 each, one at a profit of 20% and the other at a loss of 20%. What is the overall result?
questions.explanation_en: CP of first = 1200/1.2 = 1000; CP of second = 1200/0.8 = 1500. Total CP = 2500, total SP = 2400. Loss = 100, i.e. 4% of 2500 (formula: loss % = (20/10)² = 4%).

questions.question_en: The price of sugar increases by 25%. By what percentage must a family cut its consumption so that its expenditure remains unchanged?
questions.explanation_en: Reduction % = r / (100 + r) × 100 = 25/125 × 100 = 20%. (Taking 25% is the common mistake.)

questions.question_en: A man goes from his house to his office at 40 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation_en: For equal distances the average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 40 × 60 / 100 = 48 km/h. (The arithmetic mean 50 is the usual wrong answer.)

questions.question_en:
Identify the segment that contains an error.
Between you and I, / the project / is not likely / to succeed.
questions.explanation_en: A preposition takes the objective case: “Between you and me”.

questions.question_en:
Select the option that best replaces the part in square brackets. If no change is needed, select ‘No improvement’.
Neither the teacher [or the students] were aware of the changes.
questions.explanation_en: “Neither” is paired with “nor”, not “or”.

questions.question_en: Each of the boys ______ given a prize.
questions.explanation_en: “Each” is singular and takes a singular verb, even when followed by “of + plural noun”.

questions.question_en: Hardly ______ the room when the phone rang.
questions.explanation_en: “Hardly/Scarcely/No sooner” is followed by the past perfect, with auxiliary–subject inversion: Hardly had she entered ... when ...

questions.question_en: 'ने' परसर्ग (विभक्ति-चिह्न) किस कारक का है?
questions.question_hi: 'ने' परसर्ग (विभक्ति-चिह्न) किस कारक का है?
questions.explanation_en: 'Ne' marks the karta (subject/agent) case.
questions.explanation_hi: 'ने' कर्ता कारक का चिह्न है — 'राम ने पत्र लिखा'। कर्म का चिह्न 'को', करण का 'से/के द्वारा' और संप्रदान का 'को/के लिए' है।

questions.question_en: 'यथाशक्ति' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.question_hi: 'यथाशक्ति' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation_en: First member 'yatha' is an indeclinable — avyayibhav samas.
questions.explanation_hi: यथाशक्ति = शक्ति के अनुसार। पहला पद 'यथा' अव्यय है और पूरा पद भी अव्यय की तरह प्रयुक्त होता है, अतः अव्ययीभाव समास है।

questions.question_en: 'विद्यालय' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.question_hi: 'विद्यालय' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: Vidya + aalay = Vidyalay; aa + aa gives aa (deergh swar sandhi).
questions.explanation_hi: विद्या + आलय = विद्यालय। यहाँ आ + आ मिलकर 'आ' बनता है, अतः यह दीर्घ स्वर संधि है।

questions.question_en: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'कमल' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'कमल' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?
questions.explanation_en: Neerad means cloud, not lotus; the other three are synonyms of lotus.
questions.explanation_hi: पंकज, जलज और सरोज तीनों 'कमल' के पर्यायवाची हैं। 'नीरद' का अर्थ बादल (नीर देने वाला) है, कमल नहीं।

questions.question_en: 'चरण-कमल बंदौं हरि राई' — इस पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.question_hi: 'चरण-कमल बंदौं हरि राई' — इस पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation_en: Feet are identified with lotuses without a comparison word, which is Rupak (metaphor).
questions.explanation_hi: यहाँ चरणों (उपमेय) पर कमल (उपमान) का अभेद आरोप किया गया है — 'कमल रूपी चरण'। बिना वाचक शब्द के उपमेय-उपमान को एक मान लेना रूपक अलंकार है।

questions.question_en: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य चुनिए: (अनेक)
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वाक्य चुनिए: (अनेक)
questions.explanation_en: 'Anek' is already plural, so 'anekon' is incorrect.
questions.explanation_hi: 'अनेक' स्वयं बहुवचन (एक से अधिक) का बोध कराता है, इसलिए 'अनेकों' अशुद्ध है। 'समस्याओं' विभक्ति-रहित स्थिति में प्रयोग नहीं होगा।

questions.question_en: When both inputs of a clocked JK flip-flop are held at 1 (J = K = 1), on each active clock edge the flip-flop:
questions.question_hi: क्लॉक्ड JK फ्लिप-फ्लॉप के दोनों इनपुट 1 (J = K = 1) होने पर प्रत्येक सक्रिय क्लॉक एज पर फ्लिप-फ्लॉप क्या करता है?
questions.explanation_en: For J = K = 1 the JK flip-flop complements its output (Q+ = Q'), removing the invalid state of the SR flip-flop. J = K = 0 is the hold condition.

questions.question_en: The most distinguishing feature of the spiral model, compared with the waterfall model, is its explicit emphasis on:
questions.explanation_en: Each loop (cycle) of the spiral includes a dedicated risk-identification and risk-resolution step, so the spiral model is called a risk-driven model. The waterfall model has no explicit risk-handling phase.

questions.question_en: Which C library function allocates memory dynamically and initialises all its bytes to zero?
questions.explanation_en: calloc(n, size) allocates n blocks of the given size and zeroes them; malloc leaves the memory uninitialised, realloc resizes, free releases.

questions.question_en: Which of the following built-in Python data types is immutable?
questions.explanation_en: Once created, a tuple's elements cannot be added, removed or reassigned, so tuples (like str, int and frozenset) are immutable and hashable. Lists, dictionaries and sets can be changed in place.

questions.question_en: An e-mail that pretends to come from a bank and asks the user to click a link and 'verify' the account password is an example of:
questions.explanation_en: Phishing uses fake but genuine-looking messages and websites to trick users into revealing passwords, OTPs or card details. Cyber squatting is registering a domain name similar to a famous brand in bad faith.

questions.question_en: If an int pointer p holds the address 1000 and int occupies 4 bytes, what is the value of p + 1?
questions.explanation_en: Pointer arithmetic is scaled by the size of the pointed-to type. p + 1 moves to the next int, i.e. 1000 + 4 = 1004. For a char pointer the answer would be 1001.

questions.question_en: Which Python file mode opens a text file for appending, creates the file if it does not exist, and also allows reading from it?
questions.explanation_en: 'a+' = append and read; writes always go to the end and a missing file is created. 'a' allows appending only, 'r+' needs the file to already exist, and 'w+' truncates the existing contents.
Specificity decides, not order: an id selector (1,0,0) beats a class selector (0,1,0), which beats a type selector (0,0,1). Only inline styles or !important could override the id rule here.

questions.question_en: How many cells does a Karnaugh map for a four-variable Boolean function contain?
questions.question_hi: चार चर वाले बूलियन फलन के कार्नो मैप (K-map) में कितने सेल होते हैं?
questions.explanation_en: A K-map has one cell per minterm, and n variables give 2^n minterms: 4 cells for 2 variables, 8 for 3 and 16 for 4 (arranged 4 × 4).

questions.question_en: Which transmission medium carries data as pulses of light and is immune to electromagnetic interference?
questions.explanation_en: Optical fibre transmits light through a glass or plastic core using total internal reflection, so electrical noise cannot affect it and it supports the highest bandwidth over long distances.

questions.question_en: Which CPU register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.question_hi: कौन-सा CPU रजिस्टर अगले निर्देश का पता (address) रखता है?
questions.explanation_en: The Program Counter (PC) always points to the next instruction and is incremented after each fetch. The Instruction Register holds the instruction currently being executed, and the MAR holds the address of whatever memory location is being accessed right now.

questions.question_en: Which SDLC model is a linear, sequential approach in which each phase must be completed before the next one begins and there is no overlapping of phases?
questions.explanation_en: The classical waterfall model moves strictly from requirements to design, coding, testing and maintenance with no overlap. Spiral and agile are iterative, and prototyping builds a working mock-up first.

questions.question_en: The Agile Manifesto (2001) values 'working software' over:
questions.explanation_en: The four Agile values are: individuals and interactions over processes and tools, working software over comprehensive documentation, customer collaboration over contract negotiation, and responding to change over following a plan. The other three options are themselves values on the preferred side.

questions.question_en: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in ascending sorted order?
questions.explanation_en: Inorder visits left subtree, root, right subtree; since left keys < root < right keys in a BST, the output is sorted. This is the basis of 'tree sort'.

questions.question_en: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once even if the condition is false initially?
questions.explanation_en: A do-while loop tests the condition after the body, so the body always runs once. for and while are entry-controlled loops that test first.

questions.question_en: A candidate key that is chosen by the designer to uniquely identify tuples in a relation is called the:
questions.explanation_en: Among the candidate keys one is selected as the primary key; the remaining candidate keys are alternate (secondary) keys. A super key may contain extra attributes.

questions.question_en: Which of the following SQL commands belongs to DDL (Data Definition Language)?
questions.explanation_en: DDL commands define or change structure: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE. INSERT and UPDATE are DML (data manipulation), GRANT is DCL.

questions.question_en: How many layers does the OSI reference model have?
questions.explanation_en: The OSI model has seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation and Application. The TCP/IP model is usually described with four layers, which is the common distractor.

questions.question_en: With the default box-sizing (content-box), an element has width: 200px; padding: 10px; border: 5px solid; margin: 20px. What is the width of its visible box (from border edge to border edge)?
questions.explanation_en: Visible width = content + left/right padding + left/right border = 200 + 2×10 + 2×5 = 230px. Adding the margins (2×20) gives the 270px of space the element occupies, but margins are outside the border.

questions.question_en: The Information Technology Act, 2000 of India came into force on:
questions.explanation_en: The Act received Presidential assent on 9 June 2000 and was brought into force on 17 October 2000. 27 October 2009 is when the IT (Amendment) Act 2008 came into force.

questions.question_en: A fully connected mesh network has 10 computers. How many point-to-point links are required?
questions.explanation_en: A full mesh of n nodes needs n(n−1)/2 links = 10×9/2 = 45. Option 4 counts each link twice (n(n−1)).

questions.question_en: A binary tree has root A with left child B and right child C. B has left child D and right child E; C has only a right child F. The postorder traversal is:

options.en: D E F B C A
A B D E C F
D E B F C A
D B E A C F

questions.explanation_en: Postorder = left, right, root. Left subtree of A gives D E B; right subtree gives F C; then A → D E B F C A. D B E A C F is inorder and A B D E C F is preorder.

questions.question_en: Table A has rows with ID values 1, 2, 3 and table B has rows with ID values 2, 3, 4. How many rows does SELECT * FROM A INNER JOIN B ON A.ID = B.ID; return?
questions.explanation_en: An inner join keeps only matching IDs: 2 and 3, i.e., 2 rows. A LEFT JOIN would give 3 rows, a FULL OUTER JOIN 4 rows and a CROSS JOIN 9 rows.

questions.question_en: According to De Morgan's theorem, the complement of (A·B) is equal to:
questions.question_hi: डी मॉर्गन प्रमेय के अनुसार (A·B) का पूरक (complement) किसके बराबर है?
questions.explanation_en: De Morgan's first theorem states (A·B)' = A' + B': the complement of a product is the sum of the complements. The second theorem is (A + B)' = A'·B'. Option 2 is the complement of (A + B), not of (A·B).

questions.question_en: An attribute in one relation that refers to the primary key of another relation is a:
questions.explanation_en: A foreign key enforces referential integrity: its values must match a primary-key value in the referenced table or be NULL. Example: Dept_ID in EMPLOYEE referring to DEPARTMENT(Dept_ID).

questions.question_en: How many usable host addresses are available in a subnet with prefix /27?
questions.explanation_en: Host bits = 32 − 27 = 5, so 2^5 = 32 addresses. Subtracting the network and broadcast addresses gives 32 − 2 = 30 usable hosts.

questions.question_en: Alpha testing is performed:

options.en: At the developer's site by selected users or in-house testers
Only by automated tools after deployment
At the customer's site by end users without developers

questions.explanation_en: Alpha testing happens in a controlled environment at the developer's site. Beta testing is done later by real users in their own environment, with developers absent.

questions.question_en: Which of the following sorting algorithms is NOT stable in its standard form?
questions.explanation_en: A stable sort keeps equal keys in their original relative order. Heap sort's swaps with the root can move equal keys past each other; quick sort and selection sort are also unstable, while merge, insertion and bubble sort are stable.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a checked exception in Java?
questions.explanation_en: Checked exceptions (such as IOException, SQLException, FileNotFoundException) must be caught or declared with throws, and the compiler enforces this. The other three are subclasses of RuntimeException and are unchecked.

questions.question_en: A C program on Linux executes the statement fork() three times in sequence (none of the calls fails). How many processes exist in total after the third call, counting the original?
questions.explanation_en: Each fork() duplicates every existing process, so n sequential forks produce 2^n processes: 2 after the first, 4 after the second and 8 after the third (7 children plus the original).

questions.question_en: Second Normal Form (2NF) removes which kind of dependency from a 1NF relation?

options.en: Partial dependency of non-key attributes on part of a composite key

questions.explanation_en: 2NF requires every non-prime attribute to be fully functionally dependent on the whole primary key. Partial dependency can only exist when the key is composite, so a 1NF relation with a single-attribute key is automatically in 2NF.

questions.question_en: Which CSS selector selects the element having id="header"?
questions.explanation_en: The hash (#) selects by id, the dot (.) selects by class, and a bare name such as header selects the element type <header>.

questions.question_en: Which generation of computers used vacuum tubes as the main electronic component?
questions.question_hi: कंप्यूटर की किस पीढ़ी में मुख्य इलेक्ट्रॉनिक घटक के रूप में वैक्यूम ट्यूब का प्रयोग हुआ?
questions.explanation_en: First-generation machines (1940s–mid 1950s, e.g. ENIAC, UNIVAC I) were built from vacuum tubes, which were bulky, hot and unreliable. Transistors replaced them in the second generation, ICs in the third and microprocessors in the fourth.

questions.question_en: A model is trained on thousands of e-mails, each already labelled 'spam' or 'not spam', so that it can classify new e-mails. This is an example of:
questions.explanation_en: Supervised learning learns from input–output pairs (labelled data). Unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabelled data and reinforcement learning learns from rewards and penalties.

questions.question_en: The postfix form of the infix expression A + B * C − D / E is:
questions.explanation_en: * and / bind tighter than + and −: B * C → B C *, D / E → D E /. Then left-to-right: (A + BC*) − DE/ → A B C * + D E / −.

questions.question_en: Java does not allow a class to extend more than one class. Multiple inheritance of type is achieved in Java by using:
questions.explanation_en: A Java class can extend only one class but can implement any number of interfaces, e.g. class C extends A implements X, Y. Abstract classes are still classes, so only one can be extended.

questions.question_en: What is the maximum number of comparisons binary search needs to find a key (or report failure) in a sorted array of 1000 elements?
questions.explanation_en: Worst case = ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1 = ⌊log₂ 1000⌋ + 1 = 9 + 1 = 10, because 2^10 = 1024 ≥ 1000. 500 is the average for linear search, not binary search.

questions.question_en: After the Linux command chmod 754 report.sh, the permissions of report.sh are:
questions.explanation_en: Each octal digit is r = 4, w = 2, x = 1 for owner, group, others: 7 = rwx, 5 = r-x, 4 = r--. So the owner can do everything, the group can read and execute, others can only read.

questions.question_en: A process that is waiting to be assigned to the CPU and has everything it needs except the processor is in which state?
questions.explanation_en: The ready state means the process is in main memory and runnable, only waiting for the scheduler to dispatch it. A waiting/blocked process cannot run until an event such as I/O completion occurs.

questions.question_en: The binary number (1011)2 is equal to which decimal number?
questions.question_hi: बाइनरी संख्या (1011)2 का दशमलव मान क्या है?

questions.question_en: Testing in which the tester designs test cases only from the specification, without looking at the internal code, is called:
questions.explanation_en: Black-box (functional/behavioural) testing treats the program as a closed box and checks outputs for given inputs. White-box, glass-box and structural testing are names for code-based testing.

questions.question_en: Section 66A of the IT Act, which punished sending 'offensive' messages through communication services, was struck down by the Supreme Court in:

options.en: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

questions.explanation_en: In Shreya Singhal (2015) the Court held Section 66A unconstitutional for violating freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a). Puttaswamy (2017) recognised the right to privacy.

questions.question_en: Cache memory improves performance because programs tend to access the same or nearby memory locations repeatedly. This property is called:
questions.explanation_en: Temporal locality (recently used data is reused soon) and spatial locality (neighbouring addresses are used together) are together called locality of reference; cache exploits both. DMA and interleaving are unrelated techniques.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is an absolute cell reference in MS Excel that does not change when the formula is copied?
questions.explanation_en: Placing $ before both the column letter and the row number locks both, so $C$5 always points to C5. $C5 and C$5 are mixed references and C5 is relative.

questions.question_en: Three processes P1, P2, P3 arrive at time 0 in that order with CPU burst times 10, 4 and 6 ms. Under FCFS scheduling the average waiting time is:
questions.explanation_en: FCFS runs P1 (0-10), P2 (10-14), P3 (14-20). Waiting times: P1 = 0, P2 = 10, P3 = 14; total 24, average 24/3 = 8 ms. 14.67 ms is the average turnaround time (10+14+20)/3, a common mix-up.

name() is non-virtual, so the call is bound at compile time using the pointer type (Shape*) and prints Shape. draw() is virtual, so it is bound at run time to the actual object type (Circle) and prints drawCircle.

questions.question_en: Belady's anomaly — the number of page faults increasing when the number of allocated frames is increased — can occur with which page-replacement algorithm?
questions.explanation_en: FIFO is not a stack algorithm, so the set of pages held with n frames need not be a subset of those held with n+1 frames. LRU and Optimal are stack algorithms and never show the anomaly.

questions.question_en: Which transport-layer protocol is connection-oriented and guarantees reliable, in-order delivery of data?
questions.explanation_en: TCP sets up a connection, numbers segments, uses acknowledgements and retransmission, so delivery is reliable and ordered. UDP is connectionless and gives no such guarantee; IP and ICMP are network-layer protocols.

questions.question_en: The COCOMO cost-estimation model was developed by:
questions.explanation_en: Boehm introduced COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) in 1981. Albrecht proposed function points, Halstead proposed software science metrics, and McCabe proposed cyclomatic complexity.

questions.question_en: Cells A1:A5 contain 10, the text "Delhi", a blank cell, 25 and 0. What do =COUNT(A1:A5) and =COUNTA(A1:A5) return?
questions.explanation_en: COUNT counts only numeric cells: 10, 25 and 0 = 3 (zero is a number). COUNTA counts all non-empty cells: 10, Delhi, 25, 0 = 4. The blank cell is ignored by both.

questions.question_en: Using FIFO page replacement with 3 frames (initially empty), how many page faults occur for the reference string 5, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4, 2, 3, 0, 3, 1, 2?
questions.explanation_en: Frames after each fault: [5] [5,0] [5,0,1] → 2 replaces 5 → 0 hit → 3 replaces 0 → 0 replaces 1 → 4 replaces 2 → 2 replaces 3 → 3 replaces 0 → 0 replaces 4 → 3 hit → 1 replaces 2 → 2 replaces 3. Only 2 hits out of 14 references → 12 faults. LRU would give 11 and Optimal 8.

questions.question_en: A CS teacher records a video explaining 'normalisation' for students to watch at home and uses class time for solving problems and clearing doubts. This approach is known as:
questions.explanation_en: In a flipped classroom direct instruction is shifted outside the class through videos and class time is used for higher-order activities, practice and interaction. It is a form of blended learning.

questions.question_en: According to NEP 2020, the new national assessment centre to set standards for student assessment is called:
questions.explanation_en: PARAKH (Performance Assessment, Review and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development) was proposed by NEP 2020 and set up under NCERT in 2023. NISHTHA is a teacher training programme and NIPUN Bharat is the FLN mission.

questions.question_en: Bloom's taxonomy of educational objectives (1956) classifies objectives into how many domains?
questions.explanation_en: Bloom and co-workers proposed three domains: cognitive (Bloom, 1956), affective (Krathwohl, 1964) and psychomotor (Simpson/Harrow/Dave). Six is the number of levels within the cognitive domain, a common confusion.

questions.question_en: Which teaching method is most suitable for teaching the procedure of installing an operating system to a class of 40 students with only two computers?
questions.explanation_en: In the demonstration method the teacher performs the activity while students observe, which suits limited equipment and a procedural skill. Laboratory/heuristic methods need every student to work hands-on.

questions.question_en: In the revised Bloom's taxonomy (Anderson and Krathwohl, 2001), the highest level of the cognitive domain is:
questions.explanation_en: The revised taxonomy reorders the top levels to Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create, with 'Create' at the top. 'Synthesis' was the fifth level in the original 1956 version and is replaced by Create.

questions.question_en: According to Piaget, a child who can think logically about concrete objects but not about abstract hypotheses is in the:
questions.explanation_en: The concrete operational stage (about 7–11 years) brings conservation, reversibility and logical thought about concrete things; abstract, hypothetical reasoning appears in the formal operational stage (11+).

questions.question_en: Which of the following is the most important objective of teaching Computer Science at the secondary stage?

options.en: Memorising the syntax of several languages
Developing computational thinking and problem-solving ability
Preparing students only for board examinations
Making every student a professional programmer

questions.explanation_en: NCF and the CBSE Class 11–12 CS curriculum state that the core aim is computational thinking (decomposition, abstraction, algorithms) and logical problem solving. Syntax memorisation and professional programming are narrow, instrumental aims.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a limitation of the lecture method in teaching Computer Science?

options.en: It keeps the learner passive and gives little scope for hands-on practice
It is not suitable for large classes
It cannot cover a large syllabus in limited time
It cannot be used to introduce a new topic

questions.explanation_en: The lecture method is economical for large classes and wide syllabi and is fine for introductions; its real weakness is passive listening with no activity, which is a serious drawback for a skill-based subject like CS.

questions.question_en: NEP 2020 recommends that coding be introduced to students from which class onwards?
questions.explanation_en: NEP 2020 (para 4.25) states that coding will be introduced at the Middle Stage, i.e. from Class 6, along with vocational exposure and 'bagless' internship days.

questions.question_en: The five formal steps of lesson planning — Preparation, Presentation, Association (Comparison), Generalisation and Application — were given by followers of:
questions.explanation_en: These are the Herbartian steps, formulated by Herbart's followers (Ziller and Rein) from his four steps. Dewey is associated with the project/problem method and Montessori with sense training.

tests.description: 100 high-probability questions chosen from the 2023–24 paper trends, all sections.

tests.title: Section Test — Arithmetical & Numerical Ability 1
tests.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability

questions.question_en: A rectangular park is 60 m long and 40 m wide. A path 5 m wide runs all around it on the outside. The area of the path is:
questions.explanation_en: Outer rectangle = (60 + 10) × (40 + 10) = 70 × 50 = 3500 m². Park = 60 × 40 = 2400 m². Path = 3500 − 2400 = 1100 m². Adding only 5 m (not 2 × 5) to each side is the usual error.

questions.question_en: Using an algebraic identity, the value of 103 × 97 is:
If α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0, then α² + β² equals:
questions.explanation_en: α + β = 5 and αβ = 6. α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 25 − 12 = 13. (Roots are 2 and 3: 4 + 9 = 13.)

questions.question_en: Two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at a point P inside the circle. If AP = 6 cm, PB = 4 cm and CP = 3 cm, then PD is:
questions.explanation_en: By the intersecting chords theorem, AP × PB = CP × PD → 6 × 4 = 3 × PD → PD = 8 cm.

questions.question_en: The value of (1 − sin²θ) × sec²θ is:
questions.explanation_en: 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ, and cos²θ × sec²θ = cos²θ × 1/cos²θ = 1.

questions.question_en: A point P is 25 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 7 cm. The length of the tangent drawn from P to the circle is:
questions.explanation_en: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so tangent = √(25² − 7²) = √(625 − 49) = √576 = 24 cm.

questions.question_en: A and B together can do a job in 12 days. A alone can do it in 20 days. In how many days can B alone do it?
questions.explanation_en: B's one-day work = 1/12 − 1/20 = (5 − 3)/60 = 1/30. So B alone takes 30 days.

questions.question_en: The sum of the interior angles of a hexagon is:
questions.explanation_en: Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180° = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°.

questions.question_en: What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years?

The table shows the number of students who appeared and passed in a Computer Science examination from five schools.
School | Appeared | Passed
P | 240 | 180
Q | 300 | 255
R | 180 | 117
S | 360 | 288
T | 220 | 198
Which school has the highest pass percentage?
questions.explanation_en: Pass % = passed/appeared × 100: P 75%, Q 85%, R 65%, S 80%, T 90%. T is highest; S has the most passes but not the highest rate.

questions.question_en: A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the stream flows at 5 km/h. How much time does it take to go 60 km downstream and come back?
questions.explanation_en: Downstream speed = 20 km/h, time = 3 h. Upstream speed = 10 km/h, time = 6 h. Total = 9 hours.

questions.question_en: The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. Its area is (take π = 22/7):
For a moderately skewed distribution, the mean is 25 and the median is 24. Using the empirical relation, the mode is:
questions.explanation_en: Empirical relation: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean = 3 × 24 − 2 × 25 = 72 − 50 = 22.

questions.question_en: From a point on the ground 30 m away from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60°. The height of the tower is:
questions.explanation_en: tan 60° = height / 30 → height = 30 × √3 = 30√3 m (≈ 51.96 m). 10√3 m would result from using tan 30° by mistake.

questions.question_en: If tan θ = 3/4 and θ is acute, then sin θ is:
questions.explanation_en: Take opposite = 3, adjacent = 4, so hypotenuse = √(9 + 16) = 5. sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse = 3/5.

questions.question_en: The area of a triangle with sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm is:
A 180 m long train crosses a 270 m long platform in 30 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation_en: Distance covered = 180 + 270 = 450 m in 30 s, so speed = 15 m/s = 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.question_en: If x + 1/x = 5, then the value of x² + 1/x² is:
questions.explanation_en: Square both sides: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25, so x² + 1/x² = 25 − 2 = 23. The trap answer 27 adds 2 instead of subtracting it.

questions.question_en: Two articles are sold at ₹1,200 each, one at a profit of 20% and the other at a loss of 20%. What is the overall result?
questions.explanation_en: CP of first = 1200/1.2 = 1000; CP of second = 1200/0.8 = 1500. Total CP = 2500, total SP = 2400. Loss = 100, i.e. 4% of 2500 (formula: loss % = (20/10)² = 4%).

questions.question_en: If a + b = 10 and ab = 21, then a² + b² is:

tests.description: 20 questions, Arithmetical & Numerical Ability only, exam pattern.

tests.title: Section Test — Arithmetical & Numerical Ability 2
tests.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability

questions.question_en: If x is 20% more than y, then y is what percent less than x?
questions.explanation_en: Let y = 100, so x = 120. y is less than x by 20, i.e. 20/120 × 100 = 16 2/3%.

questions.question_en: What is 35% of 240?

The table shows the production (in thousand units) of three items by a company.
Year | Laptops | Tablets | Printers
2020 | 40 | 25 | 15
2021 | 45 | 30 | 20
2022 | 50 | 35 | 18
2023 | 60 | 32 | 24
2024 | 55 | 40 | 30
In which year did printers form the highest percentage of the company's total production in that year?
The speed of a boat in still water is 9 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. What is the downstream speed?
questions.explanation_en: Downstream speed = boat speed + stream speed = 9 + 3 = 12 km/h.

questions.question_en: What is the HCF of 2/3, 4/9 and 8/27?
questions.explanation_en: HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators / LCM of denominators = HCF(2, 4, 8) / LCM(3, 9, 27) = 2/27. (8/3 is their LCM.)

questions.question_en: What is the unit digit of 7^243?
questions.explanation_en: Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat in a cycle of 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. 243 = 4 × 60 + 3, so the unit digit is the 3rd in the cycle, 3.

questions.question_en: A policeman spots a thief 200 m away. The thief starts running at 10 km/h and the policeman chases him at 11 km/h. How far does the thief run before he is caught?
questions.explanation_en: Relative speed = 1 km/h = 1000 m per hour. To close 200 m takes 0.2 hour. The thief runs 10 × 0.2 = 2 km = 2000 m (the policeman runs 2200 m).

questions.question_en: Ramesh walks to school at 4 km/h and reaches 5 minutes late. At 5 km/h he reaches 10 minutes early. What is the distance to school?
questions.explanation_en: The difference in time = 15 min = 1/4 h. d/4 − d/5 = 1/4, so d/20 = 1/4 and d = 5 km.

questions.question_en:
The table shows the production (in thousand units) of three items by a company.
Year | Laptops | Tablets | Printers
2020 | 40 | 25 | 15
2021 | 45 | 30 | 20
2022 | 50 | 35 | 18
2023 | 60 | 32 | 24
2024 | 55 | 40 | 30
What was the total production of all three items in 2022?
questions.explanation_en: 2022 total = 50 + 35 + 18 = 103 thousand units.

questions.question_en: The median of the data 7, 3, 9, 4, 12, 6 is:
questions.explanation_en: Arrange in order: 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 12. With an even count (6), median = average of the 3rd and 4th values = (6 + 7)/2 = 6.5. 6.83 is the mean, not the median.

questions.question_en: The areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio 16 : 25. The ratio of their corresponding altitudes is:
questions.explanation_en: For similar triangles, ratio of areas = square of the ratio of corresponding sides, altitudes or medians. So altitude ratio = √16 : √25 = 4 : 5.

questions.question_en: A ladder 20 m long leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of 60° with the ground. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation_en: Height = ladder × sin 60° = 20 × √3/2 = 10√3 m (≈ 17.32 m). 10 m is the distance of the foot from the wall (20 cos 60°).

questions.question_en: If x = 2 + √3, then x² + 1/x² equals:

The table shows the production (in thousand units) of three items by a company.
Year | Laptops | Tablets | Printers
2020 | 40 | 25 | 15
2021 | 45 | 30 | 20
2022 | 50 | 35 | 18
2023 | 60 | 32 | 24
2024 | 55 | 40 | 30
By what percent did laptop production increase from 2020 to 2023?
questions.explanation_en: Increase = 60 − 40 = 20 thousand. Percent increase = 20/40 × 100 = 50%. 33.3% wrongly divides by the final value (20/60).

questions.question_en: What is the greatest 4-digit number divisible by 12?
questions.explanation_en: 9999 ÷ 12 leaves remainder 3, so subtract 3: 9996 = 12 × 833.

questions.question_en: If a − b = 3 and a³ − b³ = 117, then the value of ab is:
questions.explanation_en: a³ − b³ = (a − b)³ + 3ab(a − b). So 117 = 27 + 9ab → 9ab = 90 → ab = 10. (Check: a = 5, b = 2.)

questions.question_en: The value of sin 30° + cos 60° is:
questions.explanation_en: sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 60° = 1/2, so the sum is 1.

questions.question_en: What is the remainder when 2^50 is divided by 7?
questions.explanation_en: 2^3 = 8 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 7. 2^50 = (2^3)^16 × 2^2 = 1 × 4, so the remainder is 4.

questions.question_en: A father is 3 times as old as his son. After 12 years he will be twice as old as his son. What is the present age of the son?
questions.explanation_en: Let the son be S, father 3S. 3S + 12 = 2(S + 12), so S = 12 (father is 36).

questions.question_en: What single discount is equivalent to successive discounts of 20% and 10%?
questions.explanation_en: Net multiplier = 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72, so the net discount = 28%. (Adding to 30% is the common mistake.)

tests.description: 20 questions, Arithmetical & Numerical Ability only, exam pattern.

tests.title: Section Test — Computer Science 1
tests.subject: Computer Science

questions.question_en: In C, the statement int add(int, int); placed before main() is called a:
questions.explanation_en: A prototype declares the function's name, return type and parameter types so the compiler can check calls before the definition appears. The definition includes the body.

questions.question_en: An undirected graph has 6 vertices with degrees 3, 3, 2, 2, 2 and 2. How many edges does it have?
questions.explanation_en: By the handshaking lemma, the sum of degrees = 2E. Sum = 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 14, so E = 14 / 2 = 7. 14 forgets that each edge is counted at both ends.

questions.question_en: Which of the following state transitions is NOT possible in the five-state process model?
questions.explanation_en: When the awaited event occurs, a blocked process moves to Ready, never straight to Running; only the dispatcher moves a process from Ready to Running. Running → Ready happens on a timer interrupt (preemption) and Running → Waiting on an I/O request.

questions.question_en: Why is the spiral model often called a 'meta model'?

options.en: It is used only to model metadata
It is meant only for small projects
It can incorporate features of other SDLC models

questions.explanation_en: The spiral model subsumes other models: a single loop resembles the waterfall model, its early loops use prototyping, and its loop-by-loop growth resembles the incremental/evolutionary approach. Hence it is termed a meta model.

questions.question_en: A priority queue is most efficiently implemented using a binary heap. The time complexity of inserting an element into such a priority queue of n elements is:
questions.explanation_en: The new element is placed at the end of the heap and moved up (heapify-up) at most the height of the tree, which is ⌊log₂ n⌋. A sorted array would need O(n) shifting per insertion.

questions.question_en: In the relationship 'Department HAS Employees' where one department has many employees and every employee belongs to exactly one department, the cardinality ratio Department : Employee is:
questions.explanation_en: One department maps to many employees and each employee to one department, so Department : Employee is one-to-many (1 : N). N : 1 would be the same relationship read from the Employee side.

questions.question_en: Which relational-algebra operator is used to select a subset of columns (attributes) of a relation?
questions.explanation_en: Projection picks columns (and removes duplicate rows); selection picks rows that satisfy a condition. Students often confuse the two: σ is 'horizontal', π is 'vertical'.

questions.question_en: Which of the following queries is INVALID in standard SQL?

options.en: SELECT Dept FROM EMP GROUP BY Dept HAVING COUNT(*) > 2;
SELECT Dept, COUNT(*) FROM EMP GROUP BY Dept;
SELECT Dept, Name, COUNT(*) FROM EMP GROUP BY Dept;

questions.explanation_en: Every non-aggregated column in SELECT must appear in GROUP BY; Name is neither grouped nor aggregated, so the query is invalid (MySQL in ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY mode rejects it). The other three are well-formed.

questions.question_en: In a max-heap, which property holds for every node?

options.en: Its key is smaller than the keys of its children
Its left child is smaller than its right child
Its key is greater than or equal to the keys of its children
All keys in its left subtree are smaller than all keys in its right subtree

questions.explanation_en: The max-heap property orders each parent above its children, so the maximum is always at the root. There is no left–right ordering between siblings; that kind of ordering belongs to a BST.
An unsigned char holds 0-255. 250 + 10 = 260 wraps around modulo 256, giving 260 - 256 = 4.

questions.question_en: Under Highest Response Ratio Next (HRRN), response ratio = (waiting time + burst time) / burst time. At a scheduling instant the ready processes are A (waited 10, burst 5), B (waited 12, burst 8), C (waited 6, burst 2) and D (waited 14, burst 7). Which is selected next?
questions.explanation_en: Ratios: A = 15/5 = 3, B = 20/8 = 2.5, C = 8/2 = 4, D = 21/7 = 3. C has the highest ratio. HRRN favours short jobs but also ages long waiters, avoiding starvation.

questions.question_en: Using adjacency lists, the time complexity of BFS or DFS on a graph with V vertices and E edges is:
questions.explanation_en: Each vertex is enqueued/visited once (O(V)) and each adjacency list is scanned once (O(E) in total). With an adjacency matrix the cost rises to O(V²).

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

with open("m.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("ABCDEF")
with open("m.txt", "r+") as f:
    f.write("xy")
with open("m.txt") as f:
    print(f.read())
questions.explanation_en: Mode 'r+' opens an existing file for reading and writing without truncating it, with the pointer at the start. Writing xy overwrites the first two characters, leaving xyCDEF. 'w+' would have erased the file, and 'a+' would have appended.

Static methods are not overridden but hidden; the call obj.s() is resolved at compile time from the reference type P, giving Ps. The instance method i() is overridden, so the run-time object type Q decides, giving Qi.

this(...) must be the first statement, so Box() calls Box(5), which calls Box(5, 5). The innermost constructor finishes first and prints C, then control returns to print B and then A. w = h = 5, so 25 is printed.

questions.question_en: In an Entity–Relationship diagram, an entity set is drawn as a:
questions.explanation_en: Chen notation uses a rectangle for an entity set, a diamond for a relationship set and an ellipse for an attribute. A double line shows total participation.

questions.question_en: A hub forwards every incoming signal to all of its ports and operates at the ______ layer of the OSI model.
questions.explanation_en: A hub is a multi-port repeater: it regenerates electrical signals without reading addresses, so it belongs to layer 1 and creates one large collision domain.
fact(5) = 5 x 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 120. The base case returns 1 when n is 1 or less.

questions.question_en: A pointer that still points to a memory location that has already been freed is called a:
questions.explanation_en: After free(p), p still holds the old address but the memory is no longer valid; using it is a dangling-pointer bug. A wild pointer is one that was never initialised.

questions.question_en: The naive recursive Fibonacci function  int fib(int n){ if(n <= 1) return n; return fib(n-1) + fib(n-2); }  is called as fib(5). How many calls to fib are made in total, including the first one?
questions.explanation_en: Let C(n) = 1 + C(n − 1) + C(n − 2) with C(0) = C(1) = 1. Then C(2) = 3, C(3) = 5, C(4) = 9, C(5) = 1 + 9 + 5 = 15. This exponential growth is why memoisation or iteration is preferred.

questions.question_en: A weighted undirected graph has edges A–B (4), A–C (1), B–C (2), B–D (5), C–D (8) and A–D (7). What is the total weight of its minimum spanning tree found by Kruskal's algorithm?
questions.explanation_en: Sort edges by weight and add those that do not form a cycle: A–C (1), B–C (2), skip A–B (4, would close A–B–C), B–D (5). Three edges join four vertices: 1 + 2 + 5 = 8.

questions.question_en: Fourth Normal Form (4NF) is concerned with removing:
questions.explanation_en: 4NF requires that every non-trivial multivalued dependency X →→ Y has X as a super key. Partial and transitive dependencies are handled by 2NF and 3NF; join dependencies belong to 5NF.

questions.question_en: In a 10 × 10 lower-triangular matrix (all elements above the main diagonal are zero), how many elements can be non-zero?
questions.explanation_en: Row i (1 to 10) has i possibly non-zero elements, so the total is 1 + 2 + … + 10 = n(n + 1)/2 = 10 × 11 / 2 = 55. Storing only these saves almost half the memory.

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

sq = lambda x: x * x
print(sq(4) + sq(3))
questions.explanation_en: A lambda is an anonymous one-line function. sq(4) = 16 and sq(3) = 9, so the sum is 25.
a = 1, b = 3 (positional overrides the default), args = (4, 5) with length 2, kwargs = {'x': 6} with length 1. Total 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 7.
The recursive call happens BEFORE the printf, so printing is done while the calls unwind: the last node prints first. This prints the list in reverse without changing it.

questions.question_en: The File Allocation Table (FAT) used by MS-DOS and many USB drives is a variation of which allocation method?
questions.explanation_en: FAT keeps the 'next block' pointers of linked allocation together in one table at the start of the volume instead of inside each data block, which speeds up random access.

questions.question_en: Keys 45, 20, 60, 10, 30, 50, 70, 25 are inserted into an empty BST. The root 45 is then deleted, replacing it with its INORDER SUCCESSOR. What is the new root?
questions.explanation_en: A node with two children is replaced by the smallest key of its right subtree: from 60 go left to 50, which has no left child → 50 becomes the root. 30 is the inorder PREDECESSOR (largest key in the left subtree).

questions.question_en: The main purpose of normalisation in database design is to:

options.en: Reduce redundancy and avoid insertion, deletion and update anomalies
Increase the speed of every query

questions.explanation_en: Normalisation decomposes relations to eliminate redundant data and the anomalies it causes. It can actually slow some queries because more joins are needed, which is why denormalisation is sometimes used for reporting.

questions.question_en: In the worst case, how many swaps does selection sort perform on an array of n elements?
questions.explanation_en: Selection sort performs at most one swap per pass and there are n − 1 passes, so swaps are O(n) even though comparisons are O(n²). This makes it useful when writes are expensive.

questions.question_en: Binary search for 38 is performed on the sorted array [3, 8, 12, 17, 23, 31, 38, 45, 52] (indices 0–8, mid = ⌊(low + high)/2⌋). Which elements are compared with 38, in order?
questions.explanation_en: low = 0, high = 8 → mid = 4 (23); 38 > 23 so low = 5. mid = ⌊(5 + 8)/2⌋ = 6 → 38, found after 2 comparisons.

questions.question_en: Attempting to perform a POP operation on an empty stack results in:
questions.explanation_en: Underflow means removing from an empty structure; overflow means pushing onto a full (fixed-size) stack. A correct implementation checks top == −1 before popping.

questions.question_en: Compared with unshielded twisted pair (UTP), shielded twisted pair (STP):

options.en: Uses glass fibres instead of copper
Has a metallic foil or braid that gives better protection against EMI but makes it costlier and bulkier

questions.explanation_en: STP adds a shield around the pairs to resist electromagnetic interference, at the cost of price, weight and ease of installation. UTP is the usual choice for office LANs.

questions.question_en: What does SELECT ROUND(15.678, 1), TRUNCATE(15.678, 1); return in MySQL?
questions.explanation_en: ROUND rounds to the nearest value at 1 decimal (15.678 → 15.7); TRUNCATE simply cuts off digits after the first decimal (15.6) without rounding.

questions.question_en: Which integrity rule states that no primary-key attribute can be NULL?
questions.explanation_en: Entity integrity guarantees every tuple is identifiable. Referential integrity concerns foreign keys matching a referenced primary key, and domain integrity concerns valid attribute values.

questions.question_en: A recursive function that has no base case (terminating condition) will usually result in:
questions.explanation_en: Without a base case the function keeps calling itself, each call adding a frame to the call stack until memory is exhausted. The compiler cannot detect this at compile time.

questions.question_en: What is the time complexity of accessing the element at a given index i of an array?
questions.explanation_en: Because elements are stored contiguously, the address is computed directly as base + i × size, so access takes constant time regardless of n.

questions.question_en: In C++, members of a class that are declared without any access specifier are, by default:
questions.explanation_en: In a C++ class the default access is private; in a struct it is public. This is the only real difference between class and struct in C++.

questions.question_en: A hash table of size 10 uses h(k) = k mod 10 with quadratic probing: the i-th probe is (h(k) + i²) mod 10. Keys 23, 43, 13 and 33 are inserted in this order. At which index is 33 stored?
questions.explanation_en: 23 → 3. 43 → 3 busy, 3 + 1 = 4. 13 → 3, 4 busy, 3 + 4 = 7. 33 → 3, 4, 7 busy, then (3 + 9) mod 10 = 2 → index 2. Linear probing would have put 33 at 5.

questions.question_en: What is the maximum number of edges in a simple undirected graph with 8 vertices?
questions.explanation_en: Each pair of distinct vertices can have at most one edge: 8C2 = 8 × 7 / 2 = 28. 56 would be the maximum for a simple DIRECTED graph.

questions.question_en: Reversing a singly linked list of n nodes in place (by changing the next pointers with three pointer variables) requires:

options.en: O(log n) time and O(1) extra space
O(n²) time and O(1) extra space
O(n) time and O(1) extra space
O(n) time and O(n) extra space

questions.explanation_en: One pass reverses each link using prev, curr and next pointers, so time is linear and only a constant number of extra pointers is used. A recursive or stack-based reversal would use O(n) extra space.

questions.question_en: Using the Master theorem, the recurrence T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n solves to:
questions.explanation_en: Here a = 4, b = 2, f(n) = n, and n^(log_b a) = n^(log₂ 4) = n². Since f(n) = n grows polynomially slower than n², case 1 applies: T(n) = Θ(n²). T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n (merge sort) would give Θ(n log n).

questions.question_en: Which statement about the Rapid Application Development (RAD) model is correct?

options.en: It is the same as the classical waterfall model
It relies on component reuse and short time-boxed cycles, so it needs highly skilled developers and active users
It forbids any user involvement until final delivery
It is ideal for large, high-risk projects using new technology

questions.explanation_en: RAD (James Martin) achieves speed through reusable components, time-boxing (typically 60–90 days) and strong user involvement; it is unsuitable for high technical risk or when the system cannot be modularised.

questions.question_en: A data structure in which elements can be inserted and deleted at BOTH ends but not in the middle is called a:
questions.explanation_en: A deque (double-ended queue) supports insertion and deletion at both front and rear. A stack and a simple queue each restrict operations to particular ends.

questions.question_en: An entity type that has no key attribute of its own and depends on an owner entity for identification is a:
questions.explanation_en: A weak entity (e.g., Dependent of an Employee) is identified by a partial key plus the owner's key; it is drawn as a double rectangle with a double-diamond identifying relationship.
range(1, 10, 3) starts at 1 and adds 3 each time while the value is below 10: 1, 4, 7. The stop value 10 is excluded.

questions.question_en: Which MySQL function returns the current date and time together?
questions.explanation_en: NOW() (also SYSDATE(), CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) returns date and time, e.g., '2026-10-19 10:30:00'. CURDATE() returns only the date and CURTIME() only the time.

questions.question_en: The numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 are pushed onto a stack in this order, and pops may be performed at any time. Which output sequence is IMPOSSIBLE?
questions.explanation_en: To output 3 first, 1 and 2 must already be on the stack with 2 on top, so 2 must come out before 1; '3, 1' is therefore impossible. 2,4,3,1 = push1 push2 pop push3 push4 pop pop pop; the other two are similarly achievable.

questions.question_en: Which SQL isolation level is the strictest and prevents dirty reads, non-repeatable reads and phantom reads?
questions.explanation_en: SERIALIZABLE forbids all three anomalies. READ UNCOMMITTED allows all; READ COMMITTED prevents dirty reads only; standard REPEATABLE READ still permits phantoms (InnoDB's implementation largely prevents them, but the standard does not).

questions.question_en: Which of the following lists functions in correct INCREASING order of growth rate?

options.en: log n < n < n log n < n² < 2ⁿ
log n < n < n² < n log n < 2ⁿ
log n < n log n < n < n² < 2ⁿ
n < log n < n log n < 2ⁿ < n²

questions.explanation_en: Logarithmic grows slowest, then linear, then n log n, then polynomial n², and exponential 2ⁿ eventually overtakes every polynomial.

tests.description: 50 questions, Computer Science only, exam pattern.

tests.title: Section Test — Computer Science 2
tests.subject: Computer Science

questions.question_en:
What does the following Python code print?

a = [3, 1, 2]
b = a.sort()
print(a, b)
questions.explanation_en: list.sort() sorts the list in place and returns None, so b is None and a becomes [1, 2, 3]. The built-in sorted(a) would instead return a new sorted list and leave a unchanged.

questions.question_en: An array A[1..6][1..8] with 2-byte elements is stored in COLUMN-major order from base address 2000. The address of A[4][5] is:
Tasks have dependencies A → B, A → C, B → D and C → D (X → Y means X must come before Y). Which of the following is a valid topological order?
questions.explanation_en: A must be first (no incoming edges) and D last (it depends on B and C); B and C may come in either order. Every other option places some vertex before one of its prerequisites.

questions.question_en: An input field accepts ages from 18 to 60 (inclusive). Which set of values best represents boundary value analysis test inputs?
questions.explanation_en: Boundary value analysis tests just below, at and just above each boundary: min−1, min, min+1 and max−1, max, max+1, giving 17, 18, 19, 59, 60, 61. Errors cluster at boundaries, such as writing 'less than' where 'less than or equal to' was needed.

questions.question_en: A relation is in BCNF if for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y:
questions.explanation_en: BCNF requires every determinant to be a super key. 3NF is weaker: it also allows X → Y when Y is a prime attribute, which is why every BCNF relation is in 3NF but not vice versa.

questions.question_en: A candidate key that is not selected as the primary key is called a/an:
questions.explanation_en: Candidate keys not chosen as primary key are alternate keys. For example, if Student has Roll_No and Aadhaar as candidate keys and Roll_No is the primary key, Aadhaar is an alternate key.

questions.question_en: An inner <div id="in"> is nested inside <div id="out">. Both have click listeners added with addEventListener (default options) that log their id. When the inner div is clicked, what is logged?
questions.explanation_en: By default listeners run in the bubbling phase: the event is handled first at the target (in) and then bubbles up through its ancestors (out). Calling event.stopPropagation() in the inner handler would stop it reaching out.

questions.question_en: The tendency of occupied slots to form long consecutive runs, which slows down insertion and search, is called primary clustering. It is mainly caused by:
questions.explanation_en: With linear probing any key hashing into a run lands at its end and lengthens it. Quadratic probing removes primary clustering (but suffers secondary clustering) and double hashing reduces both.

questions.question_en: A host has the address 10.1.1.130 with mask 255.255.255.128. What is the broadcast address of its subnet?
questions.explanation_en: Block size = 256 − 128 = 128, so the subnets are .0–.127 and .128–.255. Host .130 lies in the second block, whose last address 10.1.1.255 is the broadcast; .128 is that subnet's network address.
The condition i is true while i is non-zero. Values 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 are printed; when i becomes 0 the loop stops.

questions.question_en:
What is printed by the following C statement?

printf("%d", strcmp("abc", "abd") < 0);
questions.explanation_en: strcmp returns a negative value when the first string is lexicographically smaller: c (99) < d (100), so strcmp is negative and the comparison < 0 yields 1 (true).

questions.question_en: In an AVL tree, the balance factor (height of left subtree − height of right subtree) of every node must be:
questions.explanation_en: An AVL tree is height-balanced: subtree heights may differ by at most 1. When an insertion or deletion makes a balance factor ±2, rotations (LL, RR, LR, RL) restore balance, keeping height O(log n).

questions.question_en: Which data structure does the system use to keep track of active function calls during recursion?
questions.explanation_en: Each call's parameters, local variables and return address form an activation record pushed on the call stack; the most recent call returns first (LIFO).

questions.question_en: A feasibility study that checks whether the expected benefits of the proposed system outweigh its costs is called:
questions.explanation_en: Economic feasibility is a cost–benefit analysis. Technical feasibility checks whether the technology and skills exist, and operational feasibility checks whether users will actually accept and use the system.

questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?

x = 10
def f():
    x = 5
    return x
print(f(), x)
questions.explanation_en: Assigning x inside f creates a new local variable that shadows the global. f() returns 5, while the global x is untouched and still 10.

options.en: Compilation error: + cannot be applied to class objects

questions.explanation_en: The overloaded operator+ adds component-wise. p + q gives (4, 6); adding p again gives (5, 8). Operator overloading is a form of compile-time polymorphism.

questions.question_en: Relation R(A, B, C) has functional dependencies AB → C and C → B. Candidate keys are AB and AC. The highest normal form of R is:
questions.explanation_en: C → B has a determinant (C) that is not a super key, so BCNF fails. But B is a prime attribute (part of key AB), which 3NF permits, so R is in 3NF. This is the classic 3NF-but-not-BCNF example.

questions.question_en: An undirected graph has edges A–B, A–C, B–D, C–D, C–E, D–F and E–F. Starting from A and always visiting neighbours in alphabetical order, what is the DFS order?

options.en: A C E F D B
A B C D E F
A B D C E F
A B D F E C

questions.explanation_en: A → B (first neighbour) → D (B's only unvisited neighbour) → C (D's neighbours B, C, F: C first) → E (C's unvisited neighbour) → F. A B C D E F is the BFS order from A.

questions.question_en: Why is binary search NOT efficient on a sorted singly linked list?

options.en: Linked lists cannot store sorted data
The middle element cannot be reached in constant time because there is no random access
