questions.explanation_en: 'Se adhik' alone marks comparison; adding -tar or -tam is double comparison.
questions.explanation_hi: दो के बीच तुलना में 'से अधिक' पर्याप्त है; 'अधिक' के साथ 'तर' जोड़ना दोहरी तुलना है। 'सबसे' या 'तम' तीन या अधिक की तुलना में आते हैं।

questions.question_en: 'काली घटा का घमंड घटा' — इस पंक्ति में मुख्य रूप से कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.question_hi: 'काली घटा का घमंड घटा' — इस पंक्ति में मुख्य रूप से कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation_en: 'Ghata' is repeated with two meanings (clouds, decreased), so it is Yamak.
questions.explanation_hi: 'घटा' शब्द दो बार आया है — पहली बार 'बादलों का समूह' और दूसरी बार 'कम हुआ' अर्थ में। भिन्न अर्थों में शब्द की आवृत्ति के कारण यमक अलंकार है ('घ' की आवृत्ति से अनुप्रास भी है, पर मुख्य यमक है)।

questions.question_en: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्दालंकार है?
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्दालंकार है?
questions.explanation_en: Shlesh depends on the word itself, so it is a shabdalankar; the rest are arthalankars.
questions.explanation_hi: शब्दालंकार में चमत्कार शब्द पर निर्भर होता है — अनुप्रास, यमक, श्लेष इसके मुख्य भेद हैं। उपमा, रूपक और उत्प्रेक्षा अर्थालंकार हैं क्योंकि उनका सौंदर्य अर्थ पर टिका है।

questions.subtopic: अनेक शब्दों के लिए एक शब्द
questions.question_en: 'जिसका कोई शत्रु पैदा ही न हुआ हो' — इसके लिए एक शब्द चुनिए।
questions.question_hi: 'जिसका कोई शत्रु पैदा ही न हुआ हो' — इसके लिए एक शब्द चुनिए।
questions.explanation_en: One with no enemy ever born = ajatshatru.
questions.explanation_hi: अजातशत्रु = जिसका शत्रु जन्मा ही न हो (अ + जात + शत्रु)। 'शत्रुहीन' शाब्दिक अनुवाद है, मानक एक-शब्द 'अजातशत्रु' है, जो युधिष्ठिर का विशेषण भी है।

questions.question_en: 'शरणागत' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.question_hi: 'शरणागत' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation_en: Sharanagat = come to refuge; accusative marker dropped — karm tatpurush.
questions.explanation_hi: शरणागत = शरण को आया हुआ। 'को' (कर्म कारक) विभक्ति का लोप है, अतः कर्म तत्पुरुष समास है।

questions.question_en: 'इम्तिहान' के अर्थ वाले तत्सम शब्द की शुद्ध वर्तनी चुनिए।
questions.question_hi: 'इम्तिहान' के अर्थ वाले तत्सम शब्द की शुद्ध वर्तनी चुनिए।
questions.explanation_en: Pari + iksha = pariksha with a long 'ee'.
questions.explanation_hi: परि + ईक्षा = परीक्षा (दीर्घ संधि), इसलिए 'री' दीर्घ होता है और 'क्ष' संयुक्ताक्षर आता है।

questions.question_en: 'माता-पिता' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.question_hi: 'माता-पिता' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation_en: Both members are equally principal (mother and father) — dvandva.
questions.explanation_hi: माता-पिता = माता और पिता। दोनों पद प्रधान हैं और बीच में 'और' का लोप है, अतः द्वंद्व समास है।

questions.question_en: 'आजन्म' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.question_hi: 'आजन्म' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation_en: Aajanma = since birth; indeclinable compound — avyayibhav.
questions.explanation_hi: आजन्म = जन्म से लेकर (जन्म पर्यंत)। 'आ' उपसर्ग/अव्यय पहला पद है और समस्त पद क्रिया-विशेषण की तरह प्रयुक्त होता है, अतः अव्ययीभाव समास है।

questions.question_en: 'दयालु' शब्द में कौन-सा प्रत्यय है?
questions.question_hi: 'दयालु' शब्द में कौन-सा प्रत्यय है?
questions.explanation_en: Dayalu = daya + aalu; 'aalu' forms adjectives from nouns.
questions.explanation_hi: दयालु = दया + आलु। 'आलु' तद्धित प्रत्यय है जो संज्ञा से विशेषण बनाता है, जैसे कृपालु, श्रद्धालु, ईर्ष्यालु।

questions.question_en: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'हाथी' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'हाथी' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?
questions.explanation_en: Kesari means lion; gaj, kunjar and matang mean elephant.
questions.explanation_hi: गज, कुंजर, मतंग, हस्ती और करी हाथी के पर्यायवाची हैं। 'केसरी' सिंह का पर्यायवाची है।

tests.description: 15 questions, Hindi Language only, exam pattern.

tests.title: Section Test — Teaching Methodology 1
tests.subject: Teaching Methodology

questions.question_en: NEP 2020 reaffirms that public investment in education by the Centre and States together should reach:
questions.explanation_en: NEP 2020 commits to raising combined public expenditure on education to 6% of GDP, a target first set by the Kothari Commission. Current spending is around 4% of GDP.

questions.question_en: A teacher wants students to see, line by line, how variables and the call stack change while a recursive Python function runs. The most useful ICT tool is:

options.en: A word processor with track changes
A presentation with a single static slide
An online code visualiser such as Python Tutor

questions.explanation_en: Code visualisers step through execution and draw frames, variables and the stack, making abstract recursion concrete. Charts, word processors and static slides cannot show program state as it changes.

questions.question_en: 'The student will be able to write a Python function that returns the factorial of a given number.' This instructional objective belongs to which domain of educational objectives?
questions.explanation_en: Writing a function requires understanding and applying knowledge, i.e. intellectual activity, which is the cognitive domain. Psychomotor covers physical skills such as typing speed; affective covers attitudes and values.

questions.question_en: Before teaching 'linked lists', a teacher gives a brief overview relating them to arrays that students already know. According to David Ausubel, this introductory material is called a/an:
questions.explanation_en: Ausubel's meaningful reception learning uses advance organisers to link new content to existing cognitive structure. Discovery tasks belong to Bruner's approach.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is the most appropriate first response when a student is found accessing a non-educational website during a lab class?

options.en: Permanently ban the student from the lab
Calmly redirect the student to the task and remind the class of the acceptable-use policy

questions.explanation_en: Effective lab management uses a graded response: a calm, low-key redirection and reference to pre-agreed rules handles most incidents. Ignoring reinforces misbehaviour, while extreme punishment is disproportionate.

questions.question_en: Bruner's three modes of representation in the correct developmental order are:
questions.explanation_en: Bruner proposed enactive (action-based), iconic (image-based) and symbolic (language/symbol-based) representation. A CS teacher may first let students physically sort cards (enactive), then show flowcharts (iconic), then write code (symbolic).

questions.question_en:
Which of the following statements about a unit plan and a lesson plan is correct?
I. A unit plan covers a larger chunk of content and spans several periods.
II. A lesson plan is prepared first and unit plans are derived from it.
questions.explanation_en: A unit plan (H. C. Morrison) organises a related body of content over several lessons; daily lesson plans are then derived from the unit plan, not the other way round. So only I is correct.

questions.question_en: In a micro-teaching session the usual duration of the teaching phase and the number of pupils are approximately:
questions.explanation_en: Micro-teaching scales down the class size to 5–10 pupils, time to about 5–10 minutes (often 6 minutes) and content to a single concept so that a single skill can be practised and observed.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a limitation of the lecture method in teaching Computer Science?

options.en: It keeps the learner passive and gives little scope for hands-on practice
It is not suitable for large classes
It cannot cover a large syllabus in limited time
It cannot be used to introduce a new topic

questions.explanation_en: The lecture method is economical for large classes and wide syllabi and is fine for introductions; its real weakness is passive listening with no activity, which is a serious drawback for a skill-based subject like CS.

questions.question_en: The National Education Policy 2020 replaces the 10+2 school structure with the:
questions.explanation_en: NEP 2020 proposes 5+3+3+4: Foundational (3 years pre-primary + Classes 1–2), Preparatory (3–5), Middle (6–8) and Secondary (9–12), covering ages 3–18.

questions.question_en: NEP 2020 recommends that coding be introduced to students from which class onwards?
questions.explanation_en: NEP 2020 (para 4.25) states that coding will be introduced at the Middle Stage, i.e. from Class 6, along with vocational exposure and 'bagless' internship days.

questions.question_en: Micro-teaching was first developed at Stanford University in 1963 by:
questions.explanation_en: Dwight W. Allen and his associates (Acheson, Bush) developed micro-teaching at Stanford in 1963 as a scaled-down teaching encounter for practising single skills.

questions.question_en: Bloom's taxonomy of educational objectives (1956) classifies objectives into how many domains?
questions.explanation_en: Bloom and co-workers proposed three domains: cognitive (Bloom, 1956), affective (Krathwohl, 1964) and psychomotor (Simpson/Harrow/Dave). Six is the number of levels within the cognitive domain, a common confusion.

questions.question_en: A CS teacher records a video explaining 'normalisation' for students to watch at home and uses class time for solving problems and clearing doubts. This approach is known as:
questions.explanation_en: In a flipped classroom direct instruction is shifted outside the class through videos and class time is used for higher-order activities, practice and interaction. It is a form of blended learning.

questions.question_en: According to NEP 2020, the new national assessment centre to set standards for student assessment is called:
questions.explanation_en: PARAKH (Performance Assessment, Review and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development) was proposed by NEP 2020 and set up under NCERT in 2023. NISHTHA is a teacher training programme and NIPUN Bharat is the FLN mission.

questions.question_en: In the revised Bloom's taxonomy (Anderson and Krathwohl, 2001), the highest level of the cognitive domain is:
questions.explanation_en: The revised taxonomy reorders the top levels to Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create, with 'Create' at the top. 'Synthesis' was the fifth level in the original 1956 version and is replaced by Create.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is the most important objective of teaching Computer Science at the secondary stage?

options.en: Memorising the syntax of several languages
Developing computational thinking and problem-solving ability
Preparing students only for board examinations
Making every student a professional programmer

questions.explanation_en: NCF and the CBSE Class 11–12 CS curriculum state that the core aim is computational thinking (decomposition, abstraction, algorithms) and logical problem solving. Syntax memorisation and professional programming are narrow, instrumental aims.

questions.question_en: Which teaching method is most suitable for teaching the procedure of installing an operating system to a class of 40 students with only two computers?
questions.explanation_en: In the demonstration method the teacher performs the activity while students observe, which suits limited equipment and a procedural skill. Laboratory/heuristic methods need every student to work hands-on.

questions.question_en: According to Piaget, a child who can think logically about concrete objects but not about abstract hypotheses is in the:
questions.explanation_en: The concrete operational stage (about 7–11 years) brings conservation, reversibility and logical thought about concrete things; abstract, hypothetical reasoning appears in the formal operational stage (11+).

questions.question_en: The five formal steps of lesson planning — Preparation, Presentation, Association (Comparison), Generalisation and Application — were given by followers of:
questions.explanation_en: These are the Herbartian steps, formulated by Herbart's followers (Ziller and Rein) from his four steps. Dewey is associated with the project/problem method and Montessori with sense training.

tests.description: 20 questions, Teaching Methodology only, exam pattern.

tests.title: Section Test — Teaching Methodology 2
tests.subject: Teaching Methodology

questions.question_en: NEP 2020 recommends that the medium of instruction, wherever possible, should be the home language/mother tongue at least till:

options.en: Class 5, preferably till Class 8 and beyond

questions.explanation_en: Para 4.11 of NEP 2020 says the medium of instruction will be the home language/mother tongue/local language until at least Grade 5, but preferably till Grade 8 and beyond, with the three-language formula retained flexibly.

questions.question_en: Evaluation carried out during the teaching–learning process to give feedback and improve learning is called:
questions.explanation_en: Formative evaluation (Scriven, 1967) happens during instruction and is 'assessment for learning'. Summative is at the end for grading; diagnostic identifies specific learning difficulties; placement happens before instruction.

questions.question_en: DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) is best described as:

options.en: A satellite television channel for Class 12
A university-level MOOC platform with credit transfer
A hardware scheme for distributing laptops to teachers
A national platform for school education with QR-coded energised textbooks and teacher resources

questions.explanation_en: DIKSHA, launched in 2017 by MoE/NCERT, hosts e-content linked to textbook QR codes, teacher training courses (NISHTHA) and state-wise resources. SWAYAM is the MOOC platform and PM e-VIDYA/SWAYAM Prabha are TV channels.

questions.question_en: Edgar Dale's 'Cone of Experience' places which of the following at the base (most concrete) level?
questions.explanation_en: Dale's cone runs from the most concrete direct purposeful experiences at the base to the most abstract verbal symbols at the apex. Students learn and retain more from concrete experiences.

questions.question_en: Under the CCE scheme introduced by CBSE in 2009, 'Continuous' and 'Comprehensive' respectively refer to:

options.en: Regular unit tests only; scholastic subjects only
Assessment spread over the whole year; coverage of both scholastic and co-scholastic areas
Daily homework; coverage of all textbook chapters
Term-end examination; covering the complete syllabus

questions.explanation_en: In CCE 'continuous' means assessment is regular and integrated with teaching (formative and summative across the year) and 'comprehensive' means it covers scholastic (academic) as well as co-scholastic (life skills, attitudes, co-curricular) growth.

questions.question_en: Programmed instruction and the 'teaching machine', in which content is broken into small steps with immediate reinforcement, are based on the work of:
questions.explanation_en: Skinner's operant conditioning led to linear programmed instruction: small frames, active response and immediate reinforcement. This idea is also behind many e-learning drill modules.

questions.question_en: The TPACK framework (Mishra and Koehler) suggests that effective technology integration requires the teacher to combine:
questions.explanation_en: TPACK = Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge; it extends Shulman's PCK by adding technology, emphasising that knowing a tool alone is not enough — the teacher must know how it fits the content and the pedagogy.

questions.question_en: A teacher first shows students several Python programs in which a 'for' loop iterates over a list and then lets them frame the general rule of how iteration works. The teacher is using:
questions.explanation_en: Moving from specific examples to a general rule is induction. The deductive method would state the rule first and then apply it to examples.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is the best example of a diagnostic test in Computer Science?

options.en: A weekly quiz to award marks
An entrance test for admission to Class 11
A test to find out exactly which steps in writing a SQL JOIN a student gets wrong
A board examination at the end of Class 12

questions.explanation_en: A diagnostic test locates the specific weaknesses behind a learning difficulty so that remedial teaching can be planned. Board examinations are summative; entrance tests are for placement/selection.

questions.question_en: The most effective way to prevent loss of practical time in a school computer lab is to:

options.en: Let students log in whenever they wish
Allow only the brightest students to use computers
Prepare and test the required software and files before the period starts
Keep the lab locked except during examinations

questions.explanation_en: Advance preparation (booting systems, checking software, loading sample files) is a proactive management practice that avoids wastage and indiscipline. The other options either waste time or deny access.

questions.question_en:
Which statement about general aims and specific (instructional) objectives of teaching Computer Science is correct?
I. Aims are long-term and broad; objectives are short-term and achievable in a lesson.
II. Objectives are written in terms of observable student behaviour.
questions.explanation_en: Aims (e.g. digital literacy for citizenship) are broad goals of the subject, while instructional objectives are specific, measurable statements of what a learner will do after a lesson, written as observable behaviour (Mager). Both statements are correct.

questions.question_en: In a computer lab with 20 computers and 40 students, the most practical seating arrangement for a programming practical is:

options.en: Cancel the practical until more computers arrive
Pair programming — two students per computer with alternating 'driver' and 'navigator' roles
Each student works for 5 minutes and leaves
Let the first 20 students work and the rest watch from the back

questions.explanation_en: Pair programming keeps all students actively engaged, encourages peer learning and is a recognised practice in CS pedagogy. Passive watching or very short turns waste the period.

questions.question_en: 'Developing the ability to type a program accurately and operate the keyboard and mouse efficiently' is an objective of which domain?
questions.explanation_en: Manual and physical skills such as keyboarding, handling hardware and connecting cables fall in the psychomotor domain (Simpson's taxonomy). Cognitive deals with knowledge, affective with attitudes.

questions.question_en: For good ergonomics in a school computer lab, a monitor should be placed so that:

options.en: Its top is well above the student's head
It faces a bright window directly behind it
It is as close to the eyes as possible
Its top is at or slightly below eye level and about an arm's length away

questions.explanation_en: Standard ergonomic guidance places the top of the screen at or just below eye level at roughly 50–70 cm, reducing neck strain and eye fatigue. Glare from a window behind the screen strains the eyes.

questions.question_en: A term-end examination conducted to award grades and decide promotion to the next class is an example of:
questions.explanation_en: Summative evaluation comes at the end of a unit, term or course to judge and certify achievement. Formative evaluation happens during teaching to improve learning, not to certify it.

questions.question_en: SWAYAM PRABHA, an ICT initiative of the Ministry of Education, is:

options.en: A portal for online teacher recruitment
A group of DTH channels telecasting educational programmes 24x7
A digital library of university theses

questions.explanation_en: SWAYAM PRABHA is a group of DTH educational TV channels (34 originally, expanded under PM eVIDYA) broadcasting curriculum content round the clock. Theses are hosted on Shodhganga, not SWAYAM PRABHA.

questions.question_en: Which sequence of steps is correct for the project method?

options.en: Providing a situation → Choosing the project → Planning → Executing → Evaluating → Recording
Planning → Providing a situation → Choosing the project → Executing → Evaluating → Recording
Executing → Planning → Choosing → Providing a situation → Evaluating → Recording
Choosing the project → Providing a situation → Executing → Planning → Recording → Evaluating

questions.explanation_en: The teacher first creates a situation that raises a need, students choose and purpose the project, plan it, execute it, evaluate the outcome and finally record the whole work in a project report.

questions.question_en: In Dewey's problem-solving method, the correct sequence of steps is:

options.en: Formulating hypotheses → Sensing the problem → Defining the problem → Conclusion → Testing
Sensing the problem → Defining the problem → Formulating hypotheses → Collecting and testing data → Drawing conclusions
Collecting data → Sensing the problem → Hypothesis → Verification → Defining the problem
Defining the problem → Sensing the problem → Conclusion → Hypotheses → Testing

questions.explanation_en: Dewey's reflective thinking proceeds from feeling a difficulty, locating and defining it, suggesting possible solutions (hypotheses), reasoning out and testing them with data, and finally accepting or rejecting the hypothesis.

questions.question_en: Thorndike's 'law of effect' implies that a Computer Science teacher should:

options.en: Teach only when students are physically ready
Ensure that a student's correct response is followed by a satisfying result such as praise or a working program
Make students practise the same program repeatedly without feedback
Present abstract concepts before concrete examples

questions.explanation_en: Law of effect: responses followed by satisfaction are strengthened and those followed by annoyance are weakened. Immediate positive feedback (a running program, praise) strengthens the correct behaviour. Repetition without feedback relates to the law of exercise alone.

questions.question_en: A student stares at a failing loop for a long time and then suddenly 'sees' the complete solution at once. This type of learning was explained by:
questions.explanation_en: Kohler (Gestalt school) showed with the chimpanzee Sultan that learners may perceive the whole relationship suddenly ('aha' moment). Trial and error involves gradual, random attempts instead.

tests.description: 20 questions, Teaching Methodology only, exam pattern.

tests.title: Chapter Test — Advanced Maths & Data Interpretation
tests.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability

questions.question_en: A ladder 20 m long leans against a vertical wall and makes an angle of 60° with the ground. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation_en: Height = ladder × sin 60° = 20 × √3/2 = 10√3 m (≈ 17.32 m). 10 m is the distance of the foot from the wall (20 cos 60°).

questions.question_en: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral in which ∠A = 70° and ∠B = 95°. The measure of ∠C is:
questions.explanation_en: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: ∠C = 180° − ∠A = 180° − 70° = 110°. (∠D = 180° − 95° = 85°, the trap answer.)

questions.question_en: If x = 2 + √3, then x² + 1/x² equals:
If x + 1/x = 3, then x³ + 1/x³ equals:
The mean of five numbers is 20. When one number is removed, the mean of the remaining four numbers becomes 18. The number removed is:
questions.explanation_en: Sum of five = 5 × 20 = 100; sum of four = 4 × 18 = 72. Removed number = 100 − 72 = 28.

questions.question_en:
The table shows the production (in thousand units) of three items by a company.
Year | Laptops | Tablets | Printers
2020 | 40 | 25 | 15
2021 | 45 | 30 | 20
2022 | 50 | 35 | 18
2023 | 60 | 32 | 24
2024 | 55 | 40 | 30
What is the average annual production of tablets over the five years?
questions.explanation_en: Total tablets = 25 + 30 + 35 + 32 + 40 = 162 thousand. Average = 162 / 5 = 32.4 thousand units.

questions.question_en:
The table shows the number of students who appeared and passed in a Computer Science examination from five schools.
School | Appeared | Passed
P | 240 | 180
Q | 300 | 255
R | 180 | 117
S | 360 | 288
T | 220 | 198
In how many schools is the pass percentage higher than the overall pass percentage of all five schools combined?
questions.explanation_en: Overall = 1038/1300 ≈ 79.85%. School pass %: P 75, Q 85, R 65, S 80, T 90. Q, S and T exceed 79.85%, so the answer is 3 (S just qualifies at 80%).

questions.question_en:
The table shows the number of students who appeared and passed in a Computer Science examination from five schools.
School | Appeared | Passed
P | 240 | 180
Q | 300 | 255
R | 180 | 117
S | 360 | 288
T | 220 | 198
What is the average number of students who passed per school?
questions.explanation_en: Total passed = 1038. Average = 1038 / 5 = 207.6. 260 is the average number appeared (1300/5).

questions.question_en: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 12 cm. The perimeter of the rhombus is:
questions.explanation_en: The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so side = √(8² + 6²) = 10 cm and perimeter = 4 × 10 = 40 cm. 96 cm² is its area (½ × 16 × 12).

questions.question_en: The curved surface area of a right circular cone of base radius 6 cm and height 8 cm is:
questions.explanation_en: Slant height l = √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm. Curved surface area = πrl = π × 6 × 10 = 60π cm². Using the height instead of the slant height gives the wrong 48π.

questions.question_en: If sin 3θ = cos(θ − 6°), where 3θ and (θ − 6°) are acute angles, then θ equals:
questions.explanation_en: sin A = cos B with both acute means A + B = 90°. So 3θ + θ − 6° = 90° → 4θ = 96° → θ = 24°.

questions.question_en: The value of tan 10° × tan 20° × tan 70° × tan 80° is:
questions.explanation_en: tan 80° = cot 10° and tan 70° = cot 20°. So the product = (tan 10° cot 10°)(tan 20° cot 20°) = 1 × 1 = 1.

questions.question_en: The median of the data 7, 3, 9, 4, 12, 6 is:
questions.explanation_en: Arrange in order: 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 12. With an even count (6), median = average of the 3rd and 4th values = (6 + 7)/2 = 6.5. 6.83 is the mean, not the median.

questions.question_en:
The table shows the production (in thousand units) of three items by a company.
Year | Laptops | Tablets | Printers
2020 | 40 | 25 | 15
2021 | 45 | 30 | 20
2022 | 50 | 35 | 18
2023 | 60 | 32 | 24
2024 | 55 | 40 | 30
In which year did printers form the highest percentage of the company's total production in that year?
If a − b = 3 and a³ − b³ = 117, then the value of ab is:
questions.explanation_en: a³ − b³ = (a − b)³ + 3ab(a − b). So 117 = 27 + 9ab → 9ab = 90 → ab = 10. (Check: a = 5, b = 2.)

questions.question_en: The areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio 16 : 25. The ratio of their corresponding altitudes is:
questions.explanation_en: For similar triangles, ratio of areas = square of the ratio of corresponding sides, altitudes or medians. So altitude ratio = √16 : √25 = 4 : 5.

questions.question_en:
The table shows the production (in thousand units) of three items by a company.
Year | Laptops | Tablets | Printers
2020 | 40 | 25 | 15
2021 | 45 | 30 | 20
2022 | 50 | 35 | 18
2023 | 60 | 32 | 24
2024 | 55 | 40 | 30
By what percent did laptop production increase from 2020 to 2023?
questions.explanation_en: Increase = 60 − 40 = 20 thousand. Percent increase = 20/40 × 100 = 50%. 33.3% wrongly divides by the final value (20/60).

questions.question_en: If the radius of a circle is increased by 10%, its area increases by:
questions.explanation_en: Area ∝ r². New area factor = 1.1² = 1.21, an increase of 21%. Equivalently a + b + ab/100 = 10 + 10 + 1 = 21%.

questions.question_en:
The table shows the production (in thousand units) of three items by a company.
Year | Laptops | Tablets | Printers
2020 | 40 | 25 | 15
2021 | 45 | 30 | 20
2022 | 50 | 35 | 18
2023 | 60 | 32 | 24
2024 | 55 | 40 | 30
What was the total production of all three items in 2022?
questions.explanation_en: 2022 total = 50 + 35 + 18 = 103 thousand units.

questions.question_en: The range of the data 15, 22, 8, 31, 19 is:
questions.explanation_en: Range = largest − smallest = 31 − 8 = 23.

questions.question_en: The standard deviation of the data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 is:
questions.explanation_en: Mean = 30 / 5 = 6. Squared deviations: 16, 4, 0, 4, 16 → sum 40. Variance = 40 / 5 = 8, so SD = √8 = 2√2 ≈ 2.83. 8 is the variance, not the SD.

questions.question_en:
The table shows the number of students who appeared and passed in a Computer Science examination from five schools.
School | Appeared | Passed
P | 240 | 180
Q | 300 | 255
R | 180 | 117
S | 360 | 288
T | 220 | 198
What is the overall pass percentage of all five schools taken together (approximately)?
questions.explanation_en: Total appeared = 240 + 300 + 180 + 360 + 220 = 1300; total passed = 180 + 255 + 117 + 288 + 198 = 1038. 1038/1300 × 100 ≈ 79.85%. Averaging the five percentages (79%) is wrong because school sizes differ.

questions.question_en: The average marks of 30 students was found to be 60. Later it was found that one student's marks were read as 75 instead of 45. The correct average is:
questions.explanation_en: Wrong total = 30 × 60 = 1800. Correct total = 1800 − 75 + 45 = 1770. Correct average = 1770 / 30 = 59.

questions.question_en: The value of sin 30° + cos 60° is:
questions.explanation_en: sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 60° = 1/2, so the sum is 1.

questions.question_en: The value of 2 sin²30° + 3 tan²60° − cos²45° is:

tests.description: 25 questions on Advanced Maths & Data Interpretation (Arithmetical & Numerical Ability).

tests.title: Chapter Test — Arithmetic
tests.subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability

questions.question_en: A tap can fill a tank in 8 hours. What part of the tank is filled in 3 hours?
questions.explanation_en: In 1 hour it fills 1/8 of the tank, so in 3 hours it fills 3/8.

questions.question_en: What is the greatest 4-digit number divisible by 12?
questions.explanation_en: 9999 ÷ 12 leaves remainder 3, so subtract 3: 9996 = 12 × 833.

questions.question_en: The average age of 40 students is 15 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average rises to 16 years. What is the teacher's age?
questions.explanation_en: Total with teacher = 41 × 16 = 656. Total of students = 40 × 15 = 600. Teacher's age = 656 − 600 = 56 years.

questions.question_en: Ramesh walks to school at 4 km/h and reaches 5 minutes late. At 5 km/h he reaches 10 minutes early. What is the distance to school?
questions.explanation_en: The difference in time = 15 min = 1/4 h. d/4 − d/5 = 1/4, so d/20 = 1/4 and d = 5 km.

questions.question_en: A policeman spots a thief 200 m away. The thief starts running at 10 km/h and the policeman chases him at 11 km/h. How far does the thief run before he is caught?
questions.explanation_en: Relative speed = 1 km/h = 1000 m per hour. To close 200 m takes 0.2 hour. The thief runs 10 × 0.2 = 2 km = 2000 m (the policeman runs 2200 m).

questions.question_en: Convert 54 km/h into metres per second.
questions.explanation_en: To convert km/h to m/s multiply by 5/18: 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s.

questions.question_en: A trader sells an article at a loss of 20% for ₹640. What is its cost price?
A and B can complete a work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. They work together and are paid ₹3,000 in all. What is A's share?
questions.explanation_en: Shares are in the ratio of work done = 1/12 : 1/18 = 3 : 2. A gets 3/5 × 3000 = ₹1,800.

questions.question_en: Simplify: 15 + 3 × 12 ÷ 4 − 6
What is the remainder when 2^50 is divided by 7?
questions.explanation_en: 2^3 = 8 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 7. 2^50 = (2^3)^16 × 2^2 = 1 × 4, so the remainder is 4.

questions.question_en: A father is 3 times as old as his son. After 12 years he will be twice as old as his son. What is the present age of the son?
questions.explanation_en: Let the son be S, father 3S. 3S + 12 = 2(S + 12), so S = 12 (father is 36).

questions.question_en: What is the HCF of 2/3, 4/9 and 8/27?
questions.explanation_en: HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators / LCM of denominators = HCF(2, 4, 8) / LCM(3, 9, 27) = 2/27. (8/3 is their LCM.)

questions.question_en: Walking at 5/6 of his usual speed, a man reaches his office 12 minutes late. What is his usual time to reach the office?
questions.explanation_en: At 5/6 speed the time becomes 6/5 of the usual. So 6/5 T − T = T/5 = 12 min, giving T = 60 minutes.

questions.question_en: What is 35% of 240?
The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 12 and 144 respectively. If one number is 48, the other is:
questions.explanation_en: Product of the numbers = HCF × LCM = 12 × 144 = 1728. Other number = 1728 / 48 = 36.

questions.question_en: The speed of a boat in still water is 9 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. What is the downstream speed?
questions.explanation_en: Downstream speed = boat speed + stream speed = 9 + 3 = 12 km/h.

questions.question_en: What is the smallest positive number which leaves remainder 3 when divided by 5 and remainder 5 when divided by 7?
questions.explanation_en: Numbers leaving remainder 5 with 7 are 5, 12, 19, 26, 33, ... Checking remainder 3 with 5: 33 = 5 × 6 + 3. So the smallest is 33.

questions.question_en: A tank can be filled by a pipe in 4 hours and emptied by another pipe in 6 hours. If both are opened together, how long will it take to fill half of the empty tank?
questions.explanation_en: Net rate = 1/4 − 1/6 = 1/12 per hour, so the full tank takes 12 hours. Half the tank takes 6 hours.

questions.question_en: If x is 20% more than y, then y is what percent less than x?
questions.explanation_en: Let y = 100, so x = 120. y is less than x by 20, i.e. 20/120 × 100 = 16 2/3%.

questions.question_en: The price of sugar increases by 25%. By what percentage must a family cut its consumption so that its expenditure remains unchanged?
questions.explanation_en: Reduction % = r / (100 + r) × 100 = 25/125 × 100 = 20%. (Taking 25% is the common mistake.)

questions.question_en: A man goes from his house to his office at 40 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation_en: For equal distances the average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 40 × 60 / 100 = 48 km/h. (The arithmetic mean 50 is the usual wrong answer.)

questions.question_en: What is the unit digit of 7^243?
questions.explanation_en: Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat in a cycle of 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. 243 = 4 × 60 + 3, so the unit digit is the 3rd in the cycle, 3.

questions.question_en: The product of two numbers is 1620 and their HCF is 9. What is their LCM?
questions.explanation_en: HCF × LCM = product of the numbers. LCM = 1620 / 9 = 180.

questions.question_en: A number is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net change?
questions.explanation_en: Let the number be 100. After +20% → 120. After −20% of 120 (= 24) → 96. Net = 4% decrease. (Rule: x − y − xy/100 = 20 − 20 − 4 = −4.)

questions.question_en: What single discount is equivalent to successive discounts of 20% and 10%?
questions.explanation_en: Net multiplier = 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72, so the net discount = 28%. (Adding to 30% is the common mistake.)

tests.description: 25 questions on Arithmetic (Arithmetical & Numerical Ability).

tests.title: Chapter Test — Computer Fundamentals & Digital Logic
tests.subject: Computer Science

questions.question_en: How many distinct values can be represented using 8 bits?
questions.question_hi: 8 बिट्स से कितने भिन्न मान निरूपित किए जा सकते हैं?
questions.explanation_en: n bits give 2^n combinations, so 8 bits give 2^8 = 256 values (0 to 255 unsigned). 255 is the largest value, not the count of values.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is an example of a second-generation (transistor-based) computer?
questions.explanation_en: IBM 1401 (1959) was a popular transistorised second-generation machine. ENIAC used vacuum tubes (first generation), System/360 used ICs (third) and the Intel 4004 is a microprocessor (fourth generation).

questions.question_en: A 4-to-1 MUX has select inputs S1 = A and S0 = B, with data inputs I0 = 0, I1 = C, I2 = C' and I3 = 1. The function it realises is:
questions.question_hi: एक 4-से-1 MUX में S1 = A, S0 = B तथा डेटा इनपुट I0 = 0, I1 = C, I2 = C', I3 = 1 हैं। यह कौन-सा फलन बनाता है?
questions.explanation_en: F = A'B'·0 + A'B·C + AB'·C' + AB·1 = A'BC + AB'C' + AB. These give minterms 011 = 3, 100 = 4, 110 = 6 and 111 = 7.

questions.question_en: Arrange the following computers in the correct chronological order of their introduction: IBM System/360, ENIAC, IBM 1401, UNIVAC I.

options.en: ENIAC → UNIVAC I → IBM 1401 → IBM System/360
IBM 1401 → ENIAC → UNIVAC I → IBM System/360
UNIVAC I → ENIAC → IBM System/360 → IBM 1401
ENIAC → IBM 1401 → UNIVAC I → IBM System/360

questions.explanation_en: ENIAC (1946) was the first general-purpose electronic computer, UNIVAC I (1951) the first commercial computer, IBM 1401 (1959) a transistor machine and IBM System/360 (1964) an IC-based third-generation family.

questions.question_en: If both inputs of a two-input NAND gate are connected together to a single signal A, the gate behaves as:
questions.explanation_en: With both inputs equal to A, the output is (A·A)' = A'. So a NAND (or NOR) gate with shorted inputs works as an inverter, which is the first step in proving that NAND is universal.

questions.question_en: The product-of-sums expression (A + B)(A + B') is equivalent to:
questions.explanation_en: Expanding: AA + AB' + AB + BB' = A + A(B' + B) + 0 = A + A = A. Alternatively, by the dual of the distributive law, (A + B)(A + B') = A + BB' = A + 0 = A.

questions.question_en: How many different bit patterns represent zero in 8-bit sign-magnitude representation?
questions.explanation_en: Sign-magnitude has +0 (00000000) and −0 (10000000); 1's complement also has two zeros. Only 2's complement has a single representation of zero, which is one reason computers use it.

questions.question_en: Which of the following lists storage units in increasing order of size?
questions.question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प भंडारण इकाइयों को बढ़ते क्रम में दर्शाता है?
questions.explanation_en: Each step is 1024× (binary) larger: KB → MB → GB → TB → PB → EB → ZB → YB. So GB < TB < PB < EB.

questions.question_en: What is the minimum number of two-input NAND gates required to implement a two-input AND gate?
questions.explanation_en: NAND gives (AB)'. Passing that through a second NAND with its inputs tied together inverts it, producing AB. Hence two NAND gates. A two-input OR needs three NANDs and XOR needs four.

questions.question_en: The binary number 11010110 written in hexadecimal is:
questions.explanation_en: Group into nibbles: 1101 0110. 1101 = 13 = D and 0110 = 6, so the number is D6 (214 in decimal).

questions.question_en: Using 4-bit 2's complement arithmetic, compute 1010 − 0110. What is the result?
questions.explanation_en: 2's complement of 0110 is 1010. Adding: 1010 + 1010 = 10100. The fifth bit (end carry) is discarded, leaving 0100 = 4, which matches 10 − 6 = 4 for the unsigned interpretation.

questions.question_en: In the ASCII code, the uppercase letter 'A' has the decimal value 65. What is the decimal ASCII value of the lowercase letter 'a'?
questions.question_hi: ASCII कोड में बड़े अक्षर 'A' का दशमलव मान 65 है। छोटे अक्षर 'a' का दशमलव ASCII मान क्या है?
questions.explanation_en: Lowercase letters are 32 positions after their uppercase forms in ASCII: 65 + 32 = 97. Standard ASCII is a 7-bit code (0–127), so 129 is impossible.

questions.question_en: The Boolean expression A + A'B simplifies to:
questions.explanation_en: A + A'B = (A + A')(A + B) by the distributive law of + over ·, and A + A' = 1, so the result is A + B. This is the second absorption-type identity; the plain absorption law A + AB = A (option 2) is a different expression.

questions.question_en: According to IEC binary prefixes, which statement is correct?
questions.question_hi: IEC बाइनरी उपसर्गों के अनुसार कौन-सा कथन सही है?
questions.explanation_en: The IEC introduced kibi (Ki), mebi (Mi), gibi (Gi) for powers of 2, so 1 KiB = 2^10 = 1024 bytes, while SI kilo means 1000, so 1 kB = 1000 bytes. Many exam questions still use KB = 1024 bytes in the traditional sense.

questions.question_en: A group of 4 bits is called a:
questions.question_hi: 4 बिट के समूह को क्या कहते हैं?
questions.explanation_en: 4 bits form a nibble (half a byte) and 8 bits form a byte. A word is machine-dependent (e.g. 32 or 64 bits).

questions.question_en: Integrated circuits (ICs) were first used as the main building block in which generation of computers?
questions.explanation_en: Third-generation computers (1964–1971, e.g. IBM System/360) used small- and medium-scale integrated circuits. The second generation used discrete transistors, and the fourth moved to VLSI microprocessors.

questions.question_en: What is the result of the binary subtraction 110111 − 10101?
How many cells does a Karnaugh map for a four-variable Boolean function contain?
questions.question_hi: चार चर वाले बूलियन फलन के कार्नो मैप (K-map) में कितने सेल होते हैं?
questions.explanation_en: A K-map has one cell per minterm, and n variables give 2^n minterms: 4 cells for 2 variables, 8 for 3 and 16 for 4 (arranged 4 × 4).

questions.question_en: Which logic gate produces an output of 1 only when all of its inputs are 1?
questions.question_hi: कौन-सा लॉजिक गेट केवल तभी आउटपुट 1 देता है जब उसके सभी इनपुट 1 हों?
questions.explanation_en: An AND gate implements logical multiplication: Y = A·B, which is 1 only for the input row 1,1. An OR gate gives 1 if any input is 1, and NAND gives 0 (not 1) for the all-ones input.

questions.question_en: Which CPU register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.question_hi: कौन-सा CPU रजिस्टर अगले निर्देश का पता (address) रखता है?
questions.explanation_en: The Program Counter (PC) always points to the next instruction and is incremented after each fetch. The Instruction Register holds the instruction currently being executed, and the MAR holds the address of whatever memory location is being accessed right now.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is the fastest type of memory in a computer?
questions.question_hi: कंप्यूटर में निम्न में से सबसे तेज़ मेमोरी कौन-सी है?
questions.explanation_en: Registers sit inside the CPU and are accessed in a single clock cycle, making them the fastest (and smallest) level of the memory hierarchy. Cache is next, followed by RAM and then secondary storage.

questions.question_en: According to De Morgan's theorem, the complement of (A·B) is equal to:
questions.question_hi: डी मॉर्गन प्रमेय के अनुसार (A·B) का पूरक (complement) किसके बराबर है?
questions.explanation_en: De Morgan's first theorem states (A·B)' = A' + B': the complement of a product is the sum of the complements. The second theorem is (A + B)' = A'·B'. Option 2 is the complement of (A + B), not of (A·B).

questions.question_en: The range of integers that can be represented in 8-bit 2's complement form is:
questions.question_hi: 8-बिट 2's complement में निरूपित की जा सकने वाली पूर्णांकों की सीमा है:
questions.explanation_en: An n-bit 2's complement number spans −2^(n−1) to +2^(n−1) − 1, so for n = 8: −128 to +127. Only one zero exists, which is why the negative side has one extra value. −127 to +127 is the range of sign-magnitude and 1's complement.

questions.question_en: Cache memory improves performance because programs tend to access the same or nearby memory locations repeatedly. This property is called:
questions.explanation_en: Temporal locality (recently used data is reused soon) and spatial locality (neighbouring addresses are used together) are together called locality of reference; cache exploits both. DMA and interleaving are unrelated techniques.

questions.question_en: When both inputs of a clocked JK flip-flop are held at 1 (J = K = 1), on each active clock edge the flip-flop:
questions.question_hi: क्लॉक्ड JK फ्लिप-फ्लॉप के दोनों इनपुट 1 (J = K = 1) होने पर प्रत्येक सक्रिय क्लॉक एज पर फ्लिप-फ्लॉप क्या करता है?
questions.explanation_en: For J = K = 1 the JK flip-flop complements its output (Q+ = Q'), removing the invalid state of the SR flip-flop. J = K = 0 is the hold condition.

tests.title: Chapter Test — Computer Networks & Internet
tests.subject: Computer Science

questions.question_en: A school's private network that uses Internet technologies (web pages, e-mail) but is accessible only to its own staff is called a(n):
questions.explanation_en: An intranet is an organisation-only network built on Internet protocols. An extranet extends controlled access to selected outsiders such as suppliers, and Ethernet is a LAN wiring standard.

questions.question_en: The theoretical total number of IPv4 addresses is approximately:
questions.explanation_en: IPv4 uses 32 bits, so there are 2^32 ≈ 4.29 billion addresses. 3.4 × 10^38 (2^128) is the IPv6 address space, which is why IPv6 was introduced.

questions.question_en: Which type of address exists in IPv4 but has been removed in IPv6?
questions.explanation_en: IPv6 defines unicast, multicast and anycast addresses only; the functions of broadcast are carried out using multicast groups such as FF02::1.

questions.question_en: By default, a web server serving HTTPS pages listens on TCP port:
questions.explanation_en: HTTPS (HTTP over TLS) uses well-known port 443. Port 80 is plain HTTP, 8080 is a common alternate HTTP port and 21 is FTP control.

questions.question_en: In a star topology, what is the effect of a failure of the central hub, and of a failure of a single cable?

options.en: Both bring the whole network down
Hub failure brings the whole network down; a cable failure isolates only one node
Hub failure isolates one node; cable failure brings the whole network down

questions.explanation_en: The hub is a single point of failure, but each node has its own cable, so a cable break affects only that node. This is why star is easy to troubleshoot.

questions.question_en: An IPv4 address is written in dotted-decimal notation as four numbers. Each of these numbers can range from:
questions.explanation_en: Each of the four parts is one octet (8 bits), so its value ranges from 0 to 2^8 − 1 = 255. That is why an address such as 192.168.300.1 is invalid.

questions.question_en: Which service translates a domain name such as www.education.delhi.gov.in into an IP address?
questions.explanation_en: The Domain Name System resolves human-readable names to IP addresses. DHCP assigns IP addresses, FTP transfers files and ARP maps IP addresses to MAC addresses.

questions.question_en: Small pieces of data that a website stores in the user's browser to remember login status or preferences are called:
questions.explanation_en: Cookies are small text files sent by a website and stored by the browser, then returned with later requests so the stateless HTTP protocol can 'remember' the user. Bookmarks are saved links chosen by the user.

questions.question_en: The address used by the Transport layer to deliver data to the correct application process on a host is the:
questions.explanation_en: Port numbers identify processes (services) on a host. MAC addresses are Data Link addresses and IP addresses are Network layer addresses.

questions.question_en: In the Routing Information Protocol (RIP), a destination whose hop count is 16 is treated as:
questions.explanation_en: RIP is a distance-vector protocol whose maximum valid hop count is 15; a metric of 16 means 'infinity', i.e. unreachable. This limit keeps RIP suitable only for small networks.

questions.question_en: The four networks 192.168.0.0/24, 192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24 and 192.168.3.0/24 are to be advertised as one summary (supernet) route. The summary route is:
questions.explanation_en: Four contiguous /24 networks = 2^2, so 2 bits are removed from the prefix: /24 − 2 = /22. The third octets 0–3 share the first 6 bits (000000xx), giving 192.168.0.0/22.

questions.question_en: A browser displays the HTTP status code 404. This means:

options.en: The requested page was not found on the server
The server had an internal error

questions.explanation_en: 404 Not Found is a client-error code meaning the resource does not exist at that URL. 200 means OK, 500 is Internal Server Error and 301 is Moved Permanently.

questions.question_en: In network security, a DMZ (demilitarised zone) is best described as:

options.en: A separate subnet holding public-facing servers, isolated from the internal LAN by firewalls
A part of the LAN where no passwords are required
The range of private IP addresses reserved for routers
A wireless zone in which encryption is disabled

questions.explanation_en: Web, mail and DNS servers that must be reachable from the Internet are placed in a DMZ so that if one is compromised the attacker still faces a firewall before reaching the internal network.

questions.question_en: What is the default subnet mask of a Class C IPv4 address?
questions.explanation_en: Class C uses the first 24 bits for the network, so the default mask is 255.255.255.0 (/24). 255.255.0.0 is the Class B default.

questions.question_en: The protocol data unit (PDU) handled at the Data Link layer is called a:
questions.explanation_en: Data Link layer PDU = frame; Network layer = packet (datagram); Transport layer = segment; Physical layer = bits.

questions.question_en: The correct sequence of segments in the TCP three-way handshake is:
questions.explanation_en: The client sends SYN, the server replies SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK; the connection is then established. FIN is used to close a connection, not to open one.

questions.question_en: A Virtual Private Network (VPN) allows a teacher working from home to access the school server securely because it:

options.en: Removes the need for any password
Creates an encrypted tunnel across the public Internet
Gives the laptop a faster processor
Connects directly by a dedicated physical cable

questions.explanation_en: A VPN encapsulates and encrypts traffic between the remote user and the private network, so the public Internet carries it privately. It still uses the ordinary Internet link, not a dedicated cable.

questions.question_en: Which device simply regenerates and retimes a weakened signal so that it can travel a longer distance on the same network?
questions.explanation_en: A repeater is a layer-1 device that extends the physical length of a network by amplifying/regenerating the signal; it does not look at addresses.

questions.question_en: The two wires of each pair in a twisted-pair cable are twisted around each other mainly to:

options.en: Reduce crosstalk and external electromagnetic interference

questions.explanation_en: Twisting makes both wires pick up nearly equal noise, which cancels out at the receiver (differential signalling), reducing crosstalk and EMI.

questions.question_en: The Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is used to:

options.en: Assign IP addresses automatically to hosts
Find the IP address of a host whose domain name is known
Find the MAC address of a host whose IP address is known
Find the IP address when only the MAC address is known

questions.explanation_en: ARP broadcasts 'who has this IP?' and the owner replies with its MAC address so a frame can be built. Name-to-IP is DNS, automatic assignment is DHCP and MAC-to-IP is the older RARP.

questions.question_en: Which protocol automatically assigns an IP address, subnet mask, default gateway and DNS server to a computer when it joins a network?
questions.explanation_en: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol leases IP configuration to clients automatically, avoiding manual setup. DNS only resolves names.

questions.question_en: Which protocol–layer pairing (in the TCP/IP model) is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation_en: UDP, like TCP, is a Transport-layer protocol. SMTP is an application protocol, IP works at the Internet layer, and Ethernet operates at the Network Access (link) layer.

questions.question_en: Which protocol is used to SEND e-mail from a mail client to a mail server and between mail servers?
questions.explanation_en: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol is a 'push' protocol used for sending and relaying mail. POP3 and IMAP are used by clients to retrieve mail from the server.

questions.question_en: The ping utility checks whether a remote host is reachable by sending messages of which protocol?
questions.explanation_en: ping sends ICMP Echo Request messages and waits for Echo Reply messages, reporting round-trip time and loss. It does not use TCP, DNS's UDP port or HTTP.

questions.question_en: The MAC address burnt into a Network Interface Card (NIC) is:

options.en: 32 bits long, written in dotted decimal
128 bits long, written in hexadecimal groups
48 bits long, written as 12 hexadecimal digits

questions.explanation_en: A MAC address is 48 bits (6 bytes), e.g. 3C:5A:B4:12:9F:01; the first 3 bytes identify the manufacturer (OUI). 32-bit dotted decimal describes IPv4 and 128-bit hex describes IPv6.

tests.title: Chapter Test — Current Affairs

questions.question_en: Who won the men's singles title at the Australian Open 2026 by beating Novak Djokovic in the final?
questions.explanation_en: Alcaraz won his first Australian Open title in January-February 2026, completing a career Grand Slam.

questions.question_en: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, what share of the programme cost do most states have to bear?
questions.explanation_en: Unlike MGNREGA (Centre paid the full wage bill), most states now bear 40%; North-Eastern and Himalayan states bear only 10%.

questions.question_en: Census 2027, whose first phase (houselisting) began in April 2026, is India's first:
questions.explanation_en: Houselisting ran April-September 2026 using mobile apps and online self-enumeration; population enumeration follows in early 2027.

questions.question_en: Which franchise won the IPL 2026 title, defending the crown it won in 2025?
questions.explanation_en: RCB beat Gujarat Titans by five wickets in the final at Ahmedabad, their second consecutive title.

questions.question_en: How many persons were honoured with the Padma Awards announced on 25 January 2026?
questions.explanation_en: The 2026 list had 131 awardees (5 Vibhushan, 13 Bhushan, 113 Shri per most reports); 2025 had 139 and 2024 had 132.

questions.question_en: Who is the Vice President of India (elected in September 2025 after Jagdeep Dhankhar's resignation)?
questions.explanation_en: C. P. Radhakrishnan, former Maharashtra Governor, was elected the 15th Vice President on 9 September 2025.

questions.question_en: Who captained India's women's team to the 2025 ICC Women's ODI World Cup triumph?
questions.explanation_en: Harmanpreet Kaur led India to its maiden Women's World Cup title in November 2025 (earlier finals lost in 2005 and 2017).

questions.question_en: Runa Khan, a 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Award winner announced on 31 August 2026, is from which country?
questions.explanation_en: The 2026 awardees: Tommy Koh (Singapore), Runa Khan (Bangladesh) and Bo Kyi (Myanmar).

questions.question_en: Who was sworn in as Chief Minister of Bihar for the tenth time after the NDA's win in the November 2025 election?
questions.explanation_en: The NDA won a landslide in the November 2025 Bihar Assembly election and Nitish Kumar took oath on 20 November 2025.

questions.question_en: With the Union Budget 2026-27 presented on 1 February 2026, how many consecutive Union Budgets has Nirmala Sitharaman presented?
questions.explanation_en: The 2026-27 Budget was her ninth in a row, counting the July 2019 budget and both 2024 budgets (interim and full).

questions.question_en: Who became the Chief Minister of Kerala after the Congress-led UDF's win in the 2026 Assembly election?
questions.explanation_en: The UDF secured a big majority in May 2026 and Congress named V. D. Satheesan as CM.

questions.question_en: Navtej Sarna won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 (English), announced in March 2026, for which novel?
questions.explanation_en: Former diplomat Navtej Sarna won for 'Crimson Spring', a novel on the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

questions.question_en: Which veteran actor was honoured posthumously with the Padma Vibhushan in 2026?
questions.explanation_en: Dharmendra and former Kerala CM V. S. Achuthanandan were among the posthumous Padma Vibhushan recipients of 2026.

questions.question_en: Who won the men's singles title at Wimbledon 2026?
questions.explanation_en: Sinner defended his Wimbledon title, beating Alexander Zverev in four sets in the July 2026 final.

tests.description: 25 questions on Current Affairs (General Awareness).

tests.title: Chapter Test — DBMS & SQL
tests.subject: Computer Science

questions.question_en: A decomposition of R into R1 and R2 is lossless if:

options.en: R1 ∩ R2 is a super key of R1 or of R2
R1 ∪ R2 has fewer attributes than R
Both R1 and R2 have the same number of tuples

questions.explanation_en: Lossless-join condition: the common attributes must functionally determine all attributes of at least one of the two sub-relations, i.e., be a key of R1 or R2. If the intersection is empty, the natural join becomes a Cartesian product and spurious tuples appear.

questions.question_en: What does SELECT MONTH('2026-10-19'), DAYNAME('2026-10-19'); return? (19 October 2026 is a Monday.)
questions.explanation_en: MONTH() extracts the numeric month (10) and DAYNAME() returns the weekday name. MONTHNAME() would return 'October' and DAY() would return 19.

questions.question_en: The relational-algebra expression σ_Salary>50000 (π_Name,Salary (EMP)) returns:

options.en: A count of employees with Salary > 50000
Name and Salary of employees earning more than 50000
All columns of employees earning more than 50000

questions.explanation_en: The inner projection keeps only Name and Salary; the outer selection then filters rows by Salary > 50000. Relational algebra never returns a count — that is an aggregate function.

questions.question_en: Given functional dependencies A → B and B → C, which dependency follows by the transitivity rule of Armstrong's axioms?
questions.explanation_en: Transitivity: if A → B and B → C then A → C. Armstrong's three primary axioms are reflexivity, augmentation and transitivity; reversing a dependency is never implied.

questions.question_en: The 'Employee SUPERVISES Employee' relationship, where both roles come from the same entity set, is an example of a:
questions.explanation_en: A relationship between instances of the same entity set is recursive (unary) and role names such as 'supervisor' and 'supervisee' are added. A ternary relationship involves three entity sets.

questions.question_en: What is the output of SELECT MOD(17, 5), POWER(2, 5), SQRT(49); in MySQL?
questions.explanation_en: MOD gives the remainder 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2; POWER(2,5) = 2^5 = 32; SQRT(49) = 7.

questions.question_en: Relation STUDENT(Roll, Name, Email, Phone) has candidate keys Roll and Email. Which of the following is a super key but NOT a candidate key?
questions.explanation_en: A super key is any attribute set that uniquely identifies tuples; (Roll, Name) does so but contains an unnecessary attribute, so it is not minimal and hence not a candidate key. Roll and Email are candidate keys; Name alone is not unique.

questions.question_en: Which anomaly occurs when deleting the only tuple that stores a department's name also loses the department's information?
questions.explanation_en: A deletion anomaly is the unintended loss of facts when a row is removed. An insertion anomaly is being unable to add a fact (e.g., a new department) without an unrelated fact (an employee).

questions.question_en: Which MySQL function removes leading and trailing spaces from a string?
questions.explanation_en: TRIM removes spaces from both ends; LTRIM only from the left and RTRIM only from the right. STRIP and CLEAN are not MySQL functions (strip is Python).

questions.question_en: A subquery placed in the FROM clause and used as a temporary table is called a/an:
questions.explanation_en: A subquery in FROM is a derived table and in MySQL it must be given an alias. Subqueries can appear in SELECT, FROM, WHERE and HAVING clauses.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental (basic) operation of relational algebra?
questions.explanation_en: The six basic operations are select, project, union, set difference, Cartesian product and rename. Join, intersection and division are derived operations (join = select on a Cartesian product).

questions.question_en: Which command undoes all changes made in the current transaction since the last COMMIT?
questions.explanation_en: ROLLBACK discards uncommitted changes; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT name undoes only up to a savepoint. REVOKE withdraws privileges and is unrelated to transactions.

questions.question_en: In the two-phase locking (2PL) protocol, a transaction:

options.en: Acquires all its locks in a growing phase and releases them in a shrinking phase, never acquiring a lock after releasing one
Releases every lock immediately after each read
Must lock only two data items

questions.explanation_en: 2PL guarantees conflict serialisability by separating lock acquisition (growing phase) from release (shrinking phase). Strict 2PL additionally holds exclusive locks until commit to avoid cascading rollbacks.

questions.question_en: What is the logical order in which SQL processes these clauses?

options.en: WHERE → FROM → SELECT → GROUP BY → ORDER BY → HAVING
SELECT → FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → ORDER BY
FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY
FROM → GROUP BY → WHERE → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY

questions.explanation_en: Rows are fetched (FROM), filtered (WHERE), grouped (GROUP BY), groups filtered (HAVING), columns projected (SELECT) and finally sorted (ORDER BY). This is why a column alias from SELECT cannot be used in WHERE but can be used in ORDER BY.

questions.question_en: EMP(Name, Salary): (Amit 30000), (Bela 50000), (Chand 40000). Output of SELECT Name FROM EMP WHERE Salary > ALL (SELECT Salary FROM EMP WHERE Name IN ('Amit','Chand')); is:
questions.explanation_en: The subquery returns 30000 and 40000. '> ALL' means greater than every value, i.e., > 40000, which only Bela (50000) satisfies. '> ANY' would return Chand and Bela.

questions.question_en: Which statement removes the whole table BOOKS, including its structure, from the database?
questions.explanation_en: DROP TABLE deletes the data and the table definition. TRUNCATE empties the table but keeps the structure; DELETE TABLE and REMOVE TABLE are not valid SQL.

questions.question_en: T1 runs SELECT COUNT(*) FROM EMP WHERE D_ID = 5 twice; between the two reads T2 inserts and commits a new row with D_ID = 5. T1 sees different counts. This anomaly is a:
questions.explanation_en: New rows appearing in a repeated range query are phantoms; the SERIALIZABLE isolation level prevents them. A non-repeatable read concerns a changed value of an existing row.

questions.question_en: A money transfer debits Rs 500 from Account A and the system crashes before crediting Account B. Which property ensures the debit is undone?
questions.explanation_en: Atomicity makes the transaction all-or-nothing: the recovery manager rolls back the partial debit so the database returns to its state before the transaction began.

questions.question_en: The query SELECT DISTINCT City FROM CUSTOMER; on a table with cities Delhi, Pune, Delhi, Goa, Pune returns how many rows?
questions.explanation_en: DISTINCT removes duplicate values, leaving Delhi, Pune and Goa — 3 rows. Without DISTINCT all 5 rows are returned.

questions.question_en: A subquery that refers to a column of the outer query and is therefore re-evaluated for each outer row is called a:
questions.explanation_en: A correlated subquery depends on the outer row (e.g., WHERE e.Salary > (SELECT AVG(Salary) FROM EMP WHERE D_ID = e.D_ID)). A non-correlated subquery runs once; a scalar subquery returns a single value.

questions.question_en: A relation has 4 attributes A, B, C, D with the single candidate key A. How many super keys does the relation have?
questions.explanation_en: A super key must contain A; the other 3 attributes may each be present or absent, giving 2^3 = 8 super keys. 16 would count all subsets including those without A.

questions.question_en: Which constraint ensures that a column cannot store an empty (missing) value?
questions.explanation_en: NOT NULL forces every row to supply a value for the column. UNIQUE prevents duplicates (but usually allows NULL), CHECK validates a condition and DEFAULT supplies a value when none is given.

questions.question_en: Two transactions both read Balance = 1000; T1 adds 200 and writes 1200, then T2 subtracts 100 and writes 900. The final value 900 illustrates:
questions.explanation_en: T1's update is overwritten by T2, which worked from the stale value; the correct result should have been 1100. Locking the row before reading prevents this.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is an advantage of using views?

options.en: They always make queries run faster than base tables
They can hide sensitive columns and simplify complex queries for users
They remove the need for primary keys
They permanently store a snapshot of the data

questions.explanation_en: Views provide security (exposing only selected columns/rows) and logical data independence. Because a view re-runs its query, it does not by itself improve speed or store data.

questions.question_en: T1 reads a value X = 100 and updates it to 150 without committing. T2 then reads X and gets 150. T1 is rolled back. The problem T2 faces is called:
questions.explanation_en: Reading uncommitted data that is later rolled back is a dirty read (uncommitted dependency). A lost update happens when two transactions overwrite each other's writes.

tests.description: 25 questions on DBMS & SQL (Computer Science).

tests.title: Chapter Test — Data Structures & Algorithms
tests.subject: Computer Science

questions.question_en: The root is deleted from the max-heap [90, 70, 80, 30, 60, 50, 40]. After re-heapification, the array becomes:
questions.explanation_en: The last element 40 moves to the root → [40, 70, 80, 30, 60, 50]. Sift down: swap with the larger child 80 → [80, 70, 40, 30, 60, 50]; 40 at index 2 has child 50 → swap → [80, 70, 50, 30, 60, 40].

questions.question_en: A complete binary tree contains 100 nodes. How many of them are leaf nodes?
questions.explanation_en: Store the tree in an array with indices 1–100. Node i has a child only if 2i ≤ 100, i.e. i ≤ 50, so nodes 1–50 are internal and nodes 51–100 are leaves: 50 leaves. In general a complete binary tree with n nodes has ⌈n/2⌉ leaves.

questions.question_en: The preorder traversal of a binary tree is P Q S T R U and its inorder traversal is S Q T P U R. What is its postorder traversal?

options.en: S T Q R U P
T S Q U R P
S T Q U R P
S Q T U R P

questions.explanation_en: Preorder's first node P is the root; inorder splits into left {S, Q, T} and right {U, R}. Left subtree: root Q (next in preorder) with S left and T right. Right subtree: root R with U as its left child. Postorder = S T Q, U R, P.

questions.question_en: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
questions.explanation_en: 2^(2n) = 4^n, and 4^n / 2^n = 2^n grows without bound, so no constant c makes 4^n ≤ c·2^n. By contrast 2^(n+1) = 2·2^n (constant factor 2) and log(n²) = 2 log n, so those are true.

questions.question_en: Big-O notation, f(n) = O(g(n)), expresses that g(n) is an asymptotic ______ of f(n).
questions.explanation_en: f(n) = O(g(n)) if f(n) ≤ c·g(n) for some constant c > 0 and all n ≥ n₀. Ω gives a lower bound and Θ gives a tight bound (both upper and lower).

questions.question_en: A singly linked list has only a head pointer (no tail pointer). Which operation takes O(n) time?

options.en: Inserting a node at the beginning
Reading the data of the first node

questions.explanation_en: To delete the last node we must reach its predecessor, which requires traversing the whole list. All operations at the head are O(1).

questions.question_en: Binary search can be applied correctly only when the list is:
questions.explanation_en: Binary search discards half the list after comparing with the middle element, which is valid only if the elements are in sorted order. It also needs random access, so an array is the usual structure.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a typical application of a stack?

options.en: Undo operation in a text editor

questions.explanation_en: BFS processes vertices level by level and therefore uses a queue. Function calls (call stack), bracket matching and undo all rely on LIFO order.

questions.question_en: After the FIRST pass of bubble sort (ascending, adjacent swaps from left to right) on [6, 2, 9, 4, 1], the array becomes:
questions.explanation_en: Compare 6,2 → swap [2,6,9,4,1]; 6,9 → no swap; 9,4 → swap [2,6,4,9,1]; 9,1 → swap [2,6,4,1,9]. The largest element 9 'bubbles' to the end after one pass.

questions.question_en: Keys 45, 20, 60, 10, 30, 50, 70, 25 are inserted in this order into an empty binary search tree. Which node is the parent of 25?
questions.explanation_en: 25 < 45 → go left to 20; 25 > 20 → go right to 30; 25 < 30 → becomes the left child of 30.

questions.question_en: A binary heap is stored in an array starting at index 1. The children of the node at index i are found at indices:
questions.explanation_en: With 1-based indexing, left = 2i, right = 2i + 1 and parent = ⌊i/2⌋. With 0-based indexing they become 2i + 1, 2i + 2 and ⌊(i − 1)/2⌋.

questions.question_en: Considering that ^ (exponent) has the highest precedence and is right-associative, the postfix form of A + B ^ C ^ D * E is:
questions.explanation_en: Right associativity makes B ^ C ^ D = B ^ (C ^ D) → B C D ^ ^. That result is multiplied by E → B C D ^ ^ E *, and finally added to A → A B C D ^ ^ E * +. Treating ^ as left-associative gives A B C ^ D ^ E * +.

questions.question_en: A circular queue is implemented in an array of size N, keeping one slot always empty to distinguish full from empty. The queue is FULL when:
questions.explanation_en: When rear is just one position behind front (moving circularly) no more insertions are allowed. front == rear means EMPTY under this convention, and rear == N − 1 is the full test of a simple linear queue.

questions.question_en: In a binary tree, every internal node has exactly two children. If there are 10 internal nodes, the number of leaf nodes is:
questions.explanation_en: For a full binary tree, leaves L = internal nodes I + 1. Reason: edges = 2I (two per internal node) and also n − 1 = I + L − 1, so 2I = I + L − 1 → L = I + 1 = 11.

questions.question_en: What is the minimum number of moves needed to solve the Tower of Hanoi puzzle with 5 discs?
questions.explanation_en: Moves satisfy M(n) = 2M(n − 1) + 1 with M(1) = 1, giving M(n) = 2^n − 1 = 2^5 − 1 = 31. 63 is the answer for 6 discs.

questions.question_en: Any sorting algorithm that sorts only by comparing pairs of elements must make, in the worst case, at least:
questions.explanation_en: A comparison sort is a binary decision tree with at least n! leaves, so its height is at least log₂(n!) = Θ(n log n). Counting and radix sort beat this only because they do not rely on comparisons.

questions.question_en: Which is a key advantage of a doubly linked list over a singly linked list?

options.en: It needs less memory per node
A node can be deleted in O(1) time when only a pointer to that node is given
Random access to the k-th element in O(1)

questions.explanation_en: The prev link gives direct access to the predecessor, so links can be fixed without a traversal; it also allows backward traversal. The price is an extra pointer per node, and access by position is still O(n).

questions.question_en: A circular queue uses an array of size 5 (indices 0–4), with front = 0 and the first element stored at index 0. A, B, C, D are enqueued, two elements are dequeued, and then E and F are enqueued. At which index is F stored?
questions.explanation_en: A–D occupy 0–3; two dequeues move front to 2. E goes to index 4, and F goes to (4 + 1) % 5 = 0, reusing the freed slot — the advantage of a circular queue over a linear one.

questions.question_en: A stack is used to check the bracket string  ( ( ) ( ( )  for balance. After the whole string is scanned, how many '(' symbols remain on the stack?
questions.explanation_en: Push, push, pop (1 left), push, push (3), pop (2). Two unmatched '(' remain, so the string is NOT balanced; a balanced string leaves the stack empty.

questions.question_en: Selection sort (ascending) is applied to [29, 10, 14, 37, 13]. What is the array after the first TWO passes?
questions.explanation_en: Pass 1: minimum 10 swaps with 29 → [10, 29, 14, 37, 13]. Pass 2: minimum of the rest is 13, swapped with 29 → [10, 13, 14, 37, 29].

questions.question_en: The key 95 is inserted into the max-heap stored as [90, 70, 80, 30, 60, 50, 40]. After the heap is restored, the array is:
questions.explanation_en: 95 is placed at index 7 (child of 30 at index 3) and sifted up: swap with 30 → index 3; swap with its parent 70 → index 1; swap with 90 → root. Result [95, 90, 80, 70, 60, 50, 40, 30].

questions.question_en: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height 4, if a tree with only the root has height 0?
questions.explanation_en: Levels 0 to 4 can hold 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16 = 2^(h+1) − 1 = 2^5 − 1 = 31 nodes. 15 would be the answer if the root were counted as height 1.

questions.question_en: The prefix (Polish) form of the infix expression (A + B) * (C − D) is:
questions.explanation_en: Each sub-expression becomes operator-first: A + B → + A B, C − D → − C D; then the outer * is placed before both → * + A B − C D. A B + C D − * is the postfix form.
f(7) = 7 × f(5) = 7 × 5 × f(3) = 7 × 5 × 3 × f(1) = 7 × 5 × 3 × 1 = 105 (the product of odd numbers, a 'double factorial'). 5040 = 7! would need n − 1 instead of n − 2.

questions.question_en: Evaluate the postfix expression  5 3 + 8 2 − * 4 /  using a stack.
questions.explanation_en: 5 3 + → 8; 8 2 − → 6; 8 6 * → 48; 48 4 / → 12. For each operator, the top element is the RIGHT operand and the one below it is the LEFT operand.
